PackWrite does not upload the full checkout. Keep sensitive data out of the\nprompt and README excerpt.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecrets are excluded by default\u003c/strong\u003e (\u003ccode\u003e.env*\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e*.pem\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e*.key\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eid_rsa\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003eid_ed25519\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e.git\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enode_modules\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003evendor\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edist\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ebuild\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e.next\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecoverage\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003etarget\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e.venv\u003c/code\u003e, and names containing \u003ccode\u003esecret\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e); skipped paths are reported.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGenerated paths are restricted\u003c/strong\u003e to the output directory (absolute, \u003ccode\u003e..\u003c/code\u003e traversal,\nbackslash-separator, \u003ccode\u003e~\u003c/code\u003e home-expansion, control-character, ambiguous-segment, and\nescaping paths are rejected), configured output directories must be relative project\npaths with no existing symlink components, and generated secret-looking paths are\nrejected. Model responses and generated content have explicit resource ceilings.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePrompt payloads are never logged.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003e--verbose\u003c/code\u003e reports size only. PackWrite keeps","that record beside your code:","","- **`MASTER.md`** — stable project intent + assumptions (don't rewrite).","- **`phases/*.md`** — per-phase specs with scope, out-of-scope, and acceptance criteria.","- **`HANDOFF.md` / `DECISIONS.md`** — mutable state and a decision log.","- **`REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`** — concrete, verifiable review items.","- **`DEEPSEEK_START.md` / `CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md`** — ready-to-paste prompts for an","  implementation agent and an independent reviewer.","","Code validates the required files, sections, and paths. The model writes the content.","","## Readiness and scope","","PackWrite creates local planning files. It does not implement your project, deploy","code, or coordinate concurrent writers. Review generated instructions before giving","them to an agent. Hosted authentication, organization policy, signing, and deployment","controls belong to the systems that run PackWrite.","","Current hardening includes:","","- Output directories must be relative, non-empty, non-traversing paths.","- Model manifest paths are validated before dry-runs or writes claim success.","- Secret-looking generated paths are rejected, not merely warned about after writing.","- Writes are staged and validated before promotion, with rollback on failed promotion.","- The full test suite is offline: 248 unit assertions and 116 CLI integration assertions.","","## Install","","PackWrite is written in the [Kujo language](#about-kujo) and run by the Kujo","interpreter. Set `PREFIX` to","choose a different install root, for example `make install PREFIX=\"$HOME/.local\"`.","Installation returns a nonzero status if the symlink cannot be created.","","The launcher preserves your working directory, so config discovery and the generated","`/agent` pack land where you invoke it.","","## Quickstart","","```bash","cd my-project","cat \u003e MEGA_PROMPT.md \u003c\u003c'EOF'","# Demo","","Build a small CLI that says hello, with tests and a README.","EOF","","export PACKWRITE_API_KEY=sk-...                       # your provider key (env only)","packwrite doctor","packwrite init MEGA_PROMPT.md --dry-run","packwrite init MEGA_PROMPT.md --provider deepseek --model deepseek-v4-pro","packwrite validate","packwrite prompt deepseek         # paste into your implementation agent","```","","A successful `init` prints:","","```text","PackWrite generated an agent pack.","","  Output:     agent/","  Provider:   deepseek","  Model:      deepseek-v4-pro","  Files:      13","  Phases:     6","  Validation: passed with 0 warnings","","Next:","  packwrite prompt deepseek","```","","`init` prints each stage, such as `[3/8] Collecting repository context...`.","Use `--quiet` to suppress successful progress and summary output.","","`--dry-run` calls the model and validates the returned manifest without writing a","pack. Resolution order, lowest to","highest precedence:","","```text","defaults  \u003c  global config (~/.config/packwrite/config.toml)  \u003c  packwrite.toml  \u003c  CLI flags","```","","```toml","[prompt]","file = \"MEGA_PROMPT.md\"","","[output]","dir = \"agent\"","overwrite = false","mode = \"autopilot\"          # reserved (parsed, not yet wired)","","[model]","provider = \"deepseek\"","model = \"deepseek-v4-pro\"","temperature = 0.1","# endpoint = \"https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions\"   # override the preset","","[repo_context]","# include = top-level allow-list; omit for defaults, use [] for all eligible names","include = [\"README.md\", \"Cargo.toml\", \"package.json\", \"pyproject.toml\", \"src\", \"tests\", \"docs\"]","exclude = [\".env\", \".git\", \"node_modules\", \"vendor\", \"dist\", \"build\", \".next\", \"coverage\"]","","[pack]","min_phases = 6              # validation warns below this","max_phases = 12             # included in the model instructions","include_deepseek_prompt = true        # generate + require DEEPSEEK_START.md","include_codex_review_prompt = true    # generate + require CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md","include_review_checklist = true       # generate + require REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md","```","","All keys above change observable behavior **except** `[output].mode` and `run_name`","(via `--run-name`), which are parsed but **reserved** for deferred features. PackWrite calls the Kujo","`ai_chat` builtin through an adapter.","","**The adapter speaks only the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions protocol** (it posts","`{model, messages}`, authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer`, and reads","`choices[0].message.content`). Built-in endpoint presets therefore exist only for","providers that expose that protocol natively:","","| `--provider` | Endpoint preset |","| --- | --- |","| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions` |","| `openai`   | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` |","| `local`    | `http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` |","","Any other provider has **no preset** and must point `--endpoint` (or `[model].endpoint`)","at an OpenAI-compatible URL — a gateway such as OpenRouter or LiteLLM works well.","","Set `--model` or `[model].model` to a model your endpoint supports. The default is","`deepseek-v4-pro`; check your provider's available models before running generation.","","\u003e **Anthropic is not supported natively.** Anthropic's API uses `/v1/messages` +","\u003e `x-api-key`, which this adapter does not speak. `--provider anthropic` with no endpoint","\u003e fails with a clear error; to use Claude, set `--endpoint` to an OpenAI-compatible","\u003e gateway in front of it.","","**API keys come from the environment only** — never from flags or committed config.","PackWrite checks `PACKWRITE_API_KEY` first, then a provider-specific variable","(`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).","","## Model response format","","PackWrite expects the model to return a **JSON file manifest** and nothing else:","","```json","{ \"files\": [ { \"path\": \"agent/MASTER.md\", \"content\": \"...\" }, ... ] }","```","","For DeepSeek structured pack generation, PackWrite requests strict JSON mode and","disables thinking by default:","","```json","{","  \"response_format\": { \"type\": \"json_object\" },","  \"thinking\": { \"type\": \"disabled\" },","  \"max_tokens\": 32000,","  \"temperature\": 0.1","}","```","","Parsing is tolerant — surrounding prose and ```` ``` ```` code fences are stripped — but","the payload must be valid JSON with a non-empty `files` array of `{path, content}`","string pairs whose paths stay inside the output directory. If the model returns prose","without a JSON object, you get `The model response could not be parsed into files.` with","sanitized diagnostics (provider/model/response length/head/tail/finish-reason hints)","to make failures actionable. There is no Markdown-fallback parser in v1.","","## Generated `/agent` structure","","```text","agent/","  MASTER.md               stable project intent + assumptions (don't rewrite)","  TODO.md                 phase checklist linking each phase file","  HANDOFF.md              mutable status, updated after every phase","  DECISIONS.md            confirmed / open / log","  REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md     concrete, verifiable review items","  DEEPSEEK_START.md       implementation-agent prompt","  CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md  reviewer prompt","  phases/","    00-project-brief.md","    01-\u003cslug\u003e.md ... NN-\u003cslug\u003e.md","```","","## Security \u0026 privacy","","PackWrite is conservative about what leaves your machine:","","- **API keys are read from the environment only** — never from flags, config, or logs.","- **The model receives your mega prompt and a bounded repository summary:** the root","  name, a one-line README excerpt, detected languages, and included file/directory","  names. PackWrite does not upload the full checkout. Keep sensitive data out of the","  prompt and README excerpt.","- **Secrets are excluded by default** (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa`,","  `id_ed25519`, `.git`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `.next`, `coverage`,","  `target`, `.venv`, and names containing `secret`/`token`); skipped paths are reported.","- **Generated paths are restricted** to the output directory (absolute, `..` traversal,","  backslash-separator, `~` home-expansion, control-character, ambiguous-segment, and","  escaping paths are rejected), configured output directories must be relative project","  paths with no existing symlink components, and generated secret-looking paths are","  rejected. Model responses and generated content have explicit resource ceilings.","- **Prompt payloads are never logged.** `--verbose` reports size only. Explicit raw","  response saves are owner-only, atomic, and refuse to overwrite an existing path.","- **Malformed CLI input fails cleanly** — bad or out-of-range `--temperature` /","  `--timeout` values return an actionable error instead of crashing the runtime.","","Details and reporting: **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)**.","","## Workflows","","**Autonomous implementation.** `agent/DEEPSEEK_START.md` tells the implementation agent","to run on autopilot: read the pack → implement the first incomplete phase → update","`HANDOFF`/`DECISIONS`/`REVIEW_CHECKLIST` → mark the TODO item → continue to the next","phase without human approval → repeat until done, stopping only for defined blockers.","","**Independent review.** When implementation is finished, hand a reviewer","`agent/CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md`. It asks for an overall score, category scores, a","comparison against the mega prompt, scope drift, bugs, missing tests, security issues,","and a step-by-step repair checklist.","","## Output \u0026 exit codes","","The Kujo runtime has no separate stderr, so **all output goes to stdout**, prefixed so","categories stay greppable: `warning (...)`, `! ` (validation warnings), `note:`, and","`error:`. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` operational failure, `2` usage error.","`packwrite prompt \u003ctarget\u003e` prints the prompt verbatim so it pipes cleanly.","A missing prompt uses the built-in fallback. <p dir="auto"><strong>PackWrite turns a project brief into a validated execution pack for coding agents.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">Save your brief as <code>MEGA_PROMPT.md</code> and run PackWrite in your repository. It sends
the brief and a small repository summary to a model, then writes an <code>agent/</code> directory
with phase plans, acceptance criteria, handoff notes, and review prompts. PackWrite
checks the pack's structure and paths; you review its content before using it.</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="strategy AI → MEGA_PROMPT.md → packwrite → /agent pack → implementation agent → reviewer"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>strategy AI → MEGA_PROMPT.md → packwrite → /agent pack → implementation agent → reviewer
</code></pre></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why PackWrite</h2><a id="user-content-why-packwrite" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why PackWrite" href="#why-packwrite"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A large task needs a record of its scope, progress, and decisions. PackWrite keeps
that record beside your code:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><code>MASTER.md</code></strong> — stable project intent + assumptions (don't rewrite).</li>
<li><strong><code>phases/*.md</code></strong> — per-phase specs with scope, out-of-scope, and acceptance criteria.</li>
<li><strong><code>HANDOFF.md</code> / <code>DECISIONS.md</code></strong> — mutable state and a decision log.</li>
<li><strong><code>REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md</code></strong> — concrete, verifiable review items.</li>
<li><strong><code>DEEPSEEK_START.md</code> / <code>CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md</code></strong> — ready-to-paste prompts for an
implementation agent and an independent reviewer.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Code validates the required files, sections, and paths. The model writes the content.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Readiness and scope</h2><a id="user-content-readiness-and-scope" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Readiness and scope" href="#readiness-and-scope"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">PackWrite creates local planning files. It does not implement your project, deploy
code, or coordinate concurrent writers. Review generated instructions before giving
them to an agent. Hosted authentication, organization policy, signing, and deployment
controls belong to the systems that run PackWrite.</p>
<p dir="auto">Current hardening includes:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Output directories must be relative, non-empty, non-traversing paths.</li>
<li>Model manifest paths are validated before dry-runs or writes claim success.</li>
<li>Secret-looking generated paths are rejected, not merely warned about after writing.</li>
<li>Writes are staged and validated before promotion, with rollback on failed promotion.</li>
<li>The full test suite is offline: 248 unit assertions and 116 CLI integration assertions.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">PackWrite is written in the <a href="#about-kujo">Kujo language</a> and run by the Kujo
interpreter. Install Kujo so the <code>kujo</code> command is available on your <code>PATH</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# get the released source
git clone --branch v1.1.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/kujolang/packwrite.git
cd packwrite
./bin/packwrite --help

# or install the launcher on your PATH
make install                      # symlinks bin/packwrite into /usr/local/bin
packwrite --help"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> get the released source</span>
git clone --branch v1.1.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/kujolang/packwrite.git
<span class="pl-c1">cd</span> packwrite
./bin/packwrite --help

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> or install the launcher on your PATH</span>
make install                      <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> symlinks bin/packwrite into /usr/local/bin</span>
packwrite --help</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The destination <code>PREFIX/bin</code> must already exist and be writable. Set <code>PREFIX</code> to
choose a different install root, for example <code>make install PREFIX="$HOME/.local"</code>.
Installation returns a nonzero status if the symlink cannot be created.</p>
<p dir="auto">The launcher preserves your working directory, so config discovery and the generated
<code>/agent</code> pack land where you invoke it.</p>

<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>packwrite summary</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>packwrite config</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="defaults  <  global config (~/.config/packwrite/config.toml)  <  packwrite.toml  <  CLI flags"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>defaults  <  global config (~/.config/packwrite/config.toml)  <  packwrite.toml  <  CLI flags
</code></pre></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Model / provider selection</h2><a id="user-content-model--provider-selection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Model / provider selection" href="#model--provider-selection"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Choose a provider and model with flags or config. PackWrite calls the Kujo
<code>ai_chat</code> builtin through an adapter.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>The adapter speaks only the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions protocol</strong> (it posts
<code>{model, messages}</code>, authenticates with <code>Authorization: Bearer</code>, and reads
<code>choices[0].message.content</code>). Built-in endpoint presets therefore exist only for
providers that expose that protocol natively:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>--provider</code></th>
<th>Endpoint preset</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>deepseek</code></td>
<td><code>https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>openai</code></td>
<td><code>https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>local</code></td>
<td><code>http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Any other provider has <strong>no preset</strong> and must point <code>--endpoint</code> (or <code>[model].endpoint</code>)
at an OpenAI-compatible URL — a gateway such as OpenRouter or LiteLLM works well.</p>
<p dir="auto">Set <code>--model</code> or <code>[model].model</code> to a model your endpoint supports. The default is
<code>deepseek-v4-pro</code>; check your provider's available models before running generation.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Anthropic is not supported natively.</strong> Anthropic's API uses <code>/v1/messages</code> +
<code>x-api-key</code>, which this adapter does not speak. <code>--provider anthropic</code> with no endpoint
fails with a clear error; to use Claude, set <code>--endpoint</code> to an OpenAI-compatible
gateway in front of it.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>API keys come from the environment only</strong> — never from flags or committed config.
PackWrite checks <code>PACKWRITE_API_KEY</code> first, then a provider-specific variable
(<code>DEEPSEEK_API_KEY</code>, <code>OPENAI_API_KEY</code>, <code>ANTHROPIC_API_KEY</code>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Model response format</h2><a id="user-content-model-response-format" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Model response format" href="#model-response-format"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">PackWrite expects the model to return a <strong>JSON file manifest</strong> and nothing else:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{ "files": [ { "path": "agent/MASTER.md", "content": "..." }, ... ] }"><pre>{ <span class="pl-ent">"files"</span>: [ { <span class="pl-ent">"path"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>agent/MASTER.md<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-ent">"content"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>...<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> }, <span class="pl-ii">... </span>] }</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">For DeepSeek structured pack generation, PackWrite requests strict JSON mode and
disables thinking by default:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "response_format": { "type": "json_object" },
  "thinking": { "type": "disabled" },
  "max_tokens": 32000,
  "temperature": 0.1
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"response_format"</span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>json_object<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> },
  <span class="pl-ent">"thinking"</span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>disabled<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> },
  <span class="pl-ent">"max_tokens"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">32000</span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"temperature"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">0.1</span>
}</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Parsing is tolerant — surrounding prose and <code>```</code> code fences are stripped — but
the payload must be valid JSON with a non-empty <code>files</code> array of <code>{path, content}</code>
string pairs whose paths stay inside the output directory. If the model returns prose
without a JSON object, you get <code>The model response could not be parsed into files.</code> with
sanitized diagnostics (provider/model/response length/head/tail/finish-reason hints)
to make failures actionable. There is no Markdown-fallback parser in v1.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security & privacy</h2><a id="user-content-security--privacy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security & privacy" href="#security--privacy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">PackWrite is conservative about what leaves your machine:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>API keys are read from the environment only</strong> — never from flags, config, or logs.</li>
<li><strong>The model receives your mega prompt and a bounded repository summary:</strong> the root
name, a one-line README excerpt, detected languages, and included file/directory
names. PackWrite does not upload the full checkout. Keep sensitive data out of the
prompt and README excerpt.</li>
<li><strong>Secrets are excluded by default</strong> (<code>.env*</code>, <code>*.pem</code>, <code>*.key</code>, <code>id_rsa</code>,
<code>id_ed25519</code>, <code>.git</code>, <code>node_modules</code>, <code>vendor</code>, <code>dist</code>, <code>build</code>, <code>.next</code>, <code>coverage</code>,
<code>target</code>, <code>.venv</code>, and names containing <code>secret</code>/<code>token</code>); skipped paths are reported.</li>
<li><strong>Generated paths are restricted</strong> to the output directory (absolute, <code>..</code> traversal,
backslash-separator, <code>~</code> home-expansion, control-character, ambiguous-segment, and
escaping paths are rejected), configured output directories must be relative project
paths with no existing symlink components, and generated secret-looking paths are
rejected. Model responses and generated content have explicit resource ceilings.</li>
<li><strong>Prompt payloads are never logged.</strong> <code>--verbose</code> reports size only. Explicit raw
response saves are owner-only, atomic, and refuse to overwrite an existing path.</li>
<li><strong>Malformed CLI input fails cleanly</strong> — bad or out-of-range <code>--temperature</code> /
<code>--timeout</code> values return an actionable error instead of crashing the runtime.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Details and reporting: <strong><a href="/kujolang/packwrite/blob/b8467535c74263abc59fd3f48028b67d42cd7e68/SECURITY.md">SECURITY.md</a></strong>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Workflows</h2><a id="user-content-workflows" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Workflows" href="#workflows"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Autonomous implementation.</strong> <code>agent/DEEPSEEK_START.md</code> tells the implementation agent
to run on autopilot: read the pack → implement the first incomplete phase → update
<code>HANDOFF</code>/<code>DECISIONS</code>/<code>REVIEW_CHECKLIST</code> → mark the TODO item → continue to the next
phase without human approval → repeat until done, stopping only for defined blockers.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Independent review.</strong> When implementation is finished, hand a reviewer
<code>agent/CODEX_REVIEW_PROMPT.md</code>. It asks for an overall score, category scores, a
comparison against the mega prompt, scope drift, bugs, missing tests, security issues,
and a step-by-step repair checklist.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Output & exit codes</h2><a id="user-content-output--exit-codes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Output & exit codes" href="#output--exit-codes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The Kujo runtime has no separate stderr, so <strong>all output goes to stdout</strong>, prefixed so
categories stay greppable: <code>warning (...)</code>, <code>! </code> (validation warnings), <code>note:</code>, and
<code>error:</code>. Exit codes: <code>0</code> success, <code>1</code> operational failure, <code>2</code> usage error.
<code>packwrite prompt <target></code> prints the prompt verbatim so it pipes cleanly.
A missing prompt uses the built-in fallback. Existing unreadable files, directories,
and symlinks return an operational error instead of emitting a fallback.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Development</h2><a id="user-content-development" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Development" href="#development"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">The suite (248 unit + 116 CLI integration assertions) is <strong>fully offline</strong> — AI calls go
through a fake-injection seam (<code>PACKWRITE_FAKE_RESPONSE_FILE</code>), so no API key or network
is required. The 24 permission assertions skip under root. See <a href="/kujolang/packwrite/blob/b8467535c74263abc59fd3f48028b67d42cd7e68/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> for setup and the Kujo runtime
conventions.</p>
<p dir="auto">Root files are intentionally kept for project entrypoints and governance:
<code>packwrite.kujo</code> is the CLI entrypoint, <code>bin/packwrite</code> is the launcher, <code>Makefile</code>
drives developer tasks, <code>kujo.toml</code> identifies the Kujo package, and
<code>packwrite.example.toml</code> is the canonical copyable config. Runtime logic lives under
<code>src/</code>; tests live under <code>tests/</code>; user/developer docs live under <code>docs/</code>.</p>

interpreter; it lives in its own repository and does not modify the Kujo language repo.</p>

Kennel","","[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.1.0-black)](https://github.com/kujolang/kennel)","[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)](LICENSE)","[![built with Kujo](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Kujo-white.svg)](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo)","","Kennel is the official package and project manager for [Kujo](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/). It supports deterministic local/source development and immutable first-party package releases through the official static registry.","","Official first-party distribution is available through the versioned HTTPS protocol at `https://kennel.kujolang.ai`. Accounts, third-party publishing, private hosted packages, moderation and public trust scoring remain deferred.","","## Official Kennel Registry","","**Runtime prerequisite:** install [Kujo 1.4.0](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/releases/tag/v1.4.0) or newer. It provides isolated imports and the native package primitives required by Kennel. The installer rejects incompatible runtimes.","","","Kennel **1.1.0** adds global commands and a per-user installer for macOS/Linux. To install from a reviewed source checkout, Git is required:","","```bash","\"${KUJO_BIN:-kujo}\" run scripts/install.kujo --interpreter -- --source .",". \"$HOME/.kennel/env\"","kennel --version","kennel tool install shipcheck","shipcheck --help","```","","The source installer copies tracked checkout files, including reviewed local edits. For an isolated review without shell profile changes, use `--home /absolute/review-directory --no-modify-path` and invoke its `bin/kennel`. `KUJO_BIN` selects a non-default Kujo executable; keep it set when invoking the installed tools if Kujo is not otherwise on PATH.","","Install the released client from the registry:","","```bash","curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh","sh install.sh",". \"$HOME/.kennel/env\"","```","","The installer checks Kujo, verifies the official package archive and provenance, and activates the client atomically. Historical releases are rejected with an explanation. It never installs an unreleased main branch implicitly. See [global tools and installer](docs/global-tools.md) for commands, PATH setup, updates and removal.","","```bash","kennel init --name demo","kennel add changebucket","kennel add kennel@1.0.1","kennel install","kennel info changebucket","kennel search change","```","","The CLI form is also available as `kujo run /path/to/kennel/kennel.kujo --interpreter -- add changebucket --project-dir /path/to/demo`. No GitHub URL or login is needed by consumers. Downloads, provenance and cache bytes are verified before staged archive replacement. Exact versions and digests are locked using additive schema-1 fields.","","The built-in registry is used when no explicit registry or project `index.json` exists. Set `[registry].index = \"https://your-registry.example/api/v1/index.json\"` to override it. Existing file/Git dependencies, local static indexes and local hosted auth/publish commands retain their behavior. Official names are unscoped; future third-party identities use `@scope/name`, with publishing still unavailable.","","Read [the protocol and trust contract](docs/registry/protocol.md), [audit and implementation spec](docs/registry/audit-and-spec.md), and [publisher runbook](docs/registry/publishing.md). The historical Changebucket 1.0.0 release contains the original ChangeBudget CLI; backfill preserves released code.","","## Why Teams Use Kennel","","- Deterministic installs and lockfiles for stable release pipelines","- Local and source-based package/project workflows that run reproducibly in the Kujo interpreter","- Trust-policy enforcement for checksum, signature, and signing key fields","- Scripted verification profiles for fast baseline checks and deeper stage/security gates","","## Verified Behaviors","","Current verified behaviors in this repository:","","- `--flag=value` parsing preserves complete values, including token-like values containing additional `=` characters","- Lockfile output is deterministic and order-stable","- Direct and transitive dependencies are installed and locked deterministically","- Kujo automatically discovers installed package roots named by `kennel.lock`,","  so normal consumers do not need to construct `KUJO_MODULE_PATH` manually","- Unsafe dependency install paths are rejected before local copy or git clone work starts","- Pinned refs are protected during update operations","- Manifest, lockfile, registry metadata, and scaffold writes use atomic replacement","- Token-store replacement is atomic and preserves restrictive mode `0600`","","These behaviors are validated through contract suites and verify scripts in `scripts/`.","","## Supported Environments","","Validated in current project automation:","","- CI: Ubuntu (`ubuntu-latest`) via GitHub Actions","- Local development: macOS and Linux shells with Kujo installed","","Toolchain assumptions:","","- Kujo 1.4.0 or newer, available as `kujo` or overridden with `KUJO_BIN`","- Bash available for verification scripts","","The installed launcher supports `kennel --version`. Direct `kujo run kennel.kujo` retains the existing native CLI contract.","","## Security Posture Summary","","- Use `--token-file` when possible to avoid shell-history token exposure","- Keep token stores outside repositories when practical","- Prefer least-privilege local and source-based workflows for reproducibility","- Prefer explicit refs and commit pins for reproducibility","- Configure trust policy values in `kennel.toml` for sensitive environments","","Detailed security behavior and command mappings are in `docs/stage-3-security-model.md`.","","## Capability Overview","","| Capability Area | Status | Notes |","| --- | --- | --- |","| Core dependency lifecycle | Available | `init`, `new`, `add`, `install`, `update`, `remove`, `list`, `info`, `validate` |","| Deterministic lockfiles | Available | `kennel.lock` generation and reinstall parity |","| Local/source package workflows | Available | `file:` and local-path dependency installation |","| Trust policy checks | Available | `checksum`, `signature`, `signing_key` validations for local/source workflows |","| Full transitive solver | Available | Deterministic graph install with conflict diagnostics for incompatible transitive specs |","| Semver range solver | Available (optional) | Enable with `[policy.resolution].semver_ranges = true` for deterministic tag-based range selection |","| Local hosted registry lifecycle | Available | Auth, publish, access, visibility, search/metadata APIs, and hosted install against local registry artifacts |","| Multi-registry static index routing | Available | Configure `[registry].index` + `[registry].mirrors` for deterministic name-resolution fallback in `add`, `info`, and `search` |","| Operated public registry service | Deferred | Public discovery, hosted moderation, malware scanning, trust scoring, and registry operations at internet scale |","","## Production Readiness Boundary","","Kennel is production-oriented for its current launch-safe scope: deterministic lockfiles, explicit source handling, local/static registry workflows, local hosted-registry artifacts, trust-policy checks, source-policy gates, and broad scripted validation.","","It should not yet be presented as a universal enterprise package ecosystem. The remaining enterprise-exemplar work is mostly around scale and operated-service readiness: bounded parallel install performance, stronger provenance around release artifacts and hosted downloads, migration/offline cache ergonomics, richer registry audit/export tooling, and clearer adoption funnels for new Kujo users. See `docs/KENNEL_ENTERPRISE_READINESS_REVIEW_2026_06_19.md` for the current review and next-session backlog.","","## Quick Start","","```bash","cd /path/to/kujolang/kennel","kujo run kennel.kujo --interpreter -- help","","kujo run kennel.kujo --interpreter -- init --name kennel-demo","kujo run kennel.kujo --interpreter -- add file:../some-local-package --alias some-local-package","kujo run kennel.kujo --interpreter -- install","kujo run kennel.kujo --interpreter -- validate","```","","## Trust Policy Configuration","","```toml","[trust]","checksum = \"sha256:...\"","signature = \"sig-...\"","signing_key = \"key-...\"","```","","When declared, trust policy is enforced during add/install/update workflows.","","## Source Policy Configuration","","```toml","[policy.source]","strict_mutable_refs = true","allow_mutable_refs = false","```","","When strict mode is enabled, mutable refs (for example, branch refs or implicit HEAD) are blocked for non-path dependencies during add/install/update. Operators can explicitly override once per command with `--allow-mutable-ref`.","","## Resolution Policy Configuration","","```toml","[policy.resolution]","semver_ranges = true","```","","When semver range mode is enabled, range selectors (for example `^2.1.0`, `~1.4.2`, or `\u003e=1.2.0 \u003c2.0.0`) are resolved against repository tags deterministically by selecting the highest compatible semver tag.","","## Static Index Routing Configuration","","```toml","[registry]","index = \"./registry/index.primary.json\"","mirrors = [\"./registry/index.secondary.json\", \"./registry/index.tertiary.json\"]","```","","Name-based package operations (`add \u003cname\u003e`, `info \u003cname\u003e`, and `search \u003cquery\u003e`) evaluate static indexes in configured order (`index` first, then `mirrors`) and stop on the first successful match. Missing local files and HTTP URLs are skipped with diagnostics. HTTPS version-1 registries support anonymous remote resolution; integrity/schema failures fail closed.","","## Deferred Roadmap","","The following areas are intentionally out of launch-safe scope for now:","","- third-party package discovery and publishing","- an operated, multi-tenant public registry service","- internet-scale account recovery and abuse handling","- moderation and malware scanning","- trust scoring","- service-backed package signing and provenance verification","","## Validation and Release Gates","","Primary validation entrypoints:","","- `scripts/verify-all.sh`","- `scripts/verify-profiles.sh`","- `scripts/verify-shell-quality.sh`","- `scripts/verify-macos-smoke.sh`","- `scripts/verify-contract-suites.sh`","- `scripts/verify-security-regression-suite.sh`","- `scripts/verify-command-failure-matrix.sh`","- `scripts/verify-nightly-full-regression-workflow.sh`","- `scripts/cleanup-local-artifacts.sh`","- `scripts/benchmark-harness.sh`","","CI release-confidence coverage:","","- Pull request and push gates run stage and security profiles.","- Static script quality gates enforce ShellCheck diagnostics in CI.","- A nightly scheduled workflow runs `verify-profiles.sh full` and publishes artifacts for triage.","- Nightly CI exports `nightly-ci-quality-report` with pass/fail trend, duration, and warning summaries.","","Script input convention:","","- `KUJO_BIN` is the shared Kujo binary override for verify scripts","- Verify scripts default `KUJO_BIN` to `kujo` if not provided","- If `kujo` is not on PATH locally, run with `KUJO_BIN=/path/to/kujo bash ./scripts/verify-all.sh core`","","Run core baseline gate:","","```bash","bash ./scripts/verify-all.sh core","```","","Run profile-based gates:","","```bash","bash ./scripts/verify-profiles.sh core","bash ./scripts/verify-profiles.sh stage2","bash ./scripts/verify-profiles.sh stage3","bash ./scripts/verify-profiles.sh security","bash ./scripts/verify-profiles.sh full","```","","Run split contract suites:","","```bash","bash ./scripts/verify-contract-suites.sh","```","","Run deterministic benchmark harness:","","```bash","bash ./scripts/benchmark-harness.sh","BENCH_DRY_RUN=1 bash ./scripts/benchmark-harness.sh","```","","Clean local validation artifacts:","","```bash","bash ./scripts/cleanup-local-artifacts.sh","```","","## Enterprise Rollout Path","","Suggested adoption order:","","1. Start with `core` profile in pull requests.","2. Add `stage2` or `stage3` gates based on change surface.","3. Require `security` profile for security-sensitive and release-candidate changes.","4. Run `full` profile before release tagging.","","## Repository Layout","","Top-level runtime artifacts:","","- `kennel.toml`: manifest","- `kennel.lock`: deterministic dependency snapshot","- <p dir="auto">Kennel is the official package and project manager for <a href="https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/">Kujo</a>. It supports deterministic local/source development and immutable first-party package releases through the official static registry.</p>
<p dir="auto">Official first-party distribution is available through the versioned HTTPS protocol at <code>https://kennel.kujolang.ai</code>. Accounts, third-party publishing, private hosted packages, moderation and public trust scoring remain deferred.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Official Kennel Registry</h2><a id="user-content-official-kennel-registry" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Official Kennel Registry" href="#official-kennel-registry"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Runtime prerequisite:</strong> install <a href="https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/releases/tag/v1.4.0">Kujo 1.4.0</a> or newer. It provides isolated imports and the native package primitives required by Kennel. The installer rejects incompatible runtimes.</p>
<p dir="auto">Kennel <strong>1.1.0</strong> adds global commands and a per-user installer for macOS/Linux. To install from a reviewed source checkout, Git is required:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=""${KUJO_BIN:-kujo}" run scripts/install.kujo --interpreter -- --source .
. "$HOME/.kennel/env"
kennel --version
kennel tool install shipcheck
shipcheck --help"><pre><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">${KUJO_BIN<span class="pl-k">:-</span>kujo}</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> run scripts/install.kujo --interpreter -- --source <span class="pl-c1">.</span>
<span class="pl-c1">.</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.kennel/env<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
kennel --version
kennel tool install shipcheck
shipcheck --help</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The source installer copies tracked checkout files, including reviewed local edits. For an isolated review without shell profile changes, use <code>--home /absolute/review-directory --no-modify-path</code> and invoke its <code>bin/kennel</code>. <code>KUJO_BIN</code> selects a non-default Kujo executable; keep it set when invoking the installed tools if Kujo is not otherwise on PATH.</p>
<p dir="auto">Install the released client from the registry:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh
sh install.sh
. "$HOME/.kennel/env""><pre>curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh
sh install.sh
<span class="pl-c1">.</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.kennel/env<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The installer checks Kujo, verifies the official package archive and provenance, and activates the client atomically. Historical releases are rejected with an explanation. It never installs an unreleased main branch implicitly. See <a href="/kujolang/kennel/blob/6e2fc20560037970df5202e1b1ca8f61c3395570/docs/global-tools.md">global tools and installer</a> for commands, PATH setup, updates and removal.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kennel init --name demo
kennel add changebucket
kennel add kennel@1.0.1
kennel install
kennel info changebucket
kennel search change"><pre>kennel init --name demo
kennel add changebucket
kennel add kennel@1.0.1
kennel install
kennel info changebucket
kennel search change</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The CLI form is also available as <code>kujo run /path/to/kennel/kennel.kujo --interpreter -- add changebucket --project-dir /path/to/demo</code>. No GitHub URL or login is needed by consumers. Downloads, provenance and cache bytes are verified before staged archive replacement. Exact versions and digests are locked using additive schema-1 fields.</p>
<p dir="auto">The built-in registry is used when no explicit registry or project <code>index.json</code> exists. Set <code>[registry].index = "https://your-registry.example/api/v1/index.json"</code> to override it. Existing file/Git dependencies, local static indexes and local hosted auth/publish commands retain their behavior. Official names are unscoped; future third-party identities use <code>@scope/name</code>, with publishing still unavailable.</p>
<p dir="auto">Read <a href="/kujolang/kennel/blob/6e2fc20560037970df5202e1b1ca8f61c3395570/docs/registry/protocol.md">the protocol and trust contract</a>, <a href="/kujolang/kennel/blob/6e2fc20560037970df5202e1b1ca8f61c3395570/docs/registry/audit-and-spec.md">audit and implementation spec</a>, and <a href="/kujolang/kennel/blob/6e2fc20560037970df5202e1b1ca8f61c3395570/docs/registry/publishing.md">publisher runbook</a>. The historical Changebucket 1.0.0 release contains the original ChangeBudget CLI; backfill preserves released code.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Teams Use Kennel</h2><a id="user-content-why-teams-use-kennel" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Teams Use Kennel" href="#why-teams-use-kennel"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Deterministic installs and lockfiles for stable release pipelines</li>
<li>Local and source-based package/project workflows that run reproducibly in the Kujo interpreter</li>
<li>Trust-policy enforcement for checksum, signature, and signing key fields</li>
<li>Scripted verification profiles for fast baseline checks and deeper stage/security gates</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Verified Behaviors</h2><a id="user-content-verified-behaviors" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Verified Behaviors" href="#verified-behaviors"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Current verified behaviors in this repository:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>--flag=value</code> parsing preserves complete values, including token-like values containing additional <code>=</code> characters</li>
<li>Lockfile output is deterministic and order-stable</li>
<li>Direct and transitive dependencies are installed and locked deterministically</li>
<li>Kujo automatically discovers installed package roots named by <code>kennel.lock</code>,
so normal consumers do not need to construct <code>KUJO_MODULE_PATH</code> manually</li>
<li>Unsafe dependency install paths are rejected before local copy or git clone work starts</li>
<li>Pinned refs are protected during update operations</li>
<li>Manifest, lockfile, registry metadata, and scaffold writes use atomic replacement</li>
<li>Token-store replacement is atomic and preserves restrictive mode <code>0600</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">These behaviors are validated through contract suites and verify scripts in <code>scripts/</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Supported Environments</h2><a id="user-content-supported-environments" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Supported Environments" href="#supported-environments"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Validated in current project automation:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>CI: Ubuntu (<code>ubuntu-latest</code>) via GitHub Actions</li>
<li>Local development: macOS and Linux shells with Kujo installed</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Toolchain assumptions:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Kujo 1.4.0 or newer, available as <code>kujo</code> or overridden with <code>KUJO_BIN</code></li>
<li>Bash available for verification scripts</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The installed launcher supports <code>kennel --version</code>. Direct <code>kujo run kennel.kujo</code> retains the existing native CLI contract.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security Posture Summary</h2><a id="user-content-security-posture-summary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security Posture Summary" href="#security-posture-summary"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Use <code>--token-file</code> when possible to avoid shell-history token exposure</li>
<li>Keep token stores outside repositories when practical</li>
<li>Prefer least-privilege local and source-based workflows for reproducibility</li>
<li>Prefer explicit refs and commit pins for reproducibility</li>
<li>Configure trust policy values in <code>kennel.toml</code> for sensitive environments</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Detailed security behavior and command mappings are in <code>docs/stage-3-security-model.md</code>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Production Readiness Boundary</h2><a id="user-content-production-readiness-boundary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Production Readiness Boundary" href="#production-readiness-boundary"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Kennel is production-oriented for its current launch-safe scope: deterministic lockfiles, explicit source handling, local/static registry workflows, local hosted-registry artifacts, trust-policy checks, source-policy gates, and broad scripted validation.</p>
<p dir="auto">It should not yet be presented as a universal enterprise package ecosystem. The remaining enterprise-exemplar work is mostly around scale and operated-service readiness: bounded parallel install performance, stronger provenance around release artifacts and hosted downloads, migration/offline cache ergonomics, richer registry audit/export tooling, and clearer adoption funnels for new Kujo users. See <code>docs/KENNEL_ENTERPRISE_READINESS_REVIEW_2026_06_19.md</code> for the current review and next-session backlog.</p>

<p dir="auto">Top-level runtime artifacts:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>kennel.toml</code>: manifest</li>
<li><code>kennel.lock</code>: deterministic dependency snapshot</li>
<li><code>kennel_packages/</code>: installed source trees</li>
<li><code>AGENTS.md</code>: agent and contributor guidance for canonical examples, fixture boundaries, and search hygiene</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Implementation layout:</p>
<ul dir="auto">

Current published Kujo ecosystem versions, recent source changes, and explicit installation boundaries.

Source 0.1.0 — October 14, 2026

Source 0.1.0 is the first public MIT release of the Git review and evidence platform. Its Node.js server, CLI and browser UI connect agent proposals to authorized decisions. Install through Git and npm; Source is not a Kennel package. The Source guide covers local demos, Cloudflare integration and experimental deployment boundaries.

October 21 companion updates

Ability 1.3.0, AI Chat 1.3.1, CaseFile 1.0.2, Concord 1.1.2, ShipCheck 1.0.2, RunLedger 1.2.1, PatchBrief 1.0.3, Spec 1.0.2, SSG 1.2.1, Source 0.1.1, Muzzle 1.1.3 and Watchdog 1.2.2 are published. The table and linked guides identify the current versions. Each project retains its documented installation and deployment boundaries.

Start here

Install Kujo 1.9.0 for the current runtime. A standalone binary runs ordinary Kujo programs without Python, Node.js, or Rust. Individual applications and tools retain their own dependencies, supported platforms, runtime pins, and update procedures.

Kennel's official registry distributes first-party package artifacts. Kennel 1.2.1 is published separately; Kujo 1.9.0 does not change its version or historical package artifacts. See package workflows before assuming that upgrading Kujo also updates Kennel or other tools.

What changed in 1.8

Kujo 1.8.0 shares optional program analysis between CLI checking and the LSP, improves gradual inference and editor information, adds struct generator methods, and retains one measured generator-resume optimization. It strengthens VM/interpreter and optimizer-safety evidence without changing the v1 language contract.

Durable review, checkpoints, restart/resume and external-effect replay control are implemented with companion tools such as Dispatch. Watchdog and RunLedger observe and correlate evidence; they do not become workflow authority.

Experimental companion contracts

Wave C effect assurance remains experimental beta, opt-in, required/deny within a bounded single-effect domain, with alpha compatibility retained. SQLite, Workcell Git CAS and Ability application profiles supply effect-specific predicates; Dispatch owns replay admission.

Wave D generic interoperability and participant SDK APIs remain experimental alpha under a trusted-local-host model. Six participant forms, including independent TypeScript and Python implementations, have been exercised. Participant SDK packages remain private/unpublished. A correlation match is not permission to replay.

This release does not promise exactly-once execution, universal rollback, general machine-loss recovery, remote authenticated participant trust, multi-effect assurance or stable participant SDK APIs. Source-blind agent adopter rehearsal passed; human adopter usability remains post-release validation.

See the 1.8.0 release and checksums, release-readiness evidence, and publication record.

Private projects retain their documented access boundaries.

Agent discovery

The public Kujo MCP catalog exposes read-only project, skill, workflow, and installer guidance. It is separate from the MCP framework and from private application gateways. Refreshes publish a reviewed static snapshot; they do not execute installer commands or grant application permissions.

Kujo 1.8 runtime and companion delivery

Kujo 1.8 does not republish or silently upgrade companion tools. RunLedger 1.2.0, AI SDK 1.2.0 and Agents SDK 1.1.2 are published independently. AI SDK 1.2.0 adds state persistence, strict accounting, and transport controls; its release notes distinguish offline verification from live-provider evidence. Workcell, Ability and MCP 1.2.0 distribute the controlled-execution cohort while retaining experimental assurance/interoperability boundaries. Dispatch 1.3.0 completes this controller release cohort with the same experimental boundaries. Stop older workers and follow its backup/upgrade instructions before changing persisted-state versions.

SSG 1.2.0 requires pinned esbuild 0.28.2 for minified builds and adds explicit private-image opt-in and a separate DocGen repository-CI budget. See the SSG upgrade notes.

Agents SDK 1.1.3

The October 13 patch hardens approval, handoff, state, storage, retry, and token-accounting behavior while preserving public contracts. It supersedes 1.1.2 for new installations. See the Agents SDK guide for compatibility notes and the remaining cost-unit conversion limit.

October 14 capability updates

PatchBrief 1.0.2, CaseFile 1.0.1, MCP 1.3.2, ShipCheck 1.0.1, Scent 1.1.0, Kennel 1.2.0, Fence 1.1.0, Concord 1.1.1, Eval 1.1.0, CRUD API 1.0.1 and Dispatch 1.4.0 are published. Dispatch 1.4.0 requires Kujo 1.8.1. RAG 1.1.0 remains an unpublished candidate pending required review evidence; local functional tests do not certify hosted deployments.

Kujo OpenCode launch — 2026-10-18

Kujo OpenCode 0.2.0 is published on npm and GitHub. It brings six specialists, 62 supported capabilities, native approvals and inspectable receipts to OpenCode 2. Registry installation and upgrade checks passed. Native host checks cover Linux, macOS and Windows; live specialist evidence uses macOS and ChatGPT. Install through npm, not Kennel.

Kujo 1.8.2 maintenance release

Kujo 1.8.2 resolves ZIP security advisories and retired YAML, credential-store and bincode dependencies. It preserves Kujo archive behavior, stored credentials and legacy hyphenation dictionaries, corrects native dictionary handling and tightens capability and filesystem boundaries. Bounded HTTP stream collection is available. Rust embedders accessing Value::ZipArchive.writer must follow the ZIP 9 migration guide; Kujo scripts require no archive API migration.

See the release notes. Rust 1.89 remains the source-build minimum; experimental companion protocols and participant SDKs are not promoted by this patch.

Kujo 1.9.0 runtime release

Kujo 1.9.0 adds checked nested collection and struct writes, strict UTF-8 conversion, byte iteration, fallible comparator sorting, regex callbacks and match counting, headerless CSV, decimal formatting and wrapping arithmetic. Shared bytecode and copy-on-write storage improvements preserve retained values and atomic failed writes.

Native installation and upgrades from 1.8.2 and npm installation passed on all five targets. The publication record identifies the exact source and verification runs. Companion protocols and participant SDKs retain their experimental boundaries.

A correlation match never authorizes replay.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch is a workflow orchestration engine for reliable AI systems built in Kujo.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt routes structured work through repeatable workflow templates and produces reviewable run state, traces, reports, and handoff bundles.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch is strongest as a Control-layer primitive: workflow routing, run-state persistence, import/export, approval gates, and auditable orchestration evidence.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch is a showcase of Kujo's module system, typed workflow data, CLI runtime,\nand testable agent orchestration—not an enterprise certification or a drop-in\nmulti-tenant service. Start with the credential-free fixture below, then use\n\u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/enterprise-deployment.md\"\u003ethe deployment guide\u003c/a\u003e for the production trust\nmodel and \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/audits/next-review-v1.3-2026-09-22.md\"\u003ethe 1.3 follow-up review\u003c/a\u003e for open work.\nFor an existing deployment, read \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/UPGRADING_TO_1_3.md\"\u003ethe 1.3 upgrade guide\u003c/a\u003e\nbefore changing the runtime or sharing an output root with older workers.\nThe supported release runtime is \u003cstrong\u003eKujo 1.8.1 on Linux/macOS (POSIX)\u003c/strong\u003e.\n\u003ccode\u003erelease/dispatch-v1.4.1.refs\u003c/code\u003e pins the installer closure;\n\u003ccode\u003erelease/dispatch-v1.4.1-validation.refs\u003c/code\u003e pins the released companion integration\ncohort. This keeps JSON-mode and schema validation policy in the SDK instead of reimplementing it in Dispatch.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDeterministic Agent And Model Routing\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-deterministic-agent-and-model-routing\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Deterministic Agent And Model Routing\" href=\"#deterministic-agent-and-model-routing\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor a complete setup, policy, live-provider, inspection, and troubleshooting guide,\nsee \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/HOWTO.md\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eHOWTO.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor a shareable introduction to the feature, its architecture, and installation\nboundaries, see \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/BLOG_ROUTER.md\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eBLOG_ROUTER.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRouting is opt-in. Workflows without \u003ccode\u003erouting.enabled: true\u003c/code\u003e retain their configured\nagent and model exactly. An enabled workflow supplies a versioned AI SDK model\ncatalog, workflow defaults, and optional step constraints. Dispatch validates the\ncatalog hash, rejects candidates that violate hard constraints, and applies a\nstable quality-first ordering to the remainder. It persists the complete decision,\ncandidate rejections, attempts, catalog provenance, and evaluation outcome before\nthe model call.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch owns policy and run decisions. AI SDK owns provider/model catalog metadata.\nAgents SDK defines the compatible agent vocabulary (\u003ccode\u003ehandler_id\u003c/code\u003e, versioned\n\u003ccode\u003eexecution_contract\u003c/code\u003e, capabilities, model candidates, and risk metadata). Agent\nsubstitution is permitted only when enabled and handler-compatible or when the\nexecution contracts match exactly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBroader policy cannot be weakened by an agent or step. Allowlists intersect,\nrequirements and denylists accumulate, minimums increase, and maximums decrease.\nUnknown providers are rejected unless they are one of the explicit adapters:\n\u003ccode\u003efixture\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eopenai\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eopenrouter\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edeepseek\u003c/code\u003e, or configured \u003ccode\u003ecustom\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSee \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/control-boundaries.md\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edocs/control-boundaries.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e for evaluation,\npolicy, evidence, review, resume, and effect-aware retry contracts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOn resume, Dispatch reuses the persisted route. It will not silently reroute if the\ncatalog, model, agent, handler, execution contract, or plugin that supplied a route\nis unavailable. Same-route retries remain distinct from bounded fallback to a new\nroute. Provider failures, evaluation failures, and fallback eligibility are\nrecorded as route lifecycle trace events.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRun the offline example without credentials:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"DISPATCH_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=true kujo run dispatch.kujo demo \u0026quot;Routing review\u0026quot; \\\n  --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json \\\n  --yes --non-interactive\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eDISPATCH_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=true kujo run dispatch.kujo demo \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003eRouting review\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e \\\n  --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json \\\n  --yes --non-interactive\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe example is intentionally fixture-backed. \u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ereport.json\u003c/code\u003e, the\n\u003ccode\u003einspect --json\u003c/code\u003e envelope, and the runner result metadata expose \u003ccode\u003eroute_decisions\u003c/code\u003e\nand \u003ccode\u003eroute_attempts\u003c/code\u003e. Secrets and raw provider output remain subject to Dispatch's\nexisting artifact redaction policy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eValidate configuration and explain the deterministic choice before execution:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"dispatch validate --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json\ndispatch explain-route --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003edispatch validate --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json\ndispatch explain-route --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCatalogs may be referenced with \u003ccode\u003erouting.model_catalog_file\u003c/code\u003e; Dispatch resolves\nthe path relative to the workflow and embeds the loaded catalog in persisted run\nstate. Declarative agents can use the built-in \u003ccode\u003ehandler_id: \"model\"\u003c/code\u003e rather than\nshipping custom runtime code. Evaluation outcome \u003ccode\u003erequest_human_review\u003c/code\u003e uses the\nnative Dispatch pause/resume approval lifecycle.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMinimal workflow routing
