mutation mode is enabled (\u003ccode\u003e--strict-mutations\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_STRICT_MUTATION_MODE=true\u003c/code\u003e), \u003ccode\u003edoctor --write\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecleanup --apply\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eimport-run\u003c/code\u003e are blocked unless \u003ccode\u003e--confirm-mutation\u003c/code\u003e is present or \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_MUTATION_CONFIRM=true\u003c/code\u003e is set.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edoctor\u003c/code\u003e supports incremental scope via \u003ccode\u003e--run-ids\u003c/code\u003e (explicit run selection) and \u003ccode\u003e--recent-count\u003c/code\u003e (most recently updated runs only), which helps reduce scan latency on large catalogs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eshow --json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einspect --json\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edoctor --json\u003c/code\u003e emit consistent machine-readable envelopes with shared metadata keys (\u003ccode\u003ecommand\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eok\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eoutput_root\u003c/code\u003e) plus command-specific payload data.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eruns --json --diagnostics\u003c/code\u003e includes index diagnostics metadata such as \u003ccode\u003eindex_fallback_count\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eindex_rebuild_count\u003c/code\u003e to surface catalog/index health quickly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edemo --tags\u003c/code\u003e stores normalized per-run metadata labels and \u003ccode\u003eruns --tags\u003c/code\u003e filters to runs that include all requested tags.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch is template-driven: \u003ccode\u003edemo\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eresume\u003c/code\u003e select workflows by template ID through \u003ccode\u003e--workflow \u0026lt;template-id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e. Direct Spec-file ingestion is not part of the verified command surface in this repository.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch supports \u003ccode\u003ehelp\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003e--help\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eversion\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003e--version\u003c/code\u003e. The version is sourced from \u003ccode\u003ekennel.toml\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003e[package].version\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSteps can be marked \u003ccode\u003eoptional\u003c/code\u003e in a workflow template. When an optional step fails (including a tool blocked by policy), Dispatch records a \u003ccode\u003estep_skipped\u003c/code\u003e trace event and continues the run instead of failing it. The built-in \u003ccode\u003eretry_probe\u003c/code\u003e step is optional, so the \u003ccode\u003eresearch-report\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ecrud-reliability\u003c/code\u003e templates complete even when \u003ccode\u003eflaky_reliability_tool\u003c/code\u003e is denied (for example under the \u003ccode\u003estaging\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eproduction\u003c/code\u003e policy profiles).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edemo\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eresume\u003c/code\u003e accept lifecycle observability and control flags:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--webhook-sink \u0026lt;path.jsonl\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e appends lifecycle events (one JSON object per line) to a local sink file. Absolute/traversal paths are blocked unless \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_ALLOW_ANY_WEBHOOK_SINK=true\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--webhook-url \u0026lt;https-url\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e records each signed envelope in the durable outbox before bounded delivery. Failed deliveries are dead-lettered and can be inspected or replayed with \u003ccode\u003edispatch webhooks status|replay\u003c/code\u003e; webhook failure does not fail the workflow.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--cancel-after-step \u0026lt;step-id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e cooperatively cancels the run after the named step completes, producing a \u003ccode\u003ecancelled\u003c/code\u003e lifecycle state.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTool and agent steps can declare an \u003ccode\u003eidempotency_key\u003c/code\u003e; a successfully\ncheckpointed result is cached in run state and reused on resume. A process can\ndie after an external effect but before its checkpoint, so Dispatch provides\nat-least-once replay in that window, not exactly-once effects. Tool handlers\nreceive a stable \u003ccode\u003econtext.effect_idempotency_key\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003erun_id:step_id\u003c/code\u003e) on retries\nand resume; the external service must enforce it for consequential actions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCommon Usage Flows\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-common-usage-flows\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Common Usage Flows\" href=\"#common-usage-flows\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e1. Use \u003ccode\u003e--allow-unsigned-bundle\u003c/code\u003e only for an explicitly trusted local development transfer; production imports must remain authenticated. Verification failures return deterministic \u003ccode\u003einvalid_bundle_signature\u003c/code\u003e errors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSignatures use standard HMAC-SHA256 (\u003ccode\u003ehmac-sha256-v1\u003c/code\u003e): each artifact is hashed, the per-artifact digests are bound to the run id, and the canonical message is authenticated with the shared key. Verification uses Kujo's constant-time HMAC tag verification. The signing key is required for both signing and verification.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBundles record a \u003ccode\u003ekey_id\u003c/code\u003e (default \u003ccode\u003edefault\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY_ID\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003e--signing-key-id\u003c/code\u003e). During a key rotation window, verification can trust multiple keys at once via \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEYS\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003eid1=key1,id2=key2\u003c/code\u003e): the verifier selects the key matching the bundle's \u003ccode\u003ekey_id\u003c/code\u003e, falling back to the single signing key when no set entry matches.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrefer \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY\u003c/code\u003e (env) over \u003ccode\u003e--signing-key\u003c/code\u003e (CLI flag) so the secret does not appear in process arguments or shell history.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--signing-key\u003c/code\u003e can be passed directly, but using \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY\u003c/code\u003e is recommended for non-interactive and managed environments.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 dir=\"auto\"\u003eArtifacts:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e: full run state snapshot\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrace.json\u003c/code\u003e: structured execution trace\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrace.md\u003c/code\u003e: human-readable trace timeline\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWatchdog integration uses \u003ccode\u003erender_watchdog_native_events\u003c/code\u003e from\n\u003ccode\u003esrc/core/trace.kujo\u003c/code\u003e. It projects run/workflow/task correlation and lifecycle\nstatus into \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog.native-event.v1\u003c/code\u003e while excluding messages, step payloads,\ninputs, outputs, and paths. Dispatch remains the orchestrator and state owner;\nthe embedding host owns fail-open delivery and Watchdog owns privacy,\npersistence, retention, and export.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ereport.md\u003c/code\u003e: human-readable report\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ereport.json\u003c/code\u003e: machine-readable report payload\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003edispatch-mutations.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e: active mutation/policy audit log for \u003ccode\u003edoctor --write\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecleanup --apply\u003c/code\u003e, bundle imports, and policy-denied tool attempts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003edispatch-mutations.\u0026lt;slot\u0026gt;.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e: rotated mutation audit backups controlled by \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_MUTATION_AUDIT_MAX_BYTES\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_MUTATION_AUDIT_MAX_BACKUPS\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e.dispatch-run-index.json\u003c/code\u003e: run metadata index used for faster run listing/filtering\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll run artifacts (\u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etrace.json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etrace.md\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ereport.*\u003c/code\u003e, the run index, and signed bundles) are written atomically: content is staged to a temporary file and renamed into place, so a crash or a concurrent reader never observes a partially written file. The run index (\u003ccode\u003e.dispatch-run-index.json\u003c/code\u003e) is a cache that can be rebuilt from per-run \u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e files; \u003ccode\u003eruns\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003edoctor\u003c/code\u003e fall back to scanning state when the index is missing or malformed. For strict isolation under heavy concurrency, use a dedicated \u003ccode\u003e--output-root\u003c/code\u003e per service.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eProtected assurance-aware state uses the guarded codec documented in \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/persisted-assurance-negotiation.md\"\u003epersisted negotiation\u003c/a\u003e; use the state loader instead of parsing its raw storage as JSON. Legacy state remains JSON. Contract metadata is embedded in persisted machine-readable artifacts: \u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etrace.json\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003ereport.json\u003c/code\u003e include \u003ccode\u003eartifact_contract_version\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eschema_name\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eschema_version\u003c/code\u003e fields to support schema-aware integrations and forward-compatible readers.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDispatch redacts sensitive fields (for example keys containing \u003ccode\u003eapi_key\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etoken\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eauthorization\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esecret\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epassword\u003c/code\u003e) before writing persisted artifacts.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePolicy-denied tool execution attempts are recorded in trace events (\u003ccode\u003epolicy_denied\u003c/code\u003e) and mutation audit entries (\u003ccode\u003eoperation=policy_deny\u003c/code\u003e) including run and command context.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTool policy can be sourced from a reusable profile alias (\u003ccode\u003e--policy-profile\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003epolicy_profile\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eDISPATCH_POLICY_PROFILE\u003c/code\u003e) plus explicit allow/deny controls. Explicit \u003ccode\u003eallow_tools\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003edeny_tools\u003c/code\u003e override profile defaults when provided. CLI flags take precedence over config and environment values.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBuilt-in policy profile aliases:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul Streaming step IDs must not contain path separators.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRun execution holds a process-owned POSIX advisory lock on \u003ccode\u003e.dispatch-run.lock\u003c/code\u003e.\nThe file is never unlinked, and the OS releases the handle when the worker exits;\nlock age no longer grants ownership. Quiesce older workers before upgrading:\ntheir age-based cleanup protocol does not coordinate with advisory locks. Run\ndirectories on multiple hosts still need a distributed lock and storage layer.\nState schema v1 artifacts migrate additively to schema v2 when loaded, with the\nmigration recorded in \u003ccode\u003estate.json\u003c/code\u003e. This keeps JSON-mode and schema validation policy in the SDK instead of reimplementing it in Dispatch.","","## Deterministic Agent And Model Routing","","For a complete setup, policy, live-provider, inspection, and troubleshooting guide,","see [`HOWTO.md`](HOWTO.md).","","For a shareable introduction to the feature, its architecture, and installation","boundaries, see [`BLOG_ROUTER.md`](BLOG_ROUTER.md).","","Routing is opt-in. Workflows without `routing.enabled: true` retain their configured","agent and model exactly. An enabled workflow supplies a versioned AI SDK model","catalog, workflow defaults, and optional step constraints. Dispatch validates the","catalog hash, rejects candidates that violate hard constraints, and applies a","stable quality-first ordering to the remainder. It persists the complete decision,","candidate rejections, attempts, catalog provenance, and evaluation outcome before","the model call.","","Dispatch owns policy and run decisions. AI SDK owns provider/model catalog metadata.","Agents SDK defines the compatible agent vocabulary (`handler_id`, versioned","`execution_contract`, capabilities, model candidates, and risk metadata). <p dir="auto">Dispatch 1.4 adds bounded graph controls, sourced resource accounting, retained-host
recovery and an experimental installed operator. Durable approval decisions are
bound to authoritative revisions and receipts.
See <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/RELEASE_1_4_1.md">release notes</a> and the <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/UPGRADING_TO_1_3.md">upgrade guide</a>.
Effect assurance beta and participant interoperability alpha remain experimental,
opt-in, and under a trusted local host. Separate participant SDK packages remain
unpublished. A correlation match never authorizes replay.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch is a workflow orchestration engine for reliable AI systems built in Kujo.</p>
<p dir="auto">It routes structured work through repeatable workflow templates and produces reviewable run state, traces, reports, and handoff bundles.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch is strongest as a Control-layer primitive: workflow routing, run-state persistence, import/export, approval gates, and auditable orchestration evidence.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch is a showcase of Kujo's module system, typed workflow data, CLI runtime,
and testable agent orchestration—not an enterprise certification or a drop-in
multi-tenant service. Start with the credential-free fixture below, then use
<a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/enterprise-deployment.md">the deployment guide</a> for the production trust
model and <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/audits/next-review-v1.3-2026-09-22.md">the 1.3 follow-up review</a> for open work.
For an existing deployment, read <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/UPGRADING_TO_1_3.md">the 1.3 upgrade guide</a>
before changing the runtime or sharing an output root with older workers.
The supported release runtime is <strong>Kujo 1.8.1 on Linux/macOS (POSIX)</strong>.
<code>release/dispatch-v1.4.1.refs</code> pins the installer closure;
<code>release/dispatch-v1.4.1-validation.refs</code> pins the released companion integration
cohort. Older candidate manifests remain historical evidence. The runtime supplies
process-owned locks and confined directory durability. Quiesce old workers before
upgrading; never mix lock protocols on a run directory. Live provider and target
infrastructure certification remain deployment-specific.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/first-workflow.md">Try your first workflow</a> for a credential-free
workflow-to-trace tour and an example of a plugin with a scoped tool allowlist.</p>
<p dir="auto">Model execution is live and fail-closed by default, including the built-in planner and writer when routing is disabled. Deterministic offline fixtures are an explicit test/demo mode enabled with <code>DISPATCH_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=true</code>; live SDK integration requires AI SDK plus provider credentials.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Dispatch</h2><a id="user-content-why-dispatch" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Dispatch" href="#why-dispatch"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Single-step chat calls are rarely enough when work needs to be repeated, reviewed, and resumed. Dispatch provides:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Declarative workflow steps and agent roles</li>
<li>Deterministic tool orchestration</li>
<li>Retry policies and failure semantics</li>
<li>Optional deterministic or random jitter in retry backoff</li>
<li>Human-in-the-loop approval controls</li>
<li>Persisted, resumable run state</li>
<li>Structured report outputs and trace artifacts</li>
<li>Deterministic, policy-driven agent and model routing with persisted decisions</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Key Capabilities</h2><a id="user-content-key-capabilities" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Key Capabilities" href="#key-capabilities"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Workflow schema with typed step metadata</li>
<li>Step lifecycle tracking (pending, running, paused, completed, failed, skipped)</li>
<li>Optional steps that skip-and-continue on failure or policy denial</li>
<li>Step input/output schema validation with actionable errors</li>
<li>Hard model/retry deadlines plus fail-closed admission for reviewed bounded in-process tools</li>
<li>Lifecycle event hooks via callback and webhook sink outputs (<code>--webhook-sink</code>)</li>
<li>Approval decisions (approved, rejected, request_changes)</li>
<li>DAG-style step dependencies (<code>depends_on</code>) with dependency-ordered scheduling and bounded concurrent execution for explicitly idempotent <code>parallel_safe</code> tool steps</li>
<li>Agent-to-agent handoff events</li>
<li>Run cataloging and filtering (<code>runs --status</code>, <code>--topic</code>, <code>--issues-only</code>, <code>--json</code>)</li>
<li>Lossless, tombstone-based catalog cleanup with safe dry-run/apply modes (<code>cleanup</code>); physical artifact retention remains operator-managed</li>
<li>Workflow template selection by ID (<code>demo/resume --workflow <template-id></code>)</li>
<li>Health diagnostics and repair (<code>doctor</code>, <code>doctor --write</code>)</li>
<li>Report generation (<code>report.md</code>, <code>report.json</code>)</li>
<li>Trace generation (<code>trace.json</code>, <code>trace.md</code>)</li>
<li>Provider-neutral human-intervention events and validated <code>resume-decision</code>
bridge handoff for Leash ChatOps routing</li>
<li>Producer-neutral evaluation results, workflow policy mapping, durable control
boundaries, and revision-bound intervention decisions</li>
<li>Quality-first route selection with hard policy constraints, explicit fallback limits,
resumable route evidence, and structured <code>no_route_available</code> failures</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Architecture and extension diagrams:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>docs/architecture-and-extension-diagrams.md</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Core modules:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>dispatch.kujo</code>: CLI entrypoint and command routing</li>
<li><code>src/cli/cli_args.kujo</code>: schema-driven CLI argument parsing</li>
<li><code>src/cli/bundled_workflow.kujo</code>: strict configuration paths and installed example allowlist</li>
<li><code>src/workflows/workflow.kujo</code>: workflow templates and template registry</li>
<li><code>src/workflows/loader.kujo</code>: declarative JSON workflow spec loader (<code>--workflow-file</code>)</li>
<li><code>src/plugins/builtin_plugins.kujo</code>: built-in plugin registry applied via <code>--plugin</code></li>
<li><code>src/cli/output.kujo</code>: CLI output, version, and contract-metadata helpers</li>
<li><code>src/core/runner.kujo</code>: orchestration engine entrypoint</li>
<li><code>src/core/control.kujo</code>: portable result validation and workflow policy mapping</li>
<li><code>src/core/control_journal.kujo</code>: append-only hash-linked control event journal</li>
<li><code>src/core/intervention.kujo</code>: revision-bound continuation validation and retry safety</li>
<li><code>src/core/routing.kujo</code>: deterministic route filtering, ranking, evaluation, and fallback policy</li>
<li><code>src/agents/agent.kujo</code>: agent execution entrypoint and handler registry mapping</li>
<li><code>src/tools/tool.kujo</code>: tool registry, payload adapters, and tool invocation entrypoint</li>
<li><code>src/tools/source_lookup.kujo</code>: source search and lookup handlers</li>
<li><code>src/tools/content_processing.kujo</code>: claim/citation/report/timestamp handlers</li>
<li><code>src/tools/reliability_tools.kujo</code>: reliability simulation handlers</li>
<li><code>src/core/approval.kujo</code>: approval request/decision handling</li>
<li><code>src/core/retry.kujo</code>: retry policies and attempt tracking</li>
<li><code>src/core/state.kujo</code>: run persistence, summaries, filtering, diagnostics</li>
<li><code>src/core/trace.kujo</code>: trace event model and markdown rendering</li>
<li><code>src/core/hooks.kujo</code>: lifecycle event hook callback and webhook sink emission</li>
<li><code>src/core/report.kujo</code>: report payload and artifact writing</li>
<li><code>src/core/tool_policy.kujo</code>: centralized tool authorization policy parsing and builder</li>
<li><code>src/core/plugins.kujo</code>: plugin registration and runtime injection for external tools/agents</li>
<li><code>src/bridge/sdk_adapter.kujo</code>: external AI SDK bridge invocation</li>
<li><code>src/bridge/bridge_chat.kujo</code>: Kujo bridge script executed with <code>AI_SDK_PATH</code> as the working directory</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Module layout:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>All implementation modules live under <code>src/</code>, including the tool handler layer (<code>src/tools/</code>).</li>
<li><code>dispatch.kujo</code> stays at the root as the CLI/package entrypoint; the bridge implementation lives in <code>src/bridge/</code>.</li>
<li>New development should target <code>src/</code> modules directly.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">External AI SDK Integration (AI Chat Style)</h2><a id="user-content-external-ai-sdk-integration-ai-chat-style" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: External AI SDK Integration (AI Chat Style)" href="#external-ai-sdk-integration-ai-chat-style"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch uses the same pattern as <code>ai-chat</code>:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Dispatch does not vendor <code>ai_sdk.kujo</code> or <code>providers.kujo</code>.</li>
<li><code>src/bridge/sdk_adapter.kujo</code> invokes the <code>src/bridge/bridge_chat.kujo</code> bridge process.</li>
<li>The bridge runs with <code>AI_SDK_PATH</code> as module root and imports shared SDK modules from that external project.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">This keeps SDK behavior centralized in one repository (<code>ai-sdk</code>) while allowing Dispatch to remain lightweight.</p>
<p dir="auto">The bridge forwards AI SDK structured-output controls (<code>response_format</code>, <code>structured_output_schema</code>, and <code>structured_output_retryable</code>) when callers provide them. This keeps JSON-mode and schema validation policy in the SDK instead of reimplementing it in Dispatch.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Deterministic Agent And Model Routing</h2><a id="user-content-deterministic-agent-and-model-routing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Deterministic Agent And Model Routing" href="#deterministic-agent-and-model-routing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">For a complete setup, policy, live-provider, inspection, and troubleshooting guide,
see <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/HOWTO.md"><code>HOWTO.md</code></a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">For a shareable introduction to the feature, its architecture, and installation
boundaries, see <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/BLOG_ROUTER.md"><code>BLOG_ROUTER.md</code></a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Routing is opt-in. Workflows without <code>routing.enabled: true</code> retain their configured
agent and model exactly. An enabled workflow supplies a versioned AI SDK model
catalog, workflow defaults, and optional step constraints. Dispatch validates the
catalog hash, rejects candidates that violate hard constraints, and applies a
stable quality-first ordering to the remainder. It persists the complete decision,
candidate rejections, attempts, catalog provenance, and evaluation outcome before
the model call.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch owns policy and run decisions. AI SDK owns provider/model catalog metadata.
Agents SDK defines the compatible agent vocabulary (<code>handler_id</code>, versioned
<code>execution_contract</code>, capabilities, model candidates, and risk metadata). Agent
substitution is permitted only when enabled and handler-compatible or when the
execution contracts match exactly.</p>
<p dir="auto">Broader policy cannot be weakened by an agent or step. Allowlists intersect,
requirements and denylists accumulate, minimums increase, and maximums decrease.
Unknown providers are rejected unless they are one of the explicit adapters:
<code>fixture</code>, <code>openai</code>, <code>openrouter</code>, <code>deepseek</code>, or configured <code>custom</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">See <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/control-boundaries.md"><code>docs/control-boundaries.md</code></a> for evaluation,
policy, evidence, review, resume, and effect-aware retry contracts.</p>
<p dir="auto">On resume, Dispatch reuses the persisted route. It will not silently reroute if the
catalog, model, agent, handler, execution contract, or plugin that supplied a route
is unavailable. Same-route retries remain distinct from bounded fallback to a new
route. Provider failures, evaluation failures, and fallback eligibility are
recorded as route lifecycle trace events.</p>
<p dir="auto">Run the offline example without credentials:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="DISPATCH_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=true kujo run dispatch.kujo demo "Routing review" \
  --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json \
  --yes --non-interactive"><pre>DISPATCH_OFFLINE_FIXTURE=true kujo run dispatch.kujo demo <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Routing review<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json \
  --yes --non-interactive</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The example is intentionally fixture-backed. <code>state.json</code>, <code>report.json</code>, the
<code>inspect --json</code> envelope, and the runner result metadata expose <code>route_decisions</code>
and <code>route_attempts</code>. Secrets and raw provider output remain subject to Dispatch's
existing artifact redaction policy.</p>
<p dir="auto">Validate configuration and explain the deterministic choice before execution:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="dispatch validate --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json
dispatch explain-route --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json"><pre>dispatch validate --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json
dispatch explain-route --workflow-file examples/workflows/routed-review.json --json</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Catalogs may be referenced with <code>routing.model_catalog_file</code>; Dispatch resolves
the path relative to the workflow and embeds the loaded catalog in persisted run
state. Declarative agents can use the built-in <code>handler_id: "model"</code> rather than
shipping custom runtime code. Evaluation outcome <code>request_human_review</code> uses the
native Dispatch pause/resume approval lifecycle.</p>

Supported help/version paths are checked for unexpected diagnostics.</p>

<p dir="auto">By default, Dispatch only allows fixture sources under <code>examples/research-report/sources</code> for demo/resume runs.</p>
<p dir="auto">By default, Dispatch also restricts <code>--output-root</code> to safe relative directories and blocks absolute/traversal-like paths unless <code>DISPATCH_ALLOW_ANY_OUTPUT_ROOT=true</code> is set explicitly.</p>
<p dir="auto">By default, Dispatch restricts <code>--config</code> to safe relative paths and enforces a maximum config size to reduce risky local path and oversized input scenarios.</p>

<p dir="auto">When strict mutation mode is enabled (<code>--strict-mutations</code> or <code>DISPATCH_STRICT_MUTATION_MODE=true</code>), <code>doctor --write</code>, <code>cleanup --apply</code>, and <code>import-run</code> are blocked unless <code>--confirm-mutation</code> is present or <code>DISPATCH_MUTATION_CONFIRM=true</code> is set.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>doctor</code> supports incremental scope via <code>--run-ids</code> (explicit run selection) and <code>--recent-count</code> (most recently updated runs only), which helps reduce scan latency on large catalogs.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>show --json</code>, <code>inspect --json</code>, and <code>doctor --json</code> emit consistent machine-readable envelopes with shared metadata keys (<code>command</code>, <code>ok</code>, and <code>output_root</code>) plus command-specific payload data.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>runs --json --diagnostics</code> includes index diagnostics metadata such as <code>index_fallback_count</code> and <code>index_rebuild_count</code> to surface catalog/index health quickly.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>demo --tags</code> stores normalized per-run metadata labels and <code>runs --tags</code> filters to runs that include all requested tags.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch is template-driven: <code>demo</code> and <code>resume</code> select workflows by template ID through <code>--workflow <template-id></code>. Direct Spec-file ingestion is not part of the verified command surface in this repository.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch supports <code>help</code>/<code>--help</code> and <code>version</code>/<code>--version</code>. The version is sourced from <code>kennel.toml</code> (<code>[package].version</code>).</p>
<p dir="auto">Steps can be marked <code>optional</code> in a workflow template. When an optional step fails (including a tool blocked by policy), Dispatch records a <code>step_skipped</code> trace event and continues the run instead of failing it. The built-in <code>retry_probe</code> step is optional, so the <code>research-report</code> and <code>crud-reliability</code> templates complete even when <code>flaky_reliability_tool</code> is denied (for example under the <code>staging</code>/<code>production</code> policy profiles).</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>demo</code> and <code>resume</code> accept lifecycle observability and control flags:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>--webhook-sink <path.jsonl></code> appends lifecycle events (one JSON object per line) to a local sink file. Absolute/traversal paths are blocked unless <code>DISPATCH_ALLOW_ANY_WEBHOOK_SINK=true</code>.</li>
<li><code>--webhook-url <https-url></code> records each signed envelope in the durable outbox before bounded delivery. Failed deliveries are dead-lettered and can be inspected or replayed with <code>dispatch webhooks status|replay</code>; webhook failure does not fail the workflow.</li>
<li><code>--cancel-after-step <step-id></code> cooperatively cancels the run after the named step completes, producing a <code>cancelled</code> lifecycle state.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Tool and agent steps can declare an <code>idempotency_key</code>; a successfully
checkpointed result is cached in run state and reused on resume. A process can
die after an external effect but before its checkpoint, so Dispatch provides
at-least-once replay in that window, not exactly-once effects. Tool handlers
receive a stable <code>context.effect_idempotency_key</code> (<code>run_id:step_id</code>) on retries
and resume; the external service must enforce it for consequential actions.</p>

<p dir="auto">Dispatch verifies bundle signatures by default during import. Use <code>--allow-unsigned-bundle</code> only for an explicitly trusted local development transfer; production imports must remain authenticated. Verification failures return deterministic <code>invalid_bundle_signature</code> errors.</p>
<p dir="auto">Signatures use standard HMAC-SHA256 (<code>hmac-sha256-v1</code>): each artifact is hashed, the per-artifact digests are bound to the run id, and the canonical message is authenticated with the shared key. Verification uses Kujo's constant-time HMAC tag verification. The signing key is required for both signing and verification.</p>
<p dir="auto">Bundles record a <code>key_id</code> (default <code>default</code>, or <code>DISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY_ID</code>/<code>--signing-key-id</code>). During a key rotation window, verification can trust multiple keys at once via <code>DISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEYS</code> (<code>id1=key1,id2=key2</code>): the verifier selects the key matching the bundle's <code>key_id</code>, falling back to the single signing key when no set entry matches.</p>
<p dir="auto">Prefer <code>DISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY</code> (env) over <code>--signing-key</code> (CLI flag) so the secret does not appear in process arguments or shell history.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>--signing-key</code> can be passed directly, but using <code>DISPATCH_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY</code> is recommended for non-interactive and managed environments.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Output Artifacts</h2><a id="user-content-output-artifacts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Output Artifacts" href="#output-artifacts"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Each run is written to:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="outputs/<run-id>/"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>outputs/<run-id>/
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Artifacts:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>state.json</code>: full run state snapshot</li>
<li><code>trace.json</code>: structured execution trace</li>
<li><code>trace.md</code>: human-readable trace timeline</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Watchdog integration uses <code>render_watchdog_native_events</code> from
<code>src/core/trace.kujo</code>. It projects run/workflow/task correlation and lifecycle
status into <code>watchdog.native-event.v1</code> while excluding messages, step payloads,
inputs, outputs, and paths. Dispatch remains the orchestrator and state owner;
the embedding host owns fail-open delivery and Watchdog owns privacy,
persistence, retention, and export.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>report.md</code>: human-readable report</li>
<li><code>report.json</code>: machine-readable report payload</li>
<li><code>dispatch-mutations.jsonl</code>: active mutation/policy audit log for <code>doctor --write</code>, <code>cleanup --apply</code>, bundle imports, and policy-denied tool attempts</li>
<li><code>dispatch-mutations.<slot>.jsonl</code>: rotated mutation audit backups controlled by <code>DISPATCH_MUTATION_AUDIT_MAX_BYTES</code> and <code>DISPATCH_MUTATION_AUDIT_MAX_BACKUPS</code></li>
<li><code>.dispatch-run-index.json</code>: run metadata index used for faster run listing/filtering</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">All run artifacts (<code>state.json</code>, <code>trace.json</code>, <code>trace.md</code>, <code>report.*</code>, the run index, and signed bundles) are written atomically: content is staged to a temporary file and renamed into place, so a crash or a concurrent reader never observes a partially written file. The run index (<code>.dispatch-run-index.json</code>) is a cache that can be rebuilt from per-run <code>state.json</code> files; <code>runs</code> and <code>doctor</code> fall back to scanning state when the index is missing or malformed. For strict isolation under heavy concurrency, use a dedicated <code>--output-root</code> per service.</p>
<p dir="auto">Protected assurance-aware state uses the guarded codec documented in <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/persisted-assurance-negotiation.md">persisted negotiation</a>; use the state loader instead of parsing its raw storage as JSON. Legacy state remains JSON. Contract metadata is embedded in persisted machine-readable artifacts: <code>state.json</code>, <code>trace.json</code>, and <code>report.json</code> include <code>artifact_contract_version</code>, <code>schema_name</code>, and <code>schema_version</code> fields to support schema-aware integrations and forward-compatible readers.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dispatch redacts sensitive fields (for example keys containing <code>api_key</code>, <code>token</code>, <code>authorization</code>, <code>secret</code>, <code>password</code>) before writing persisted artifacts.</p>
<p dir="auto">Policy-denied tool execution attempts are recorded in trace events (<code>policy_denied</code>) and mutation audit entries (<code>operation=policy_deny</code>) including run and command context.</p>
<p dir="auto">Tool policy can be sourced from a reusable profile alias (<code>--policy-profile</code>, <code>policy_profile</code>, <code>DISPATCH_POLICY_PROFILE</code>) plus explicit allow/deny controls. Explicit <code>allow_tools</code> and <code>deny_tools</code> override profile defaults when provided. CLI flags take precedence over config and environment values.</p>
<p dir="auto">Built-in policy profile aliases:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>dev</code> / <code>development</code>: no allow/deny restrictions (open profile)</li>
<li><code>staging</code>: deny <code>flaky_reliability_tool</code></li>
<li><code>prod</code> / <code>production</code>: allow <code>mock_web_search</code>, <code>local_source_lookup</code>, <code>claim_extraction</code>, <code>citation_formatter</code>, <code>markdown_report_writer</code>, <code>timestamp_tool</code>; deny <code>flaky_reliability_tool</code></li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Production execution controls</h2><a id="user-content-production-execution-controls" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Production execution controls" href="#production-execution-controls"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Workflow specifications can bound execution directly:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "max_parallel_steps": 4,
  "budgets": {
    "max_steps": 20,
    "max_total_tokens": 100000,
    "max_cost_usd": 10,
    "max_wall_time_ms": 900000
  }
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"max_parallel_steps"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">4</span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"budgets"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"max_steps"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">20</span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"max_total_tokens"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">100000</span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"max_cost_usd"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">10</span>,
    <span class="pl-ent">"max_wall_time_ms"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">900000</span>
  }
}</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Only tool steps marked <code>parallel_safe: true</code> are eligible for concurrent execution, and those steps must declare an <code>idempotency_key</code>. Dispatch uses <code>max_parallel_steps</code> as a hard concurrency bound and merges results in workflow order. Agent, approval, handoff, and report steps stay serialized so route persistence and human decisions remain deterministic.</p>
<p dir="auto">Set <code>agent.model_options.stream: true</code> to persist incremental model events to <code>stream-<step-id>.jsonl</code> in the run directory while the AI SDK bridge is active. The final normalized model response remains the step result. Streaming step IDs must not contain path separators.</p>
<p dir="auto">Run execution holds a process-owned POSIX advisory lock on <code>.dispatch-run.lock</code>.
The file is never unlinked, and the OS releases the handle when the worker exits;
lock age no longer grants ownership. Quiesce older workers before upgrading:
their age-based cleanup protocol does not coordinate with advisory locks. Run
directories on multiple hosts still need a distributed lock and storage layer.
State schema v1 artifacts migrate additively to schema v2 when loaded, with the
migration recorded in <code>state.json</code>. For a restart-sensitive single-host deployment,
use <code>DISPATCH_STATE_BACKEND=sqlite</code>; JSON artifacts remain human-readable mirrors
while SQLite is authoritative.</p>

<p dir="auto">Dispatch is designed to be extended safely and incrementally:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Add new workflow templates in <code>src/workflows/workflow.kujo</code></li>
<li>Add new tool handlers in <code>src/tools/</code> and register them in <code>src/tools/tool.kujo</code> with per-tool payload adapters instead of runner-specific branching</li>
<li>Register project-specific plugins via <code>src/core/plugins.kujo</code> to inject tools and agents without core edits</li>
<li>Extend decision policies in <code>src/core/approval.kujo</code> and <code>src/core/retry.kujo</code></li>
<li>Add reporting outputs in <code>src/core/report.kujo</code></li>
<li>Integrate observability sinks from trace events</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Language-aware documentation queries</h2><a id="user-content-language-aware-documentation-queries" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Language-aware documentation queries" href="#language-aware-documentation-queries"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The optional <code>rag</code> plugin retrieves source-cited documentation from a configured Kujo RAG server. <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/RETRIEVAL_PREFERENCES.md">Task preferences</a> select equivalent code examples upstream and persist across retries and approval resume. Use <code>examples/workflows/documentation-query.json</code> for a copyable workflow; no model-provider call is required by that workflow.</p>
<p dir="auto">An experimental <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/agents-sdk-ability.md">Agents SDK → Ability interoperability slice</a>
transports bounded evidence into the existing beta review/replay path. Dispatch
retains replay authority; standalone SDK tools remain independent.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental Wave D: <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/git-process-participant.md">controlled Workcell Git process interoperability</a> exercises a non-Ability effect with existing beta review/replay authority.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental Wave D <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/interop-handoff.md">interoperability correlation core</a>
retains SDK/MCP/HTTP/Workcell handoffs through explicit adapters. Correlation never
authorizes replay; existing persisted beta admission remains authoritative.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/packages/README.md">Experimental participant packages</a> provide unpublished npm
and Python artifacts for pure correlation/recording APIs. They contain no effect
executor, admission, assurance or replay authority.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Trusted localhost provider development</h3><a id="user-content-trusted-localhost-provider-development" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Trusted localhost provider development" href="#trusted-localhost-provider-development"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">An HTTP localhost custom provider requires an exact entry in
<code>DISPATCH_ALLOWED_CUSTOM_PROVIDER_ORIGINS</code>, plus both
<code>DISPATCH_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL_CUSTOM_PROVIDER=true</code> and
<code>KUJO_AI_SDK_ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCALHOST=true</code>. The normal subprocess bridge also
retains Kujo's private-network denial. Only a trusted development host may set
<code>KUJO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_DESTINATIONS=1</code> for that process to opt out of the
private-address guard. This runtime override broadens private-network access;
it is not a producer/model option and should not be enabled for untrusted routes.
The default remains deny-private. The release localhost fixture uses no real
provider credentials and does not certify a remote deployment.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental Wave C/D: <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/effect-set/one-effect-admission.md">one selected local effect</a>
adds locked selection and one-use admission for a verified not-started SQLite
effect. The assessor remains read-only; parent replay and automatic remainder
execution remain prohibited.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental follow-up: <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/effect-set/sequential-continuation.md">bounded sequential continuation</a>
adds explicit unconsumed renewal/abandonment and separately admitted next effects
using the same Dispatch control model over SQLite and Workcell Git. Validation
status and the one-profile-per-run boundary are recorded in that contract.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Retained-host reconciliation (experimental)</h3><a id="user-content-retained-host-reconciliation-experimental" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Retained-host reconciliation (experimental)" href="#retained-host-reconciliation-experimental"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>recover inspect</code> and <code>recover plan</code> explain surviving local control evidence.
<code>recover apply</code> requires an exact plan and local operator attribution, rechecks
sources under the run lock, and performs only proven mechanical repairs. It never
resumes execution. See the <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/recovery/retained-host.md">operator contract</a>
for supported publication gaps, immutable evidence, consumed-attempt protection,
unsupported recovery cases and the machine-readable output contract.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Experimental parent finalization</h3><a id="user-content-experimental-parent-finalization" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Experimental parent finalization" href="#experimental-parent-finalization"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Installed local controllers can separately assess and finalize the last unresolved
protected parent after verifying effects, outputs, evaluation and operator review.
See <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/parent-finalization/protocol.md">the bounded contract</a> and
<a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/parent-finalization/wave-f-crosswalk.md">Wave F crosswalk</a>.
Finalization does not schedule work, replay effects or change participant authority.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental sourced resource accounting and bounded Eval reservation planning are
documented in <a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/contracts/resources/protocol.md">the resource contract</a>. Existing
runtime/provider artifacts remain observations; Dispatch owns budget authority.</p>
<p dir="auto">For the experimental typed-output, review, Eval and budget path, see the
<a href="/kujolang/dispatch/blob/18b5c737a73904ae942f0bd1c3baa1f77c2bfb40/docs/operator-rehearsal.md">operator rehearsal</a>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Repository-backed, local-first workflow kits for the <a href="https://kujolang.ai" rel="nofollow">Kujo programming language</a> and its agency and AI tooling ecosystem. Each kit demonstrates one concrete outcome and leaves behind inspectable evidence instead of relying on an opaque hosted runner.</p>
<p dir="auto">Current release scope: <strong>locally verified support/distribution technical preview</strong> (<code>0.6.2</code>). Hosted runners, broad live-provider coverage, clean-machine installation on a separate host, and production or enterprise readiness are not claimed.</p>

<p dir="auto"><a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/webops-dashboard"><code>webops-dashboard/</code></a> is the local SQLite-backed reporting
surface for all ten WebOps workflows and the 28-role WebOps catalog. It imports

<p dir="auto"><a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/publishing-house-operator"><code>publishing-house-operator/</code></a> is the durable,
low-touch control loop above the eleven Publishing House workflow kits. It
adds portable publication and voice profiles, SourcePack intake, weekly/monthly/
campaign plans imported into StoryDesk, dependency-aware daily ticks, event
commissioning, exact-version approval routing, checkpoints, leases, exception
notifications, fixture verification, and cron/launchd templates. It reuses the
existing Publishing House tools and authority boundaries instead of creating a
second queue, approval store, evidence system, package system, or publisher.</p>

<p dir="auto">The <code>videoops-production</code> initializer packages an arbitrary request for the
VideoOps Producer and emits a prompt that can run in any file-capable agent
harness. Five specialist kits define the file-handoff production line:
creative planning, rights-aware asset resolution, explicit media generation,
HyperFrames editing, and independent critique. Their complete offline gate is
acceptance proof; it is not the content used by a real production.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why Use These Workflows?</h2><a id="user-content-why-use-these-workflows" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why Use These Workflows?" href="#why-use-these-workflows"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Start from bounded, runnable examples instead of assembling a multi-tool workflow from scratch.</li>
<li>Use fixture-first paths that are deterministic, local, and safe to evaluate without provider credentials.</li>
<li>Inspect evidence packets, receipts, reports, and handoffs produced by each workflow.</li>
<li>Keep host, provider, approval, and security boundaries explicit in both commands and documentation.</li>
<li>Adapt individual kits without adopting a hosted workflow service.</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install Publishing House locally</h3><a id="user-content-install-publishing-house-locally" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install Publishing House locally" href="#install-publishing-house-locally"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The eleven Publishing House kits have one locked, tested installation path.
Supply an existing Kujo 1.0.1 binary; the installer uses local sibling
checkouts when available and otherwise clones the exact commits in the install
lock:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="bash scripts/install-publishing-house.sh \
  --prefix "$PWD/.local/publishing-house" \
  --kujo-bin /absolute/path/to/kujo \
  --demo

.local/publishing-house/bin/publishing-house-doctor
.local/publishing-house/bin/publishing-house-demo \
  --out "$PWD/.local/publishing-house/runs/second-run""><pre>bash scripts/install-publishing-house.sh \
  --prefix <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$PWD</span>/.local/publishing-house<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --kujo-bin /absolute/path/to/kujo \
  --demo

.local/publishing-house/bin/publishing-house-doctor
.local/publishing-house/bin/publishing-house-demo \
  --out <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$PWD</span>/.local/publishing-house/runs/second-run<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The installer refuses an existing target, installs into a staging directory,
pins clean dependency checkouts, runs the Kujo-native contract doctor, and can
run the complete eleven-workflow offline proof before reporting success. It
does not install credentials or enable live publication.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Verification</h2><a id="user-content-verification" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Verification" href="#verification"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Run the portable release gates:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="python3 -m pip install jsonschema PyYAML
bash tests/release-readiness.sh
bash tests/clean-checkout.sh"><pre>python3 -m pip install jsonschema PyYAML

<p dir="auto">The first command validates release metadata, documentation links, catalog structure, contracts, tests, syntax, artifact-ignore coverage, and whitespace. The clean-checkout gate repeats the repository-owned checks from a temporary archive containing only tracked files.</p>
<p dir="auto">Catalog validation additionally resolves canonical skills and sibling tool repositories:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py \
  --skills-root "$KUJO_REPOS/kujo-skills" \

  --tools-root <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$KUJO_REPOS</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> \
  --json</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Host-dependent representative gates:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="bash workcell-execution-gate/scripts/run.sh
bash tribunal-decision-gate/scripts/run.sh

<p dir="auto">This repository is the MIT-licensed <code>0.6.2</code> technical preview of the Kujo workflow-kit distribution. The checkout covers 44 local workflows, including the Owned Agent Project proof, the eleven-workflow Publishing House lifecycle, the Publishing House Operator control layer, the VideoOps production initializer, and the five-stage VideoOps production line, plus shared contracts, documentation, versioned evidence contracts, and repository-owned validation gates. It does not publish a package, container image, hosted runner, or workflow service.</p>
<p dir="auto">For contribution, support, conduct, and vulnerability-reporting guidance, see <a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a>, <a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/SUPPORT.md">SUPPORT.md</a>, <a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md">CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md</a>, and <a href="/kujolang/kujo-workflows/blob/d766eae4fd9a131e51c34796d029fd3bc6974689/SECURITY.md">SECURITY.md</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Known Limits</h2><a id="user-content-known-limits" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Known Limits" href="#known-limits"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Some Kujo interpreter runs emit type-checking warnings before successful artifact output; workflow scripts use exit status plus expected artifacts as the contract.</li>
<li>Live providers, authenticated browser flows, external customer repositories, and hosted execution require separate credentials and approval.</li>
<li>Tribunal mock decisions are advisory and unsigned.</li>
<li>Relay proves local persistence and bounded retries, not remote exactly-once delivery.</li>
<li>Workcell is a trusted local Docker/Podman boundary, not a hosted scheduler or microVM isolation layer.</li>
<li>The locked Publishing House installer and all-eleven first run pass from a tracked archive on the development host; validation on a physically separate host remains open.</li>
</ul>

01 / Background

From the web
to languages and tools.

I’m Robert DeVore, a software engineer, security researcher, open-source developer, and technical writer. I’ve spent more than 20 years building commercial products, publishing systems, and tools that help people do their work.

I started with PHP, WordPress, and publishing systems. Building plugins led to commercial products, along with the maintenance, support, and integrations that customers relied on.

I’ve worked independently and with agencies on custom software, security audits, performance, and ongoing support. That work shaped how I approach architecture and technical leadership: a system has to make sense to the people who run it, change it, and inherit it.

Today I build programming languages, developer tools, and systems for AI-assisted engineering. Kujo brings that work together. I want people to understand how their software works, verify its behavior, and maintain it long after launch.

From the archive: agency work and independent development · building a long-lived product.

  1. Foundation

    The open web

    PHP, WordPress, publishing workflows, and software built around real users.

  2. Ownership

    Products & teams

    Commercial plugins, client systems, maintenance, and the decisions that outlast a release.

  3. Investigation

    Security research

    Tracing trust boundaries, reporting vulnerabilities responsibly, and learning from failure.

  4. Current work

    Languages & tools

    Kujo, local applications, and inspectable infrastructure for AI-assisted engineering.

02 / Security research

I don’t just build software.
I find where it breaks.

My research examines how software handles untrusted input, enforces permissions, and fails when those checks are missing.

My published disclosures cover WordPress plugins, from cross-site scripting to authorization failures. I report findings through coordinated disclosure programs so maintainers can address them and users have a public record to consult.

Language / Current focus

Kujo

A programming language and ecosystem for AI-native software. My work extends from the language and runtime into SDKs, agent workflows, package infrastructure, static publishing, evaluation, and developer tools.

These are connected engineering problems: defining what a program may do, making its state visible, and giving people a way to check the result.

05 / Engineering principles

Leave the system
easier to understand.

Make the boundaries explicit.
Know what an input can affect, which permissions an action needs, and where a person should stay in control.
Prefer evidence to assumptions.
Keep the inputs, checks, and results close enough that someone else can reproduce the work.
Choose clarity that lasts.
A smaller, understandable system is easier to secure and maintain. Documentation and useful errors belong in the design.
Build for the next person.
Good interfaces, open source, and honest handoffs help work remain useful after its original author moves on.

It is a pure adapter: it performs no network or database I/O, retains tool/server identity, timing, status, source correlation IDs, approval/risk classification, and input/output byte counts, and never accepts raw tool inputs or outputs. \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog_mcp_tool_lifecycle\u003c/code\u003e emits a stable start/completion pair and \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog_mcp_trace_metadata\u003c/code\u003e supplies bounded \u003ccode\u003e_meta\u003c/code\u003e propagation fields. The host owns fail-open delivery to Watchdog and should use one trace across the client request, server execution, and nested work while preserving source IDs as references. Propagated values are correlation only and must never select authorization, privacy, retention, tenant, or exporter policy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePortable Ability Projection\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-portable-ability-projection\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Portable Ability Projection\" href=\"#portable-ability-projection\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003esrc/abilities/projection.kujo\u003c/code\u003e uses the exact canonical \u003ccode\u003eability\u003c/code\u003e package\nrevision pinned by Kennel to validate a portable Ability and project it\ninto an MCP tool descriptor without turning MCP into the semantic source of\ntruth. Projection is opt-in (\u003ccode\u003eenabled: true\u003c/code\u003e), preserves input and output JSON\nSchemas plus canonical Ability identity and definition digest, and defaults to\nread-only effects. \u003ccode\u003eability_registry_to_mcp_tools\u003c/code\u003e projects every enabled\ncanonical \u003ccode\u003emcp\u003c/code\u003e exposure and rejects duplicate tool names.\nWrite, delete, and external effects require an explicit \u003ccode\u003eallowed_effects\u003c/code\u003e\nexposure policy. \u003ccode\u003esrc/abilities/gateway.kujo\u003c/code\u003e provides the executable bridge\nfor servers that own an Ability registry. It filters private discovery through\na server-supplied authorization callback, requires a server-resolved\nprincipal, constructs a canonical MCP invocation, delegates policy, approval,\nidempotency, and auditing to \u003ccode\u003eexecute_ability\u003c/code\u003e, and maps the terminal receipt\ninto an MCP tool result. Authentication, durable stores, and transport\nconfiguration remain application concerns and are never part of the Ability\ndefinition.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/integrations/kujo-ability\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eintegrations/kujo-ability\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e adds a tested STDIO\nbridge plus Codex plugin, Cursor, VS Code, and generic MCP configuration. It\nconnects to an application's authenticated Ability gateway; it does not turn\nthe public \u003ccode\u003emcp.kujolang.ai\u003c/code\u003e catalog into a privileged execution service.\nDeployment profiles and the enterprise control checklist are documented in\n\u003ca href=\"/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/docs/ability-host-deployment.md\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edocs/ability-host-deployment.md\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe canonical definition contract is maintained in and consumed directly from\n\u003ca href=\"https://github.com/kujolang/ability\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ekujolang/ability\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe repository-local \u003ccode\u003ekujo.mcp.core@1.0.0\u003c/code\u003e Ability Pack under \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/packs/mcp_core\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003epacks/mcp_core\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e provides two bounded read-only workflows: a redacted repository-profile summary and validation of one contained generated MCP manifest. It never executes discovered commands or returns sensitive path names. Host projection remains opt-in through the canonical Ability runtime. Applications inspecting a separate project can call \u003ccode\u003ecreate_mcp_core_ability_registry_for_project(source_root, project_root)\u003c/code\u003e: canonical definitions come from the trusted MCP source, while reads are bound to the selected project. The existing one-root constructor remains supported. Project selection is application configuration, never model-supplied authority.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" MCP server framework, demo implementation, and guarded repo-specific server generator. It is not a universal enterprise certification package by itself; remote production use still needs environment-specific review of auth, network ingress, secret custody, observability, and capacity limits.","","| Area | Current status |","|------|----------------|","| Local MCP server | Ready for local development and integration testing |","| File tools/resources | Guarded by configured roots,
