platform with SSO, centralized audit retention, distributed limits, or formal security certification |","","## Why Use This","","- Build MCP tools and resources directly in Kujo","- Start fast with a working server and demo workspace","- Ship safer defaults with path guards, request limits, and auth controls","- Scale from local development to reverse-proxy deployments","- Generate reviewable repo-specific MCP scaffolds that showcase Kujo's configuration, safety, and artifact-generation strengths","","## Who This Is For","","- Teams building MCP servers and agent tooling in Kujo","- Developers who want a practical starting point with deployment guardrails","- Projects that need secure file access patterns and configurable runtime controls","","## Who This Is Not For","","- Teams looking for a fully managed hosted MCP platform","- Workloads requiring built-in distributed/global rate limiting inside this service process","- Projects that cannot run a reverse proxy and external secret management for remote deployment","","## Highlights","","- Plugin-style tool/resource registration in dedicated modules","- Multi-root workspace support via `permissions.allowed_directories`","- Runtime endpoint gating via `tools.enabled` and `resources.enabled`","- Request guardrails with body-size and local or trusted-gateway rate limits","- Standard MCP initialize, ping, tools, resources, and prompts methods","- Bounded recursive traversal with explicit truncation metadata and optional caching","- Config-driven tool timeout controls","- Security and integration regression test suites","- Deployment baseline template included","- Explicit, effect-gated projection of portable `kujo.ability/v1` definitions into MCP tools","- Metadata-only Watchdog lifecycle helper for client/server tool correlation","","## Watchdog telemetry helper","","`src/telemetry/watchdog.kujo` maps MCP client or server tool lifecycles into the shared `watchdog.native-event.v1` ingestion contract. It is a pure adapter: it performs no network or database I/O, retains tool/server identity, timing, status, source correlation IDs, approval/risk classification, and input/output byte counts, and never accepts raw tool inputs or outputs. `watchdog_mcp_tool_lifecycle` emits a stable start/completion pair and `watchdog_mcp_trace_metadata` supplies bounded `_meta` propagation fields. The host owns fail-open delivery to Watchdog and should use one trace across the client request, server execution, and nested work while preserving source IDs as references. Propagated values are correlation only and must never select authorization, privacy, retention, tenant, or exporter policy.","","## Portable Ability Projection","","`src/abilities/projection.kujo` uses the exact canonical `ability` package","revision pinned by Kennel to validate a portable Ability and project it","into an MCP tool descriptor without turning MCP into the semantic source of","truth. Projection is opt-in (`enabled: true`), preserves input and output JSON","Schemas plus canonical Ability identity and definition digest, and defaults to","read-only effects. `ability_registry_to_mcp_tools` projects every enabled","canonical `mcp` exposure and rejects duplicate tool names.","Write, delete, and external effects require an explicit `allowed_effects`","exposure policy. `src/abilities/gateway.kujo` provides the executable bridge","for servers that own an Ability registry. It filters private discovery through","a server-supplied authorization callback, requires a server-resolved","principal, constructs a canonical MCP invocation, delegates policy, approval,","idempotency, and auditing to `execute_ability`, and maps the terminal receipt","into an MCP tool result. Authentication, durable stores, and transport","configuration remain application concerns and are never part of the Ability","definition.","","[`integrations/kujo-ability`](integrations/kujo-ability) adds a tested STDIO","bridge plus Codex plugin, Cursor, VS Code, and generic MCP configuration. It","connects to an application's authenticated Ability gateway; it does not turn","the public `mcp.kujolang.ai` catalog into a privileged execution service.","Deployment profiles and the enterprise control checklist are documented in","[`docs/ability-host-deployment.md`](docs/ability-host-deployment.md).","","The canonical definition contract is maintained in and consumed directly from","[`kujolang/ability`](https://github.com/kujolang/ability).","","The repository-local `kujo.mcp.core@1.0.0` Ability Pack under [`packs/mcp_core`](packs/mcp_core) provides two bounded read-only workflows: a redacted repository-profile summary and validation of one contained generated MCP manifest. It never executes discovered commands or returns sensitive path names. Host projection remains opt-in through the canonical Ability runtime. Applications inspecting a separate project can call `create_mcp_core_ability_registry_for_project(source_root, project_root)`: canonical definitions come from the trusted MCP source, while reads are bound to the selected project. The existing one-root constructor remains supported. Project selection is application configuration, never model-supplied authority.","","## Quick Start","","### Local Run","","```bash","bash scripts/run_server.sh","```","","Default endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:8931/mcp/v1`","","Expected health response shape:","","```json","{\"status\":\"ok\",\"server\":\"mcp-demo\",\"version\":\"1.3.3\"}","```","","If you want to run the binary directly, resolve the runtime path first:","","```bash","bash scripts/find_kujo_runtime.sh","```","","### Copilot MCP Config (stdio)","","```json","{","  \"mcpServers\": {","    \"mcp\": {","      \"type\": \"stdio\",","      \"command\": \"kujo-runtime\",","      \"args\": [\"run\", \"/path/to/mcp/server.kujo\"]","    }","  }","}","```","","The binary configured in `command` must be the Kujo language runtime binary that supports the `run` subcommand.","","Wrapper note: the Kujo runtime exposes `mcp` as a first-party command group (`kujo mcp`), so `kujo mcp make --help` documents the generation flow directly. <p dir="auto">Build MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers in <a href="https://github.com/kujolang/kujo">Kujo</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">This project gives you a local MCP server foundation with configurable tools/resources, bounded file operations, and documented guardrails for controlled remote deployments.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Readiness at a Glance</h2><a id="user-content-readiness-at-a-glance" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Readiness at a Glance" href="#readiness-at-a-glance"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>mcp</code> is ready to use as a local MCP server framework, demo implementation, and guarded repo-specific server generator. It is not a universal enterprise certification package by itself; remote production use still needs environment-specific review of auth, network ingress, secret custody, observability, and capacity limits.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Watchdog telemetry helper</h2><a id="user-content-watchdog-telemetry-helper" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Watchdog telemetry helper" href="#watchdog-telemetry-helper"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>src/telemetry/watchdog.kujo</code> maps MCP client or server tool lifecycles into the shared <code>watchdog.native-event.v1</code> ingestion contract. It is a pure adapter: it performs no network or database I/O, retains tool/server identity, timing, status, source correlation IDs, approval/risk classification, and input/output byte counts, and never accepts raw tool inputs or outputs. <code>watchdog_mcp_tool_lifecycle</code> emits a stable start/completion pair and <code>watchdog_mcp_trace_metadata</code> supplies bounded <code>_meta</code> propagation fields. The host owns fail-open delivery to Watchdog and should use one trace across the client request, server execution, and nested work while preserving source IDs as references. Propagated values are correlation only and must never select authorization, privacy, retention, tenant, or exporter policy.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Portable Ability Projection</h2><a id="user-content-portable-ability-projection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Portable Ability Projection" href="#portable-ability-projection"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>src/abilities/projection.kujo</code> uses the exact canonical <code>ability</code> package
revision pinned by Kennel to validate a portable Ability and project it
into an MCP tool descriptor without turning MCP into the semantic source of
truth. Projection is opt-in (<code>enabled: true</code>), preserves input and output JSON
Schemas plus canonical Ability identity and definition digest, and defaults to
read-only effects. <code>ability_registry_to_mcp_tools</code> projects every enabled
canonical <code>mcp</code> exposure and rejects duplicate tool names.
Write, delete, and external effects require an explicit <code>allowed_effects</code>
exposure policy. <code>src/abilities/gateway.kujo</code> provides the executable bridge
for servers that own an Ability registry. It filters private discovery through
a server-supplied authorization callback, requires a server-resolved
principal, constructs a canonical MCP invocation, delegates policy, approval,
idempotency, and auditing to <code>execute_ability</code>, and maps the terminal receipt
into an MCP tool result. Authentication, durable stores, and transport
configuration remain application concerns and are never part of the Ability
definition.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/integrations/kujo-ability"><code>integrations/kujo-ability</code></a> adds a tested STDIO
bridge plus Codex plugin, Cursor, VS Code, and generic MCP configuration. It
connects to an application's authenticated Ability gateway; it does not turn
the public <code>mcp.kujolang.ai</code> catalog into a privileged execution service.
Deployment profiles and the enterprise control checklist are documented in
<a href="/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/docs/ability-host-deployment.md"><code>docs/ability-host-deployment.md</code></a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">The canonical definition contract is maintained in and consumed directly from
<a href="https://github.com/kujolang/ability"><code>kujolang/ability</code></a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">The repository-local <code>kujo.mcp.core@1.0.0</code> Ability Pack under <a href="/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/packs/mcp_core"><code>packs/mcp_core</code></a> provides two bounded read-only workflows: a redacted repository-profile summary and validation of one contained generated MCP manifest. It never executes discovered commands or returns sensitive path names. Host projection remains opt-in through the canonical Ability runtime. Applications inspecting a separate project can call <code>create_mcp_core_ability_registry_for_project(source_root, project_root)</code>: canonical definitions come from the trusted MCP source, while reads are bound to the selected project. The existing one-root constructor remains supported. Project selection is application configuration, never model-supplied authority.</p>

<p dir="auto">Safety defaults in generated servers:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Read-only inspection tools are enabled.</li>
<li>Safe commands are allowlisted and fixed in <code>mcp.manifest.json</code>.</li>
<li>Arbitrary shell command input is not exposed.</li>
<li>Risky commands are marked blocked/review-required in artifacts.</li>
<li>Sensitive files are recorded by path only; secret values are not copied into generated outputs.</li>
<li>Generated resource reads are constrained to the analyzed repository, generated server directory, and artifact directory.</li>
<li>Generated POST endpoints enforce a bounded request body size.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">This repository is launch-honest as a local protocol-compatible MCP server foundation, repo-specific scaffold generator, and remote-deployment baseline. Production use still requires environment-specific validation, especially for auth, ingress, rate-limit, monitoring, backup, and incident-response settings described in <code>docs/production-deployment.md</code>, <code>docs/security-model.md</code>, and <code>ROADMAP.md</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">An experimental <a href="/kujolang/mcp/blob/77180a3a6c104f0c5b185cefa1f6d0835edb704b/docs/controlled-ability-stdio.md">controlled local STDIO Ability mode</a>

GitHub Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile

Move from repository questions to planned code changes and review in one continuous session with GitHub Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile.

In this article

  • How Copilot helps on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile
  • Key concepts for Copilot in the cloud
  • Access and availability
  • Starting with Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile
  • Ways to work with Copilot
  • Session history and remote control
  • Customize your experience
  • Copilot limitations and compatibility
  • The older experience
  • Further reading

On the GitHub website and GitHub Mobile, GitHub Copilot can answer questions about your repositories, plan and make changes, review pull requests, and automate repository tasks. You can ask questions and delegate work from a conversation, and use Copilot directly in your issue and pull request workflows.

With the new Copilot in the cloud experience, you can move between web or mobile and local clients (Copilot app, VS Code, or Copilot CLI), working with and steering Copilot in the same session.

Note

Starting October 28, 2026, the new Copilot in the cloud experience on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile is available to users with a paid Copilot plan, subject to applicable organization and enterprise policies. Users on Copilot Free plans will continue to use the old Copilot Chat experience.

This article explains both the newer Copilot in the cloud experience and the older Copilot cloud agent plus Copilot Chat experience. For a quick overview of what's changing, see Comparison of the two experiences.

How Copilot helps on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile

You can combine chat, agentic work, code review, and automations in your repository workflows.

For example, you might use chat to understand how a repository handles authentication, then ask Copilot to plan and add missing tests. Once the changes are in a pull request, you can request a review from Copilot. To maintain test coverage over time, you could set up an automation to check for missing tests each week and propose additions for you to review.

Key concepts for Copilot in the cloud

Copilot in the cloud allows for a continuous task flow. Copilot sessions that you start on in a cloud environment on GitHub can continue seamlessly across different clients, such as the GitHub Copilot app, your IDE, mobile, and CLI. Your work and context are preserved across these clients, meaning you can move from asking questions to agentic work to task completion, in the same conversation.

Client, session, and environment

There are three key components to understand in the task flow: the client, the session, and the environment.

To start an agent task, you interact with Copilot through a client or surface, such as the web interface, GitHub Copilot app, IDE, GitHub Mobile, or GitHub Copilot CLI.

A session is the conversation and activity associated with agentic work, including the prompts you provide and the responses generated by Copilot.

An environment is the place where the agent executes its work, such as a cloud sandbox, a GitHub Actions runner, or a remote custom environment.

For more information, see About cloud sandboxes for GitHub Copilot, About local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot, and GitHub Copilot in IDEs.

Session context

You can start a chat session with the following contexts automatically attached:

  • All repositories, owned by you or by an organization.
  • A specific file, issue, pull request.
  • A specific repository and branch.
  • A space.

You can attach context with the repository selector, the + menu, or @ mentions.

To let Copilot retrieve information from supported services during a task, use customizations such as Copilot connectors and personal custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

Session context is distinct from Copilot Memory, which builds a longer-term, persistent understanding of your repositories and preferences across sessions. For more information, see About GitHub Copilot Memory.

Sessions across surfaces

Choose a cloud sandbox when you want to continue a session across supported Copilot surfaces. You can start a cloud session on one surface and continue it on another.

Comparison of GitHub Actions-based sessions and cloud sandboxes

In Copilot in the cloud, you have three environment choices: Cloud (a cloud sandbox), GitHub Actions-based, and Remote (a connection to a custom environment).

Initial performance testing on GitHub indicates that sessions in cloud sandboxes completed execution faster on average than GitHub Actions-based sessions.

The following table compares GitHub Actions-based sessions and cloud sandbox-based sessions.

GitHub ActionsCloud sandbox
Session continuitySessions are only available on the GitHub website.Sessions can be shared and resumed across clients.
Repository scopingSessions require a repository. Changes are made only in the specific, single repository context.Sessions can span across repositories in one organization. Changes can be made across multiple repositories
Chat data retentionData is retained for 28 days.Data is retained for the life of the account.
Custom environmentsSupports GitHub Actions-specific custom compute, network and setup configuration, and self-hosted runners.Cloud sandboxes honor repository and organization firewall allowlists, but do not support custom compute, GitHub Actions-specific setup steps, or self-hosted runners.
Customizations and tool sharingSupports custom instructions, MCP servers, and content exclusions.Supports custom instructions, dotfiles personalization, repository and personal MCP servers, connectors, and content exclusions with a single configuration across all cloud sandboxes.
Why choose this environmentSuitable when you need repository-specific integrations, custom environments, or self-hosted runners.Suitable for cross-repository chat, quick access to AI models, and when custom compute or network configurations are not required in cloud sandboxes.

In the Copilot in the cloud experience, cloud and GitHub Actions compute draw on the same monthly GitHub account allowance, separate from AI credits. For details, see Billing for cloud and local sandboxes for GitHub Copilot.

Access and availability

Available Copilot features depend on your plan and organization policies. For setup guidance, see Set up Copilot. For usage allowances and costs, see GitHub Copilot billing and usage.

Repository owners and administrators can disable Copilot for particular repositories, even when your plan and policies otherwise allow you to use it. Organization and enterprise policies continue to apply. See Managing GitHub Copilot in the cloud for your enterprise or organization.

To view organization data or sessions, you must meet your organization's single sign-on requirements.

Without write access to a repository, your Copilot session is read-only.

Starting with Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile

You can start working with Copilot from several different entry points:

  • Your Copilot home page at github.com/copilot
  • The Copilot panel, displayed when starting a session within a file, issue, or pull request
  • Your GitHub dashboard at github.com
  • The Agents tab or panel within a repository

Ways to work with Copilot

You can work with Copilot in several ways:

Asking questions

Chat can explain unfamiliar code, suggest fixes, generate tests, or compare approaches. Follow-up questions let you refine your request without starting a new conversation.

Chat is preconfigured with tools for tasks such as creating branches, updating files, and creating or updating issues. It also supports semantic code search, limited to default branches only.

Agentic work

Copilot can research a repository, plan changes, and implement them in the background. It can edit files and run tests and linters in a cloud development environment, rather than your local IDE.

When you ask for changes, Copilot works against the repository and branch you provided. You can review the proposed changes and ask for refinements before creating a pull request, or request a pull request in your prompt.

From security campaigns, you can assign code scanning alerts to Copilot for fixes. See Fixing alerts in a security campaign.

Code review

On GitHub, Copilot code review reviews pull request changes, identifies potential issues, and suggests fixes. It uses agentic capabilities to gather context from your repository. You can request a review or configure automatic reviews, then review and apply the suggested changes. See GitHub Copilot code review.

Copilot can also generate a summary of your changes directly in a pull request description or comment. This helps reviewers understand the changes, but is separate from reviewing the code. See Creating a pull request summary with GitHub Copilot.

Getting pull requests ready to merge

With Agent Merge, Copilot watches a pull request and works on the blockers you select: failed GitHub Actions workflows, merge conflicts, or both. Enable it with Watch and fix in the pull request's merge box. You can also enable it automatically for pull requests you create. See Getting pull requests ready to merge with Agent Merge.

Automations and agentic workflows

Automations let you define a task once and have Copilot run it on a schedule or in response to repository events. For example, an automation can triage issues or prepare weekly release notes. You create and manage automations from the Agents tab in a repository on GitHub.com. Automations are available in eligible private and internal repositories. See Copilot automations.

GitHub Agentic Workflows provide another way to automate tasks in your repositories on GitHub.com. You define tasks in natural language in Markdown files, and they run as GitHub Actions workflows. These workflows can use Copilot or another supported coding agent. See GitHub Agentic Workflows.

Session history and remote control

On GitHub, session logs show the work and tools used. Shared sessions and pull requests let teammates with repository access follow the work and review changes. Logs do not replace your own review and testing. See Managing agent sessions.

To monitor and steer a session started from GitHub Copilot CLI, enable remote control. The session continues running on your original local machine, which must stay online. See Remote control of GitHub Copilot CLI sessions.

You can ask Copilot about your synced session history across Copilot surfaces. This includes Copilot in the cloud and Copilot code review sessions, and sessions from GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and the GitHub Copilot app.

You can only query sessions you started. Syncing must be enabled and permitted by your organization's policies. See Query past sessions.

Customize your experience

There are several ways to customize your experience with Copilot.

Instructions, tools, and shared context

On GitHub, custom instructions let you save personal preferences for chat, repository conventions, and organization guidance.

Copilot Spaces organize shared context for questions.

For delegated work, custom agents and agent skills provide task-specific instructions and resources. MCP servers connect agents to additional tools and data.

Hooks can run commands during agent work for validation or logging. For setup guidance, see Customize Copilot.

Customizations for Copilot in the cloud

In cloud sandboxes, you can also use a dotfiles repository to bring your personal instructions, skills, and custom agents to your sessions across repositories. This dotfiles personalization does not apply to GitHub Actions-based sessions. For setup guidance, see Personalizing your cloud sessions.

To bring tools and context into Copilot, you can access third-party services through GitHub connectors. Connectors are available to all your Copilot in the cloud sessions. You can also configure personal MCP server configurations to allow Copilot access to your personal tools and context. These customizations do not apply to GitHub Actions-based sessions. See Copilot connectors and Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Some existing Spaces that include data from multiple organizations or mix private and organization data may not work the same way in Copilot in the cloud. For steps to restore chat use in Spaces containing incompatible private sources, see Creating GitHub Copilot Spaces.

AI models

You can change the model Copilot uses to generate responses. You may find that different models perform better, or provide more useful responses, depending on the type of questions you ask. Options include premium models with advanced capabilities. To change the model in your IDE, see Changing the AI model for GitHub Copilot Chat. To change or compare models on GitHub, see Asking GitHub Copilot questions in GitHub.

On GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile, available models depend on your plan and account policies. See Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot.

For Copilot in the cloud, the ability to select a model also depends on how you start the task. See Changing the AI model for GitHub Copilot cloud agent.

Copilot limitations and compatibility

Copilot can produce incorrect or suboptimal code, including code that contains security vulnerabilities. Review and test the output before using it in production. See Application card: GitHub Copilot Agents.

For information about built-in security protections, see Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent.

Copilot work limitations

  • Repository scope: When Copilot runs on GitHub Actions, Copilot can only make changes in the repository specified when you start a task. It cannot make changes across multiple repositories in one run. However, sessions that run in a cloud sandbox can work across multiple repositories.
  • Context access: In GitHub Actions-based sessions, the GitHub MCP server only provides access by default to context in the repository where the agent is working, such as issues and previous pull requests. You can configure broader access through repository MCP settings. See Configure MCP servers for your repository. For sessions in cloud sandboxes, you can give additional context by configuring access to third-party services through GitHub connectors and personal custom MCP servers, see Copilot connectors and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
  • Branches and pull requests: In GitHub Actions-based sessions and cloud sandbox sessions, Copilot can only work on one branch at a time and can open one pull request per task.
  • Session duration: Each Copilot session that runs on GitHub Actions has a maximum execution time of 59 minutes. This limit cannot be extended or bypassed. If a task exceeds the limit, the session stops. For environment configuration details, see Configure the development environment for agents on GitHub Actions.

Repository compatibility

  • Repository rules: A ruleset or branch protection rule can prevent Copilot from creating or updating pull requests. Repository administrators can configure a ruleset bypass for Copilot. See Creating rulesets for a repository.
  • Repository hosting: Copilot only works with repositories hosted on GitHub. It cannot work on repositories stored on other code hosting platforms.

The older experience

The newer Copilot in the cloud experience differs from the older Copilot cloud agent plus Copilot Chat experience in several key aspects, including default environments, policies, what session choices are available. Session context and customizations also differ.

Comparison of the two experiences

Copilot cloud agent plus Copilot Chat experienceCopilot in the cloud
Default environmentAll web entry points for agents, including a repository's Agents tab, default to an GitHub Actions-based environment.Cloud is the default where an environment choice is offered. Defaults can vary by workflow, so check the selected environment before starting.
PoliciesSeparate policies for Copilot features such as cloud agent and Copilot Chat in GitHub.A single organization and enterprise policy for Copilot in the cloud on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile.
Session choiceChat conversations and delegated cloud agent tasks are separate sessions. Agent tasks started from Copilot Chat run in an GitHub Actions-based environment.You can choose where the chat and agent session runs, either in a cloud sandbox or an GitHub Actions-based environment.

Session context

You can start a chat session with the following contexts automatically attached:

  • A specific file, issue, pull request.
  • A specific repository and branch.

You cannot start a chat session with multiple repositories automatically attached.

To start a conversation with the context of multiple repositories, manually select repositories owned by you or by an organization with repository selector.

You can attach other session context with the + menu, or @ mentions.

When starting a session from Copilot Chat, you can't choose an environment; your session runs on GitHub Actions automatically.

Sessions across surfaces

Some context, permissions, and configuration can carry between surfaces. The settings and context that apply depend on the Copilot feature and the surface you use.

Customizations

Custom instructions let you save personal preferences for chat, repository conventions, and organization guidance.

Copilot Spaces organize shared context for questions.

For delegated work, custom agents and agent skills provide task-specific instructions and resources. Repository MCP servers connect agents to additional tools and data.

Hooks can run commands during agent work for validation or logging.

Kujo","","[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.9.0-black)](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1_9_0.md)","[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)](LICENSE)","[![built with Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-white.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)","","Kujo is a programming language for local-first automation, AI-native software,","and practical application scripting. The runtime is written in Rust. `kujo run`","uses the bytecode VM by default; a tree-walking interpreter remains available for","compatibility and debugging.","","## Install","","On macOS or Linux, the Kujo installer sets up the current runtime and the core","Kujo toolset in user-owned directories:","","```bash","curl -fsSL https://kujolang.ai/install.sh | KUJO_RELEASE_VERSION=v1.9.0 bash","export PATH=\"$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH\"","kujo --version","```","","The default install includes Kujo, Kennel, and the core tools used for packages,","task specs, context, tests, and run records. See [Installation](INSTALLATION.md)","for a runtime-only npm install, Windows steps, source builds, profiles, updates,","and uninstall instructions.","","Concurrency behavior and validation for the current development branch are","recorded in [the runtime completion record](docs/RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY_COMPLETION.md).","Async tasks are bounded, generator aliases share progress, and detached work has","no implicit process-exit join.","","## Run your first program","","Create `hello.kujo`:","","```kujo","func greet(name) {","    print(\"Hello, \" + name + \"!\")","}","","greet(\"Kujo\")","```","","Then check and run it:","","```bash","kujo check hello.kujo","kujo run hello.kujo","```","","## Add packages with Kennel","","[Kennel](https://kennel.kujolang.ai/) is Kujo's package manager and official","package registry. Public package reads need no account. Install the current","Kennel client on macOS or Linux after installing Kujo 1.4.0 or newer:","","```bash","curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh","sh install.sh",". \"$HOME/.kennel/env\"","kennel --version","```","","Add a project dependency:","","```bash","kennel init --name my-project","kennel add ability","kennel install","```","","Or install a command you can use from any directory:","","```bash","kennel tool install shipcheck","shipcheck --help","```","","Kennel writes `kennel.toml` and `kennel.lock`. Kujo also has a smaller built-in","`kujo.toml` / `kujo.lock` workflow. The formats serve different jobs and are not","interchangeable. Read [Packages with Kennel](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/packages/)","before choosing one.","","## What Kujo includes","","- A VM-first runtime with functions, modules, collections, structs, enums,","  pattern matching, exceptions, async work, and generator support with documented","  VM/interpreter limits.","- Native filesystem, process, network, HTTP, crypto, database, and data helpers.","- Deterministic AI request hashes, record/replay cassettes, streaming callbacks,","  multimodal messages, token estimates, secret redaction, JSON Schema validation,","  and vector math.","- A formatter, linter, test runner, LSP, documentation generator, static server,","  benchmarks, diagnostics, and stable machine-readable output contracts.","- Capability controls for scripts that should not receive ambient host access.","","Core AI-native runtime mechanisms are implemented for deterministic request hashing, offline record/replay cassettes, structured response metadata, JSON Schema validation, vector math, token budgeting, runtime secret redaction, dedicated AI egress capability controls, streaming callbacks, and multimodal message builders.","","Dotted module import workflows are supported on the default VM path. Package","workflows are deterministic: `kujo init`, `kujo package-add`, `kujo package-install`, and `kujo package-install --frozen` work with nested source layouts and reproducible `kujo.lock` snapshots.","","## Everyday commands","","```bash","kujo run app.kujo                 # run on the VM","kujo check app.kujo               # validate without running","kujo format --write app.kujo      # format in place","kujo lint app.kujo                # find common problems","kujo test                         # run snapshot fixtures","kujo test-run tests.kujo          # run test declarations","kujo doctor --json                # inspect the environment","kujo mcp make [dir]               # generate a repo-specific MCP server","kujo serve [dir]                  # preview a static directory","kujo lsp                          # start the language server","```","","Use `--` before script arguments that could be mistaken for Kujo options:","","```bash","kujo run tool.kujo -- --help","```","","## Safety Model Snapshot","","Kujo is not a sandbox. A normal `kujo run` is trusted and can use host-effect","APIs. For code you do not trust, start with `--untrusted` and grant only the","capabilities it needs:","","```bash","kujo run --untrusted --allow-fs-read report.kujo","kujo run --untrusted --allow-ai agent.kujo","```","","Use `--deny-private-net` when network clients must reject local, private,","link-local, multicast, and unspecified destinations. For AI-only access, prefer","`--allow-ai` to broad network access and set `KUJO_AI_ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS` to the","provider URLs the script may call.","","Read [Secure AI scripting](docs/SECURE_AI_SCRIPTING.md) and the","[native API security posture](docs/NATIVE_API_SECURITY_POSTURE.md) before running","untrusted code on a shared or sensitive machine.","","## AI-Native Runtime Snapshot","","Kujo keeps deterministic mechanisms in the runtime and leaves provider routing,","RAG policy, agent frameworks, and observability to packages.","","- `ai_chat`, `ai_stream_chat`, `ai_embedding`, and `ai_tool_loop` share replay,","  response, and error contracts.","- `ai_request_hash` creates credential-free cache and cassette keys.","- `ai_text`, `ai_image_url`, and `ai_message` build portable messages.","- `ai_count_tokens` and `ai_fit_context` provide deterministic estimates.","- `secret`, `reveal`, and `is_secret` keep values redacted until code reveals them.","","Run the replay example without live provider credentials:","","```bash","KUJO_AI_REPLAY=tests/fixtures/ai_cassettes \\","KUJO_AI_REPLAY_MODE=strict \\","cargo run -- run examples/ai_enterprise_replay_showcase.kujo","```","","The short and full verification commands are:","","```bash","bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --minimal","bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --full","```","","See [AI runtime](docs/AI_RUNTIME.md) and the","[standard library](docs/STANDARD_LIBRARY.md) for the complete contracts.","","## Runtime Mode Recommendations","","- Use `kujo run \u003cfile\u003e` for normal work. Developers should not need `--interpreter` for ordinary modular project layouts.","- Use `--interpreter` to isolate a compatibility or runtime-path problem.","- Treat `--jit` as experimental. Unsupported bytecode falls back to the VM.","- Use `kujo package-install --frozen` to check `kujo.toml` and `kujo.lock`","  without changing either file.","- `kujo package-publish`: preview package publish metadata only. It does not","  publish to Kennel. Kennel owns registry installation and distribution.","","See the [VM/interpreter migration playbook](docs/VM_INTERPRETER_MIGRATION_PLAYBOOK.md).","","## 1.0 Release Status","","Release boundary: Kujo `v1.9.0` is the current stable release; explicit deferrals and compatibility guarantees are governed by `docs/V1_SCOPE.md`.","","- Kujo 1.9.0 is released for Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64 and Windows x64; see [release notes](docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1_9_0.md).","- The source tree is currently at `1.9.0` in `Cargo.toml`; the latest published stable release tag is `v1.9.0`.","- The signed release, native/source archives, checksums, and all six npm packages","  passed their published-install verification matrices.","- Prebuilt Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, and Windows x64 binaries ship with","  SHA-256 checksums.","- Kujo v1.0 package scope was local manifest and lockfile determinism only; it","  did not include a public Kennel registry or package publish transport. That","  describes the historical 1.0 runtime boundary. The separate Kennel registry is","  now live at [kennel.kujolang.ai](https://kennel.kujolang.ai/).","- The v1.0 launch record remains in","  [the completed release checklist](docs/V1_0_OFFICIAL_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md).","","## Build and test from source","","Kujo requires Rust 1.89 or newer:","","```bash","git clone https://github.com/kujolang/kujo.git","cd kujo","cargo build --release","cargo test","cargo run -- test --runtime vm","cargo run -- test --runtime dual","```","","This first-ten-minutes path gives you a normal script, a replay-only AI example,","and a least-privilege execution example. <p dir="auto">Kujo is a programming language for local-first automation, AI-native software,
and practical application scripting. The runtime is written in Rust. <code>kujo run</code>
uses the bytecode VM by default; a tree-walking interpreter remains available for
compatibility and debugging.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">On macOS or Linux, the Kujo installer sets up the current runtime and the core
Kujo toolset in user-owned directories:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -fsSL https://kujolang.ai/install.sh | KUJO_RELEASE_VERSION=v1.9.0 bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
kujo --version"><pre>curl -fsSL https://kujolang.ai/install.sh <span class="pl-k">|</span> KUJO_RELEASE_VERSION=v1.9.0 bash
<span class="pl-k">export</span> PATH=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.local/bin:<span class="pl-smi">$PATH</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
kujo --version</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The default install includes Kujo, Kennel, and the core tools used for packages,
task specs, context, tests, and run records. See <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/INSTALLATION.md">Installation</a>
for a runtime-only npm install, Windows steps, source builds, profiles, updates,
and uninstall instructions.</p>
<p dir="auto">Concurrency behavior and validation for the current development branch are
recorded in <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY_COMPLETION.md">the runtime completion record</a>.
Async tasks are bounded, generator aliases share progress, and detached work has
no implicit process-exit join.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Run your first program</h2><a id="user-content-run-your-first-program" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Run your first program" href="#run-your-first-program"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Create <code>hello.kujo</code>:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="func greet(name) {
    print("Hello, " + name + "!")
}

greet("Kujo")"><pre lang="kujo" class="notranslate"><code>func greet(name) {
    print("Hello, " + name + "!")
}

greet("Kujo")
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Then check and run it:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo check hello.kujo
kujo run hello.kujo"><pre>kujo check hello.kujo
kujo run hello.kujo</pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Add packages with Kennel</h2><a id="user-content-add-packages-with-kennel" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Add packages with Kennel" href="#add-packages-with-kennel"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://kennel.kujolang.ai/" rel="nofollow">Kennel</a> is Kujo's package manager and official
package registry. Public package reads need no account. Install the current
Kennel client on macOS or Linux after installing Kujo 1.4.0 or newer:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh
sh install.sh
. "$HOME/.kennel/env"
kennel --version"><pre>curl -fsSLO https://kennel.kujolang.ai/install.sh
sh install.sh
<span class="pl-c1">.</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.kennel/env<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
kennel --version</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Add a project dependency:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kennel init --name my-project
kennel add ability
kennel install"><pre>kennel init --name my-project
kennel add ability
kennel install</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Or install a command you can use from any directory:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kennel tool install shipcheck
shipcheck --help"><pre>kennel tool install shipcheck
shipcheck --help</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Kennel writes <code>kennel.toml</code> and <code>kennel.lock</code>. Kujo also has a smaller built-in
<code>kujo.toml</code> / <code>kujo.lock</code> workflow. The formats serve different jobs and are not
interchangeable. Read <a href="https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/packages/" rel="nofollow">Packages with Kennel</a>
before choosing one.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What Kujo includes</h2><a id="user-content-what-kujo-includes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What Kujo includes" href="#what-kujo-includes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>A VM-first runtime with functions, modules, collections, structs, enums,
pattern matching, exceptions, async work, and generator support with documented
VM/interpreter limits.</li>
<li>Native filesystem, process, network, HTTP, crypto, database, and data helpers.</li>
<li>Deterministic AI request hashes, record/replay cassettes, streaming callbacks,
multimodal messages, token estimates, secret redaction, JSON Schema validation,
and vector math.</li>
<li>A formatter, linter, test runner, LSP, documentation generator, static server,
benchmarks, diagnostics, and stable machine-readable output contracts.</li>
<li>Capability controls for scripts that should not receive ambient host access.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Core AI-native runtime mechanisms are implemented for deterministic request hashing, offline record/replay cassettes, structured response metadata, JSON Schema validation, vector math, token budgeting, runtime secret redaction, dedicated AI egress capability controls, streaming callbacks, and multimodal message builders.</p>
<p dir="auto">Dotted module import workflows are supported on the default VM path. Package
workflows are deterministic: <code>kujo init</code>, <code>kujo package-add</code>, <code>kujo package-install</code>, and <code>kujo package-install --frozen</code> work with nested source layouts and reproducible <code>kujo.lock</code> snapshots.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Safety Model Snapshot</h2><a id="user-content-safety-model-snapshot" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Safety Model Snapshot" href="#safety-model-snapshot"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Kujo is not a sandbox. A normal <code>kujo run</code> is trusted and can use host-effect
APIs. For code you do not trust, start with <code>--untrusted</code> and grant only the
capabilities it needs:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run --untrusted --allow-fs-read report.kujo
kujo run --untrusted --allow-ai agent.kujo"><pre>kujo run --untrusted --allow-fs-read report.kujo
kujo run --untrusted --allow-ai agent.kujo</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Use <code>--deny-private-net</code> when network clients must reject local, private,
link-local, multicast, and unspecified destinations. For AI-only access, prefer
<code>--allow-ai</code> to broad network access and set <code>KUJO_AI_ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS</code> to the
provider URLs the script may call.</p>
<p dir="auto">Read <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/SECURE_AI_SCRIPTING.md">Secure AI scripting</a> and the
<a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/NATIVE_API_SECURITY_POSTURE.md">native API security posture</a> before running
untrusted code on a shared or sensitive machine.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">AI-Native Runtime Snapshot</h2><a id="user-content-ai-native-runtime-snapshot" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: AI-Native Runtime Snapshot" href="#ai-native-runtime-snapshot"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Kujo keeps deterministic mechanisms in the runtime and leaves provider routing,
RAG policy, agent frameworks, and observability to packages.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>ai_chat</code>, <code>ai_stream_chat</code>, <code>ai_embedding</code>, and <code>ai_tool_loop</code> share replay,
response, and error contracts.</li>
<li><code>ai_request_hash</code> creates credential-free cache and cassette keys.</li>
<li><code>ai_text</code>, <code>ai_image_url</code>, and <code>ai_message</code> build portable messages.</li>
<li><code>ai_count_tokens</code> and <code>ai_fit_context</code> provide deterministic estimates.</li>
<li><code>secret</code>, <code>reveal</code>, and <code>is_secret</code> keep values redacted until code reveals them.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Run the replay example without live provider credentials:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="KUJO_AI_REPLAY=tests/fixtures/ai_cassettes \
KUJO_AI_REPLAY_MODE=strict \
cargo run -- run examples/ai_enterprise_replay_showcase.kujo"><pre>KUJO_AI_REPLAY=tests/fixtures/ai_cassettes \
KUJO_AI_REPLAY_MODE=strict \
cargo run -- run examples/ai_enterprise_replay_showcase.kujo</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The short and full verification commands are:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --minimal
bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --full"><pre>bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --minimal
bash scripts/enterprise_verify.sh --full</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">See <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/AI_RUNTIME.md">AI runtime</a> and the
<a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/STANDARD_LIBRARY.md">standard library</a> for the complete contracts.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Runtime Mode Recommendations</h2><a id="user-content-runtime-mode-recommendations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Runtime Mode Recommendations" href="#runtime-mode-recommendations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Use <code>kujo run <file></code> for normal work. Developers should not need <code>--interpreter</code> for ordinary modular project layouts.</li>
<li>Use <code>--interpreter</code> to isolate a compatibility or runtime-path problem.</li>
<li>Treat <code>--jit</code> as experimental. Unsupported bytecode falls back to the VM.</li>
<li>Use <code>kujo package-install --frozen</code> to check <code>kujo.toml</code> and <code>kujo.lock</code>
without changing either file.</li>
<li><code>kujo package-publish</code>: preview package publish metadata only. It does not
publish to Kennel. Kennel owns registry installation and distribution.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">See the <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/VM_INTERPRETER_MIGRATION_PLAYBOOK.md">VM/interpreter migration playbook</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">1.0 Release Status</h2><a id="user-content-10-release-status" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 1.0 Release Status" href="#10-release-status"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Release boundary: Kujo <code>v1.9.0</code> is the current stable release; explicit deferrals and compatibility guarantees are governed by <code>docs/V1_SCOPE.md</code>.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Kujo 1.9.0 is released for Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64 and Windows x64; see <a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/RELEASE_NOTES_1_9_0.md">release notes</a>.</li>
<li>The source tree is currently at <code>1.9.0</code> in <code>Cargo.toml</code>; the latest published stable release tag is <code>v1.9.0</code>.</li>
<li>The signed release, native/source archives, checksums, and all six npm packages
passed their published-install verification matrices.</li>
<li>Prebuilt Linux x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, and Windows x64 binaries ship with
SHA-256 checksums.</li>
<li>Kujo v1.0 package scope was local manifest and lockfile determinism only; it
did not include a public Kennel registry or package publish transport. That
describes the historical 1.0 runtime boundary. The separate Kennel registry is
now live at <a href="https://kennel.kujolang.ai/" rel="nofollow">kennel.kujolang.ai</a>.</li>
<li>The v1.0 launch record remains in
<a href="/kujolang/kujo/blob/7a13207019a51e61d3db448bc13f59d5b0e332e5/docs/V1_0_OFFICIAL_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md">the completed release checklist</a>.</li>
</ul>

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://github.com/kujolang/kujo.git
cd kujo

cargo run -- test --runtime dual"><pre>git clone https://github.com/kujolang/kujo.git
<span class="pl-c1">cd</span> kujo
cargo build --release

Functions and operators

Add the numbers in an array with a function.

# Expected output:
# total: 42

func total(values) {
    mut sum := 0
    for value in values {
        sum = sum + value
    }
    return sum
}

let scores := [8, 13, 21]
print("total: " + to_string(total(scores)))

Save as functions.kujo, then:

kujo run functions.kujo
Expected output
total: 42

Collections

let scores := [8, 13, 21]
let report := {"name": "build", "total": scores[0] + scores[1] + scores[2]}

print(report["name"] + " total: " + to_string(report["total"]))

Async tasks

Wait for an async function to return a value.

// Simple async test

async func get_value() {
    return 42;
}

let p = get_value();
println("Promise type: ", type(p));
let result = await p;
println("Result: ", result);

kujo run async.kujo

AI runtime · Executed offline

Deterministic AI request IDs

Hash an AI request without including credentials.

The credentials are dummy values. This example makes no network request.

func kv(label, value) {
    print(label + ": " + value)
}

let options_a := {
    "endpoint": "https://api.example.test/v1/chat/completions",
    "model": "gpt-demo",
    "api_key": "credential-one",
    "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer credential-one",
        "X-App": "kujo"
    },
    "body": {
        "temperature": 0,
        "max_tokens": 32
    }
}

let options_b := {
    "endpoint": "https://api.example.test/v1/chat/completions",
    "model": "gpt-demo",
    "api_key": "credential-two",
    "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer credential-two",
        "X-App": "kujo"
    },
    "body": {
        "temperature": 0,
        "max_tokens": 32
    }
}

let hash_a := ai_request_hash("Summarize Kujo", options_a)
let hash_b := ai_request_hash("Summarize Kujo", options_b)

kv("hash_length", to_string(len(hash_a)))
kv("same_without_credentials", to_string(hash_a == hash_b))
kv("hash", hash_a)

Save as request-hash.kujo, then:

kujo run request-hash.kujo
Expected output
hash_length: 64
same_without_credentials: true
hash: a6244047c108dcf58a952ed0a6c70dc04d13ee9aa9dba08eeb623f241fbd37ce

AI calls and replay

Replay a recorded model response offline.

Use the samples bundle or the pinned Kujo checkout so the cassette fixtures are available.

func kv(label, value) {
    print(label + ": " + value)
}

let options := {
    "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:1/v1/chat/completions",
    "model": "gpt-replay",
    "cassette": {
        "mode": "replay",
        "dir": "tests/fixtures/ai_cassettes"
    }
}

let result := ai_chat("Hello model", options)

kv("replay_result", to_string(result))

Save as replay.kujo, then:

kujo run replay.kujo

<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/kujolang/casefile"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/501b2ba5b092087b0e8d38be664307138f002f6f75e1a95e452e75626373d030/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f76657273696f6e2d312e302e322d626c61636b" alt="Version" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.2-black" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="/kujolang/casefile/blob/92e1d9bee2faaba322476e82dcea7510850885e0/LICENSE"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/be07a68b57a673af622198c336264f89d82bf4cd5d87bc0cb3f7b6ae47cc43ea/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6c6963656e73652d4d49542d6c6967687467726579" alt="License" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
<a href="https://github.com/kujolang/kujo"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/6b3480f7d340221eb016f867281fb8ec9c90042bc68ea9e663eb4651d2bb75f1/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6275696c74253230776974682d4b756a6f2d77686974652e737667" alt="built with Kujo" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Kujo-white.svg" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">CaseFile is a local Kujo CLI that turns command results, existing logs, and manual notes into plaintext debugging bundles. It does not call models or hosted services.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run casefile.kujo -- help
kujo run casefile.kujo -- init
kujo run casefile.kujo -- validate
kujo run casefile.kujo -- capture --name tests -- false
kujo run casefile.kujo -- show latest --format json"><pre>kujo run casefile.kujo -- <span class="pl-c1">help</span>
kujo run casefile.kujo -- init
kujo run casefile.kujo -- validate
kujo run casefile.kujo -- capture --name tests -- <span class="pl-c1">false</span>
kujo run casefile.kujo -- show latest --format json</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Run these commands from the repository being investigated, using an absolute path to <code>casefile.kujo</code> when it lives elsewhere. Config is loaded from the current directory; output is rooted at the Git top level, or the current directory outside Git. Captured commands inherit the current directory and environment.</p>
<p dir="auto">Start with <code>case.md</code>, <code>case.json</code>, and <code>handoff.md</code>; consult logs and Git artifacts for details. <code>case.json</code> is the completion marker and the machine-readable contract. Capture returns 0 after successfully recording a failed command; use <code>--mirror-exit-code</code> to preserve its status.</p>
<p dir="auto">Requirements: Kujo 1.8.1 or newer with <code>write_file_atomic</code> and <code>path_is_symlink</code> support, Git, and POSIX utilities (<code>mkdir</code>, <code>date</code>, <code>head</code>, <code>rm</code>, <code>uname</code>). Python 3 is only used for tests and measurements. No package installation or network access is required by CaseFile itself. Tool version probes run installed executables from PATH, which must be trusted.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>kennel.toml</code> declares the official package metadata, CLI entry point, runtime requirement, and verification scripts. <code>casefile.toml</code> configures evidence capture in the workspace being investigated. Normal use runs on Kujo's default VM; <code>--interpreter</code> is an optional runtime override.</p>

<p dir="auto">Drive-qualified and extended-length paths passed to file utilities use forward slashes for Git
for Windows compatibility. Directory-creation failures include the utility error.
Exclusive creation is preserved. POSIX uses mode 0700; drive-qualified Windows
paths inherit their parent ACL and require a private parent directory.</p>

See [authoring](docs/authoring.md) for layouts, themes,","motion, and custom HTML.","","## Quick start","","Install Git, patched Node 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+, or 26.12.1+, and [Kujo 1.5+](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo), then run:","","```sh","git clone https://github.com/kujolang/presentations.git","cd presentations","npm run deck -- start investor my-pitch --title \"My company\"","```","","This copies a starter to `decks/my-pitch/`, installs pinned SSG and SiteKit","versions, builds the deck, and serves it at `http://127.0.0.1:8086/`.","Press Ctrl+C to stop. It does not verify facts or","visual fit. Review every slide before presenting. Changes require a rebuild;","the preview does not watch files.","","Ten reusable layouts cover titles, indexes, images, metrics, features, business","models, and percentage charts. The canvas keeps its 16:9 composition as the","browser resizes. The overview, controls, and text edition adapt to the viewport.","See [authoring](docs/authoring.md) for fields, themes, and custom layouts.","","## Motion and controls","","Optional Motion presets range from fade, slide, and zoom to coordinated","headline, image, card, and chart animations. Editorial, Focus, and Kinetic","presets support per-slide settings, intensity, timing, and stagger.","The configured entrance plays on the first page load and when you change slides.","Use **Replay entrance** to review it again.","","Motion loads from local files only when needed. Viewers can turn it off, and","system reduced-motion preferences always take precedence.","See [transitions](docs/transitions.md) for configuration.","","| Control | Action |","| --- | --- |","| Left / Right | Previous / next slide |","| Space | Next slide; keeps normal behavior on buttons and links |","| Home / End | First / last slide |","| F / Escape | Enter slide-only fullscreen / exit fullscreen |","| Overview | View linked thumbnails of all slides |","| Read text | Read the deck, chart values, and image descriptions as a normal page |","","Shortcuts leave text inputs and browser modifier keys alone. Native links work","without JavaScript. Fullscreen and enabled transitions fetch generated pages;","failed fetches fall back to normal navigation.","","## Build and host","","With dependencies installed under `.deps/`, or sibling `ssg/` and built","`site-kit/` checkouts, run from this repository:","","```sh","kujo run build.kujo","kujo run build.kujo -- --deck examples/field-notes","kujo serve output --port 8086","```","","Open `http://127.0.0.1:8086/reference/` or `/field-notes/`.","For dependencies elsewhere:","","```sh","kujo run build.kujo -- --deck /path/to/my-deck \\","  --ssg /path/to/ssg --sitekit /path/to/site-kit/dist \\","  --site-url https://example.com/my-deck","```","","`npm run deck -- setup` installs the pinned versions in [dependencies.json](dependencies.json)","under `.deps/`. Pass `--ssg .deps/ssg --sitekit .deps/site-kit/dist` to use those","paths explicitly with the native builder. Both entry points prefer `.deps/`","when available and otherwise use siblings. The Node CLI handles setup and review; Kujo renders","the deck.","","Deploy `output/\u003cdeck-id\u003e/` to a static host with directory-index support. Each","slide has a numbered URL, such as `/1/`, plus `/reading/` for the text edition.","Direct links and refresh need no rewrite rules. Relative links support hosting","under a subdirectory. Use HTTP for local previews; `file://` is not supported.","","The build replaces `.build/\u003cdeck-id\u003e/` and `output/\u003cdeck-id\u003e/`. Keep authored","files elsewhere, and never run two builds for the same deck ID at once.","","## Architecture","","```text","Kujo SSG ─── CLI and templates ──┐","                               ├── Presentations ── individual decks","SiteKit ─── CSS and tokens ─────┘","```","","The presentation package owns layouts, content validation, canvas geometry,","controls, and motion. SSG generates pages and copies assets. SiteKit supplies","controls, layout utilities, focus styles, and default tokens. Decks own content,","images, and themes. Neither upstream project depends on Presentations.","See [architecture](docs/architecture.md) for the boundaries and build process.","","## Repository layout","","| Path | Purpose |","| --- | --- |","| `build.kujo` | Stable public command; delegates to `src/build.kujo` |","| `src/` | Native build, validation, and rendering implementation |","| `assets/`, `layouts/` | Browser behavior, CSS, and reusable compositions |","| `scripts/` | Setup, authoring, bundling, and inspection tools |","| `examples/`, `starters/` | Separate content, themes, and starting points |","| `tests/`, `docs/` | Verification and author/maintainer guides |","| Root manifests and schema | Package metadata, pinned dependencies, and editor discovery |","","The root entry point, manifests, schema, license, and agent instructions remain","where the CLI and package tools expect them. Generated output stays ignored.","Use trusted asset trees: every file under a deck's `assets/` is published in its","output. Validation rejects hidden entries, symlinks, and special files. <p dir="auto">Kujo Presentations builds browser-native slide decks with Kujo SSG and SiteKit.
Each deck becomes a static website with numbered slide URLs, an overview, a
readable text edition, print and PDF output, and optional presenter tools.
Add Motion presets or write custom layouts and CSS without locking your content
inside a presentation app. Speaker notes stay local to the presenter tab.</p>
<p dir="auto">Presentations is an optional package. It adds no code or dependencies to SSG or
SiteKit. Version 0.3.1 is a preview; the content and extension APIs may change.
See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/release.md">release status</a> and the <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/support-matrix.md">support matrix</a>
for verified platforms and known limits. GitHub releases distribute the source;
<code>package.json</code> keeps <code>private: true</code> to prevent accidental npm publication.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://presentations.kujolang.ai/" rel="nofollow">Explore the live presentations</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/images/reference-overview.webp"><img src="/kujolang/presentations/raw/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/images/reference-overview.webp" alt="Nine-slide media example" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>

motion, and custom HTML.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick start</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick start" href="#quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Install Git, patched Node 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+, or 26.12.1+, and <a href="https://github.com/kujolang/kujo">Kujo 1.5+</a>, then run:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://github.com/kujolang/presentations.git
cd presentations
npm run deck -- start investor my-pitch --title "My company""><pre>git clone https://github.com/kujolang/presentations.git
<span class="pl-c1">cd</span> presentations
npm run deck -- start investor my-pitch --title <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>My company<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This copies a starter to <code>decks/my-pitch/</code>, installs pinned SSG and SiteKit
versions, builds the deck, and serves it at <code>http://127.0.0.1:8086/</code>.
Press Ctrl+C to stop. Use <code>--port 8087</code> if the port is busy.
The draft contains placeholders for your facts and images.</p>

<p dir="auto">For an agent-led workflow, give your agent <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/CREATE_A_DECK.md">CREATE_A_DECK.md</a>

build. See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/getting-started.md">getting started</a> for setup and troubleshooting.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Edit and review</h2><a id="user-content-edit-and-review" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Edit and review" href="#edit-and-review"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Edit <code>decks/my-pitch/deck.json</code> for content and order, <code>assets/theme.css</code> inside
that deck for its appearance, and <code>BRIEF.md</code> for sources and decisions.
Then run:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npm run deck -- check --deck decks/my-pitch --ready
npm run deck -- build --deck decks/my-pitch
npm run deck -- preview --deck decks/my-pitch"><pre>npm run deck -- check --deck decks/my-pitch --ready
npm run deck -- build --deck decks/my-pitch
npm run deck -- preview --deck decks/my-pitch</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>check --ready</code> rejects unfinished placeholders. It does not verify facts or
visual fit. Review every slide before presenting. Changes require a rebuild;
the preview does not watch files.</p>
<p dir="auto">Ten reusable layouts cover titles, indexes, images, metrics, features, business
models, and percentage charts. The canvas keeps its 16:9 composition as the
browser resizes. The overview, controls, and text edition adapt to the viewport.
See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/authoring.md">authoring</a> for fields, themes, and custom layouts.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Motion and controls</h2><a id="user-content-motion-and-controls" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Motion and controls" href="#motion-and-controls"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Optional Motion presets range from fade, slide, and zoom to coordinated
headline, image, card, and chart animations. Editorial, Focus, and Kinetic
presets support per-slide settings, intensity, timing, and stagger.
The configured entrance plays on the first page load and when you change slides.
Use <strong>Replay entrance</strong> to review it again.</p>
<p dir="auto">Motion loads from local files only when needed. Viewers can turn it off, and
system reduced-motion preferences always take precedence.
See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/transitions.md">transitions</a> for configuration.</p>
