<p dir="auto">Shortcuts leave text inputs and browser modifier keys alone. Native links work
without JavaScript. Fullscreen and enabled transitions fetch generated pages;
failed fetches fall back to normal navigation.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Build and host</h2><a id="user-content-build-and-host" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Build and host" href="#build-and-host"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">With dependencies installed under <code>.deps/</code>, or sibling <code>ssg/</code> and built
<code>site-kit/</code> checkouts, run from this repository:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run build.kujo
kujo run build.kujo -- --deck examples/field-notes
kujo serve output --port 8086"><pre>kujo run build.kujo
kujo run build.kujo -- --deck examples/field-notes
kujo serve output --port 8086</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Open <code>http://127.0.0.1:8086/reference/</code> or <code>/field-notes/</code>.
For dependencies elsewhere:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run build.kujo -- --deck /path/to/my-deck \
  --ssg /path/to/ssg --sitekit /path/to/site-kit/dist \
  --site-url https://example.com/my-deck"><pre>kujo run build.kujo -- --deck /path/to/my-deck \
  --ssg /path/to/ssg --sitekit /path/to/site-kit/dist \
  --site-url https://example.com/my-deck</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>npm run deck -- setup</code> installs the pinned versions in <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/dependencies.json">dependencies.json</a>
under <code>.deps/</code>. Pass <code>--ssg .deps/ssg --sitekit .deps/site-kit/dist</code> to use those
paths explicitly with the native builder. Both entry points prefer <code>.deps/</code>
when available and otherwise use siblings. The Node CLI handles setup and review; Kujo renders
the deck.</p>
<p dir="auto">Deploy <code>output/<deck-id>/</code> to a static host with directory-index support. Each
slide has a numbered URL, such as <code>/1/</code>, plus <code>/reading/</code> for the text edition.
Direct links and refresh need no rewrite rules. Relative links support hosting
under a subdirectory. Use HTTP for local previews; <code>file://</code> is not supported.</p>
<p dir="auto">The build replaces <code>.build/<deck-id>/</code> and <code>output/<deck-id>/</code>. Keep authored
files elsewhere, and never run two builds for the same deck ID at once.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Architecture</h2><a id="user-content-architecture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Architecture" href="#architecture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">The presentation package owns layouts, content validation, canvas geometry,
controls, and motion. SSG generates pages and copies assets. SiteKit supplies
controls, layout utilities, focus styles, and default tokens. Decks own content,
images, and themes. Neither upstream project depends on Presentations.
See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/architecture.md">architecture</a> for the boundaries and build process.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Repository layout</h2><a id="user-content-repository-layout" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Repository layout" href="#repository-layout"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">The root entry point, manifests, schema, license, and agent instructions remain
where the CLI and package tools expect them. Generated output stays ignored.
Use trusted asset trees: every file under a deck's <code>assets/</code> is published in its
output. Validation rejects hidden entries, symlinks, and special files. Failed
builds preserve the last successful deck; same-ID builds are locked. See <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/deployment.md">deployment guidance</a> for hosting and access.</p>

<p dir="auto">Tests cover content validation, routes, assets, keyboard controls, history,
fullscreen, canvas layout, no-JavaScript navigation, motion, and axe accessibility
checks. The native command runs Firefox against the hardened Kujo preview server.
See the <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/docs/firefox-fullscreen-review.md">Firefox and fullscreen review</a> for
the pinned browser source correction and evidence. Browser test preparation
requires Python 3; the test commands prepare automatically. Deck builds do not. Browser screenshots go to <code>test-results/</code>. Automated checks do not replace
visual, factual, or accessibility review.</p>
<p dir="auto">The media example uses fictional copy and metrics and follows a written design
brief. It is not a verified pixel match to a source image. Photography comes from
local AI-generated WebP artwork with recorded prompts and hashes; see <a href="/kujolang/presentations/blob/879211bbf3707ec1ec6a9e19bb9ce2b1f9691bfa/examples/reference/ASSETS.md">asset sources</a>.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Spec</strong> defines task contracts, acceptance criteria, expected outputs, and agent-readable work instructions for AI-native development.</p>
<p dir="auto">A <code>.spec.yml</code> file turns human instructions into a clear, reviewable task contract.</p>
<p dir="auto">Prioritize copyable examples over tests: examples should model the most token-efficient idioms we want agents to imitate.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Launch Readiness</h2><a id="user-content-launch-readiness" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Launch Readiness" href="#launch-readiness"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Spec 1.0 is stable for local development, CI, monorepos, and regulated automation environments where the verification suite is run against the target runtime and trust boundaries. It includes path-boundary checks, symlink escape protection, safe-write controls, strict validation mode, generated command inventory checks, completion parity checks, fuzz coverage, benchmark gates, and release quality gates.</p>
<p dir="auto">No CLI can be universally production-ready without being validated against the target organization's runtime, CI runner, trust boundaries, and release process. For enterprise adoption, run the verification suite in your environment, pin <code>KUJO_BIN</code>, enable <code>SPEC_SAFE_WRITE=on</code>, and set <code>SPEC_TEMPLATE_SOURCE_POLICY=project-only</code> in CI.</p>

<p dir="auto">Most agent failures start with vague requirements, not code generation.</p>
<p dir="auto">Spec gives Kujo a native task-contract format before implementation starts:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Goal</strong> — the primary objective</li>
<li><strong>Background</strong> — context and motivation</li>
<li><strong>Scope</strong> — what's in and out of scope</li>
<li><strong>Acceptance criteria</strong> — verifiable conditions for completion</li>
<li><strong>Eval requirements</strong> — automated checks that validate outcomes</li>
<li><strong>Risks</strong> — known risks with severity and mitigations</li>
<li><strong>Dependencies</strong> — what must be available before starting</li>
<li><strong>Review expectations</strong> — how the work will be reviewed</li>
<li><strong>Human approval points</strong> — where humans must sign off</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Safe-write mode:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>SPEC_SAFE_WRITE=auto|on|off</code> controls output-path restrictions.</li>
<li><code>auto</code> (default) enables restrictions for <code>spec ci</code> command context.</li>
<li>Use <code>--unsafe-write</code> to explicitly override per command.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Template source policy:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>SPEC_TEMPLATE_SOURCE_POLICY=allow-home|project-only</code> controls whether <code>spec init --from template:<name></code> can load templates from <code>$HOME/.config/kujo-spec/templates</code>.</li>
<li>Use <code>--strict-template-source</code> for one-off project-only resolution.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">CI scaling controls:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>spec ci --max-files <n></code> bounds scan time in very large repositories.</li>
<li><code>spec ci --fail-fast</code> exits early on first invalid spec to shorten feedback loops.</li>
<li><code>spec ci --jobs <n></code> enables deterministic parallel validation for enterprise-scale trees.</li>
<li>Flags can be combined with any argument order, for example: <code>spec ci --format json ./specs --max-files 200 --jobs 4</code>.</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Export Envelope Format</h3><a id="user-content-export-envelope-format" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Export Envelope Format" href="#export-envelope-format"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Use <code>spec export --format envelope</code> when automation needs payload + metadata in one JSON object.</p>
<p dir="auto">Spec pairs well with Eval when you want the work to be verifiable, not just described.</p>
<p dir="auto">Metadata fields:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>source_file</code></li>
<li><code>schema_version</code></li>
<li><code>checksum_sha256</code></li>
<li><code>generated_at</code></li>
<li><code>payload_format</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Example:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="spec export spec.yml --format envelope --payload-format dispatch --output artifacts/spec.envelope.json"><pre>spec <span class="pl-k">export</span> spec.yml --format envelope --payload-format dispatch --output artifacts/spec.envelope.json</pre></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Known Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-known-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Known Limitations" href="#known-limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>YAML parsing: complex YAML features (anchors, multi-document, tags) are not supported. Use the subset documented above.</li>
<li>TOML parsing: basic key=value only. Nested tables and arrays of tables are not yet supported.</li>
<li>Kujo runtime: The shell CLI delegates YAML/TOML conversion plus validate/render/export logic to Kujo modules. Cross-module imports (<code>from src.common import ...</code>) are supported as of Kujo v1.0.0+.</li>
<li>The <code>KUJO_BIN</code> environment variable must point to the Kujo language runtime (not the Python linter).</li>
<li>File size limit: 1MB maximum per spec file. Larger files are rejected before parsing.</li>
<li>When <code>SPEC_SAFE_WRITE</code> is enabled, output paths are restricted to the current project root unless <code>--unsafe-write</code> is provided.</li>
<li><code>spec changelog</code> defaults to the latest tag when present and falls back to the repository root commit when no tags exist.</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Runtime source lives in <code>src/</code>, CLI orchestration lives in <code>scripts/</code>, and generated/user-facing documentation lives in <code>docs/</code>. The root intentionally keeps package, release, policy, and ecosystem control files because external tooling expects them there.</p>
<p dir="auto">Keep these root files in place unless the corresponding release or package tooling is updated first:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>VERSION</code></li>
<li><code>RUNTIME_VERSION</code></li>
<li><code>kennel.toml</code></li>
<li><code>kujo.toml</code></li>
<li><code>package.json</code></li>
<li><code>Dockerfile</code></li>
<li><code>LICENSE</code></li>
<li><code>SECURITY.md</code></li>
<li><code>CONTRIBUTING.md</code></li>
<li><code>CHANGELOG.md</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">There are no duplicate root-level Kujo source modules to move into <code>src/</code>; the active Kujo modules are <code>src/common.kujo</code>, <code>src/convert.kujo</code>, <code>src/export.kujo</code>, <code>src/render.kujo</code>, and <code>src/validate.kujo</code>.</p>

<p dir="auto"><code>tests/benchmark.sh</code> uses a stable, single-pass methodology:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Generate <code>N</code> YAML specs with valid minimal content.</li>
<li>Time one <code>spec validate-all</code> run over that directory.</li>
<li>Compare wall-clock runtime to an environment budget.</li>
<li>Enforce trend budget using <code>ci_runtime_ms</code> from machine-readable benchmark summary output.</li>
</ul>

the question:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eDid the agent, workflow, model, generated output, or code change actually do the right thing?\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSpec defines what should happen. Eval checks whether the work actually produced the expected evidence.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEval is part of Kujo’s Control layer: measurable outcomes, repeatable checks, reviewable reports, and machine-readable evidence.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003esrc/watchdog_telemetry.kujo\u003c/code\u003e projects suite/check scores and statuses into\nbounded \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog.native-event.v1\u003c/code\u003e evaluation events. Callers supply the target\nWatchdog trace/run correlation; Eval continues to own execution and reports.\nThe projection excludes check parameters, command output, paths, diffs,\nsnapshots, and failure messages, so enabling it cannot expand content capture.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrioritize copyable examples over tests: examples should model the most token-efficient idioms we want agents to imitate.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eExclude generated/bulk paths from the main sweep unless the task explicitly targets them; document the search exclusions you used.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy This Exists\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-this-exists\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why This Exists\" href=\"#why-this-exists\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery serious AI-native ecosystem needs evaluations. Without evals, agents are vibes. With evals, agents become software components that can be tested, trusted, compared, and improved.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEval provides:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e27 deterministic checks\u003c/strong\u003e — command success/failure, file existence/content/line count, JSON shape/value/path, HTTP status/body, regex, timing, snapshots, directory comparison, environment variables, and more.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e5 report formats\u003c/strong\u003e — Markdown, HTML (collapsible details + summary cards), JUnit XML, TAP, and NDJSON streaming.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSnapshot testing\u003c/strong\u003e — store expected outputs and detect regressions with unified diff.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRun comparison\u003c/strong\u003e — compare two eval runs to detect improvements or regressions.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRetry support\u003c/strong\u003e — mark flaky tests with \u003ccode\u003e\"retry\": N\u003c/code\u003e to auto-retry on failure.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDependency ordering\u003c/strong\u003e — declare \u003ccode\u003e\"depends_on\": [...]\u003c/code\u003e to skip tests when dependencies fail.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEnterprise policy presets\u003c/strong\u003e — use \u003ccode\u003e\"policy_profile\": \"strict-ci\" | \"local-dev\" | \"release-gate\"\u003c/code\u003e for fast onboarding.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTiming\u003c/strong\u003e — every run records \u003ccode\u003eduration_ms\u003c/code\u003e; \u003ccode\u003ecommand_timing_less_than\u003c/code\u003e check for perf regression.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eQuiet/verbose modes\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e--quiet\u003c/code\u003e suppresses per-test output (CI mode); \u003ccode\u003e--verbose\u003c/code\u003e prints full check details.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e14 CLI commands\u003c/strong\u003e — init, run, report, compare, list-checks, snapshots, version, watch, lint, policy-explain, diff, export, verify-manifest, completion.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCI-ready\u003c/strong\u003e — non-zero exit on failure; JSON/NDJSON output; GitHub Actions step summary; shields.io badge.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDeterministic CI artifacts\u003c/strong\u003e — each run writes \u003ccode\u003esummary.json\u003c/code\u003e, a producer-neutral \u003ccode\u003eevaluation-result.json\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eartifact-manifest.json\u003c/code\u003e for machine consumers.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eMachine summary channel\u003c/strong\u003e — run/report write \u003ccode\u003ecli-summary.json\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e--summary-channel-path\u003c/code\u003e) as a stable automation handoff artifact.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArtifact integrity mode\u003c/strong\u003e — opt into SHA-256 checksums in \u003ccode\u003eartifact-manifest.json\u003c/code\u003e and verify with \u003ccode\u003everify-manifest\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParallel scale mode\u003c/strong\u003e — opt into \u003ccode\u003e--parallel-workers\u003c/code\u003e for independent file-check fast paths with deterministic ordering.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRetention controls\u003c/strong\u003e — bound output growth with \u003ccode\u003ehistory_retention_runs\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eaux_artifact_retention_files\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecurity controls\u003c/strong\u003e — 5-layer defense: command allowlisting + pattern policy, path boundary enforcement, output redaction, config size/depth limits, max output truncation.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCommand guardrails\u003c/strong\u003e — overly long command payloads are rejected before execution (\u003ccode\u003eMAX_COMMAND_LENGTH\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFully local\u003c/strong\u003e — no API keys, no network dependencies, completely deterministic.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eKujo's core argument is that AI-native software needs new primitives. output, or code change actually do the right thing?","","Spec defines what should happen. Eval checks whether the work actually produced the expected evidence.","","Eval is part of Kujo’s Control layer: measurable outcomes, repeatable checks, reviewable reports, and machine-readable evidence.","","`src/watchdog_telemetry.kujo` projects suite/check scores and statuses into","bounded `watchdog.native-event.v1` evaluation events. Callers supply the target","Watchdog trace/run correlation; Eval continues to own execution and reports.","The projection excludes check parameters, command output, paths, diffs,","snapshots, and failure messages, so enabling it cannot expand content capture.","","Prioritize copyable examples over tests: examples should model the most token-efficient idioms we want agents to imitate.","","Exclude generated/bulk paths from the main sweep unless the task explicitly targets them; document the search exclusions you used.","","## Why This Exists","","Every serious AI-native ecosystem needs evaluations. Without evals, agents are vibes. With evals, agents become software components that can be tested, trusted, compared, and improved.","","Eval provides:","","- **27 deterministic checks** — command success/failure, file existence/content/line count, JSON shape/value/path, HTTP status/body, regex, timing, snapshots, directory comparison, environment variables, and more.","- **5 report formats** — Markdown, HTML (collapsible details + summary cards), JUnit XML, TAP, and NDJSON streaming.","- **Snapshot testing** — store expected outputs and detect regressions with unified diff.","- **Run comparison** — compare two eval runs to detect improvements or regressions.","- **Retry support** — mark flaky tests with `\"retry\": N` to auto-retry on failure.","- **Dependency ordering** — declare `\"depends_on\": [...]` to skip tests when dependencies fail.","- **Enterprise policy presets** — use `\"policy_profile\": \"strict-ci\" | \"local-dev\" | \"release-gate\"` for fast onboarding.","- **Timing** — every run records `duration_ms`; `command_timing_less_than` check for perf regression.","- **Quiet/verbose modes** — `--quiet` suppresses per-test output (CI mode); `--verbose` prints full check details.","- **14 CLI commands** — init, run, report, compare, list-checks, snapshots, version, watch, lint, policy-explain, diff, export, verify-manifest, completion.","- **CI-ready** — non-zero exit on failure; JSON/NDJSON output; GitHub Actions step summary; shields.io badge.","- **Deterministic CI artifacts** — each run writes `summary.json`, a producer-neutral `evaluation-result.json`, and `artifact-manifest.json` for machine consumers.","- **Machine summary channel** — run/report write `cli-summary.json` (or `--summary-channel-path`) as a stable automation handoff artifact.","- **Artifact integrity mode** — opt into SHA-256 checksums in `artifact-manifest.json` and verify with `verify-manifest`.","- **Parallel scale mode** — opt into `--parallel-workers` for independent file-check fast paths with deterministic ordering.","- **Retention controls** — bound output growth with `history_retention_runs` and `aux_artifact_retention_files`.","- **Security controls** — 5-layer defense: command allowlisting + pattern policy, path boundary enforcement, output redaction, config size/depth limits, max output truncation.","- **Command guardrails** — overly long command payloads are rejected before execution (`MAX_COMMAND_LENGTH`).","- **Fully local** — no API keys, no network dependencies, completely deterministic.","","Kujo's core argument is that AI-native software needs new primitives. Eval is one of those primitives.","","Traditional tests answer:","","\u003e Does this function return the expected value?","","Eval answers:","","\u003e Did this agent or AI-assisted workflow produce the correct outcome under real project constraints?","","## Requirements","","- Kujo CLI/runtime available on your machine.","- No API keys or external services needed (fully local, deterministic).","","## Containerized Usage","","This repository includes a local/CI-oriented multi-stage `Dockerfile` that compiles the Kujo runtime from the pinned revision in `RUNTIME_VERSION`. Treat production deployment of the image as target-environment work: rebuild it in your controlled pipeline, scan it with your registry policy, and validate it against your runner boundaries before using it for production claims.","","Build the image:","","```bash","docker build -t kujo-eval:local .","```","","Optionally override the runtime ref at build time:","","```bash","docker build --build-arg KUJO_RUNTIME_REF=\u003ctag-or-commit\u003e -t kujo-eval:local .","```","","Run a suite in the container:","","```bash","docker run --rm -v \"$PWD\":/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local run","```","","Generate a report in the container:","","```bash","docker run --rm -v \"$PWD\":/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local report --format json --out eval_results/report.json","```","","## Runtime Binary Selection","","`kujo-eval` expects the Kujo language runtime command to be available as `kujo`:","","```bash","kujo --version","```","","If your shell resolves `kujo` to a different such as:","","```bash","kujo run main.kujo -- run \u003csuite\u003e","```","","Current recommended default is VM-first execution:","","```bash","kujo run main.kujo run \u003csuite\u003e","```","","Use `--interpreter` only for runtime compatibility checks, warning investigations, or parity debugging.","","Migration mapping:","","- Legacy: `kujo run main.kujo --interpreter \u003ccommand\u003e`","- Preferred: `kujo run main.kujo \u003ccommand\u003e`","- Optional compatibility check: `kujo run main.kujo --interpreter \u003ccommand\u003e`","","Interpreter mode can emit KUJORUN001 warning noise while still succeeding; rely on exit code plus generated artifacts (`summary.json`, `evaluation-result.json`, `artifact-manifest.json`) for CI pass/fail decisions.","","## Operational Watchdog Controls","","Release and parity scripts include artifact-aware watchdogs to keep CI deterministic even when interpreter output capture behaves inconsistently.","","Watchdog loops use portable `sleep` scripts/cli_smoke_matrix.sh --include-interpreter","scripts/release_quality_gates.sh","```","","## Known Runtime Limitations","","- Interpreter mode may print KUJORUN001 type-check warnings even when commands exit successfully.","- Command checks support native process timeout termination through `timeout_ms` and suite-level `timeout_seconds`.","- `watch` is intentionally long-running and should be interrupted manually in local shells.","- Command and file checks run in the host environment and are not a full sandbox boundary.","- Some interpreter invocations can stall when stdout/stderr is shell-captured; release/parity gate scripts mitigate this with artifact-driven watchdogs.","","## Launch Scope Snapshot","","Eval is verified for deterministic local and CI evaluation workflows where shell/file access is expected and controlled by repository policy.","","It is not yet a universal fit for every enterprise testing context. Before broad rollout, evaluate the following constraints for your environment:","","- Timeout enforcement depends on runtime support for `execute_status` timeout handling in your target Kujo build.","- No isolated sandbox boundary; commands execute with host-level permissions.","- Runtime warning noise in interpreter mode may require log filtering in strict observability pipelines.","- Feature roadmap items (LLM-as-judge, model-cost scoring, distributed execution) are intentionally out of current deterministic scope.","","If your use case needs strict isolation, guaranteed process preemption, or non-local execution controls, place Eval behind additional platform controls (container boundaries, workload policies, and external supervisors).","","## Enterprise Deployment Patterns","","Eval can be deployed in enterprise CI/CD and platform workflows with a simple layered model:","","1. **Runner boundary**: execute eval jobs in short-lived containers or isolated runners with least-privilege filesystem mounts.","2. **Command policy**: define `allowed_commands`, `allowed_command_patterns`, and `blocked_arg_patterns` at suite level; override only where needed at test level.","3. **Path policy**: scope file assertions using `allowed_paths` to explicitly owned workspace directories.","4. **Environment policy**: expose only approved variables and enforce with `allowed_env_vars`.","5. **Artifact policy**: keep report outputs (`--output-dir`) in per-run isolated folders and publish only required formats (JSON/JUnit/TAP/HTML/NDJSON).","","Suggested rollout:","","1. Start with `--json --quiet` in CI to establish deterministic pass/fail gates.","2. Add JUnit/TAP report publication for existing enterprise test dashboards.","3. Enforce suite-level command/path/env policy defaults before allowing per-test overrides.","4. <p dir="auto">Evaluation framework for AI-native software — deterministic checks for agents, CLIs, files, snapshots, and workflow outputs.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>v1.1.0 stable release:</strong> 27 checks, 14 CLI commands, 9 test suites.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Eval answers the question:</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Did the agent, workflow, model, generated output, or code change actually do the right thing?</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Spec defines what should happen. Eval checks whether the work actually produced the expected evidence.</p>
<p dir="auto">Eval is part of Kujo’s Control layer: measurable outcomes, repeatable checks, reviewable reports, and machine-readable evidence.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>src/watchdog_telemetry.kujo</code> projects suite/check scores and statuses into
bounded <code>watchdog.native-event.v1</code> evaluation events. Callers supply the target
Watchdog trace/run correlation; Eval continues to own execution and reports.
The projection excludes check parameters, command output, paths, diffs,
snapshots, and failure messages, so enabling it cannot expand content capture.</p>
<p dir="auto">Prioritize copyable examples over tests: examples should model the most token-efficient idioms we want agents to imitate.</p>
<p dir="auto">Exclude generated/bulk paths from the main sweep unless the task explicitly targets them; document the search exclusions you used.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why This Exists</h2><a id="user-content-why-this-exists" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why This Exists" href="#why-this-exists"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every serious AI-native ecosystem needs evaluations. Without evals, agents are vibes. With evals, agents become software components that can be tested, trusted, compared, and improved.</p>
<p dir="auto">Eval provides:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>27 deterministic checks</strong> — command success/failure, file existence/content/line count, JSON shape/value/path, HTTP status/body, regex, timing, snapshots, directory comparison, environment variables, and more.</li>
<li><strong>5 report formats</strong> — Markdown, HTML (collapsible details + summary cards), JUnit XML, TAP, and NDJSON streaming.</li>
<li><strong>Snapshot testing</strong> — store expected outputs and detect regressions with unified diff.</li>
<li><strong>Run comparison</strong> — compare two eval runs to detect improvements or regressions.</li>
<li><strong>Retry support</strong> — mark flaky tests with <code>"retry": N</code> to auto-retry on failure.</li>
<li><strong>Dependency ordering</strong> — declare <code>"depends_on": [...]</code> to skip tests when dependencies fail.</li>
<li><strong>Enterprise policy presets</strong> — use <code>"policy_profile": "strict-ci" | "local-dev" | "release-gate"</code> for fast onboarding.</li>
<li><strong>Timing</strong> — every run records <code>duration_ms</code>; <code>command_timing_less_than</code> check for perf regression.</li>
<li><strong>Quiet/verbose modes</strong> — <code>--quiet</code> suppresses per-test output (CI mode); <code>--verbose</code> prints full check details.</li>
<li><strong>14 CLI commands</strong> — init, run, report, compare, list-checks, snapshots, version, watch, lint, policy-explain, diff, export, verify-manifest, completion.</li>
<li><strong>CI-ready</strong> — non-zero exit on failure; JSON/NDJSON output; GitHub Actions step summary; shields.io badge.</li>
<li><strong>Deterministic CI artifacts</strong> — each run writes <code>summary.json</code>, a producer-neutral <code>evaluation-result.json</code>, and <code>artifact-manifest.json</code> for machine consumers.</li>
<li><strong>Machine summary channel</strong> — run/report write <code>cli-summary.json</code> (or <code>--summary-channel-path</code>) as a stable automation handoff artifact.</li>
<li><strong>Artifact integrity mode</strong> — opt into SHA-256 checksums in <code>artifact-manifest.json</code> and verify with <code>verify-manifest</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Parallel scale mode</strong> — opt into <code>--parallel-workers</code> for independent file-check fast paths with deterministic ordering.</li>
<li><strong>Retention controls</strong> — bound output growth with <code>history_retention_runs</code> and <code>aux_artifact_retention_files</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Security controls</strong> — 5-layer defense: command allowlisting + pattern policy, path boundary enforcement, output redaction, config size/depth limits, max output truncation.</li>
<li><strong>Command guardrails</strong> — overly long command payloads are rejected before execution (<code>MAX_COMMAND_LENGTH</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Fully local</strong> — no API keys, no network dependencies, completely deterministic.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Kujo's core argument is that AI-native software needs new primitives. Eval is one of those primitives.</p>
<p dir="auto">Traditional tests answer:</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Does this function return the expected value?</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Eval answers:</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Did this agent or AI-assisted workflow produce the correct outcome under real project constraints?</p>
</blockquote>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Containerized Usage</h2><a id="user-content-containerized-usage" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Containerized Usage" href="#containerized-usage"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">This repository includes a local/CI-oriented multi-stage <code>Dockerfile</code> that compiles the Kujo runtime from the pinned revision in <code>RUNTIME_VERSION</code>. Treat production deployment of the image as target-environment work: rebuild it in your controlled pipeline, scan it with your registry policy, and validate it against your runner boundaries before using it for production claims.</p>
<p dir="auto">Build the image:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker build -t kujo-eval:local ."><pre>docker build -t kujo-eval:local <span class="pl-c1">.</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Optionally override the runtime ref at build time:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker build --build-arg KUJO_RUNTIME_REF=<tag-or-commit> -t kujo-eval:local ."><pre>docker build --build-arg KUJO_RUNTIME_REF=<span class="pl-k"><</span>tag-or-commit<span class="pl-k">></span> -t kujo-eval:local <span class="pl-c1">.</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Run a suite in the container:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local run"><pre>docker run --rm -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$PWD</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>:/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local run</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Generate a report in the container:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local report --format json --out eval_results/report.json"><pre>docker run --rm -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$PWD</span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>:/workspace -w /workspace kujo-eval:local report --format json --out eval_results/report.json</pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Runtime Binary Selection</h2><a id="user-content-runtime-binary-selection" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Runtime Binary Selection" href="#runtime-binary-selection"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>kujo-eval</code> expects the Kujo language runtime command to be available as <code>kujo</code>:</p>

<p dir="auto">If your shell resolves <code>kujo</code> to a different tool, fix your <code>PATH</code> before running these examples.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">VM-First Migration Note (Interpreter-Era Guidance)</h2><a id="user-content-vm-first-migration-note-interpreter-era-guidance" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: VM-First Migration Note (Interpreter-Era Guidance)" href="#vm-first-migration-note-interpreter-era-guidance"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Older repository docs and shell snippets may still show interpreter-era commands such as:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run main.kujo -- run <suite>"><pre>kujo run main.kujo -- run <span class="pl-k"><</span>suite<span class="pl-k">></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Current recommended default is VM-first execution:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run main.kujo run <suite>"><pre>kujo run main.kujo run <span class="pl-k"><</span>suite<span class="pl-k">></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Use <code>--interpreter</code> only for runtime compatibility checks, warning investigations, or parity debugging.</p>
<p dir="auto">Migration mapping:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Legacy: <code>kujo run main.kujo --interpreter <command></code></li>
<li>Preferred: <code>kujo run main.kujo <command></code></li>
<li>Optional compatibility check: <code>kujo run main.kujo --interpreter <command></code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Interpreter mode can emit KUJORUN001 warning noise while still succeeding; rely on exit code plus generated artifacts (<code>summary.json</code>, <code>evaluation-result.json</code>, <code>artifact-manifest.json</code>) for CI pass/fail decisions.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Known Runtime Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-known-runtime-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Known Runtime Limitations" href="#known-runtime-limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Interpreter mode may print KUJORUN001 type-check warnings even when commands exit successfully.</li>
<li>Command checks support native process timeout termination through <code>timeout_ms</code> and suite-level <code>timeout_seconds</code>.</li>
<li><code>watch</code> is intentionally long-running and should be interrupted manually in local shells.</li>
<li>Command and file checks run in the host environment and are not a full sandbox boundary.</li>
<li>Some interpreter invocations can stall when stdout/stderr is shell-captured; release/parity gate scripts mitigate this with artifact-driven watchdogs.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Launch Scope Snapshot</h2><a id="user-content-launch-scope-snapshot" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Launch Scope Snapshot" href="#launch-scope-snapshot"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Eval is verified for deterministic local and CI evaluation workflows where shell/file access is expected and controlled by repository policy.</p>
<p dir="auto">It is not yet a universal fit for every enterprise testing context. Before broad rollout, evaluate the following constraints for your environment:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Timeout enforcement depends on runtime support for <code>execute_status</code> timeout handling in your target Kujo build.</li>
<li>No isolated sandbox boundary; commands execute with host-level permissions.</li>
<li>Runtime warning noise in interpreter mode may require log filtering in strict observability pipelines.</li>
<li>Feature roadmap items (LLM-as-judge, model-cost scoring, distributed execution) are intentionally out of current deterministic scope.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">If your use case needs strict isolation, guaranteed process preemption, or non-local execution controls, place Eval behind additional platform controls (container boundaries, workload policies, and external supervisors).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Enterprise Deployment Patterns</h2><a id="user-content-enterprise-deployment-patterns" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Enterprise Deployment Patterns" href="#enterprise-deployment-patterns"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Eval can be deployed in enterprise CI/CD and platform workflows with a simple layered model:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Runner boundary</strong>: execute eval jobs in short-lived containers or isolated runners with least-privilege filesystem mounts.</li>
<li><strong>Command policy</strong>: define <code>allowed_commands</code>, <code>allowed_command_patterns</code>, and <code>blocked_arg_patterns</code> at suite level; override only where needed at test level.</li>
<li><strong>Path policy</strong>: scope file assertions using <code>allowed_paths</code> to explicitly owned workspace directories.</li>
<li><strong>Environment policy</strong>: expose only approved variables and enforce with <code>allowed_env_vars</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Artifact policy</strong>: keep report outputs (<code>--output-dir</code>) in per-run isolated folders and publish only required formats (JSON/JUnit/TAP/HTML/NDJSON).</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Suggested rollout:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Start with <code>--json --quiet</code> in CI to establish deterministic pass/fail gates.</li>
<li>Add JUnit/TAP report publication for existing enterprise test dashboards.</li>
<li>Enforce suite-level command/path/env policy defaults before allowing per-test overrides.</li>
<li>Add external supervision for hard-kill guarantees on long-running processes until native runtime preemption support is available.</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">Eval fills a gap: it's a <strong>deterministic, zero-dependency, AI-native evaluation framework</strong> that tests outcomes (commands, files, JSON, HTTP) rather than code units. It's designed for agents, CLIs, and workflow outputs — not traditional unit tests.</p>

<p dir="auto">The implementation lives in <code>src/</code>; the root stays intentionally small and runtime-facing:</p>

<p dir="auto">Root copies of <code>README.md</code>, <code>SECURITY.md</code>, <code>CONTRIBUTING.md</code>, <code>LICENSE</code>, package manifests, <code>Dockerfile</code>, and <code>RUNTIME_VERSION</code> are kept for GitHub/package-manager conventions. Generated outputs such as <code>eval_results/</code>, <code>.eval_*</code>, <code>snapshots/</code>, and <code>tests/*.out</code> are ignored.</p>

<p dir="auto">Named path-policy profiles reduce boilerplate for staged hardening:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Profile</th>
<th>Effect</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>open</code></td>
<td>Leaves path policy open; use only for local exploration or externally sandboxed runs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>ci-restricted</code></td>
<td>Enables <code>allowlist-required</code> and permits common repository-owned docs, schema, examples, source, and tests paths.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>release-deny-default</code></td>
<td>Enables <code>allowlist-required</code> with a narrow release artifact/fixture/schema allowlist; add explicit <code>allowed_paths</code> for anything else.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Profiles can be set as top-level <code>path_policy_profile</code> defaults or inside <code>policy_stage_overlays.<stage>.path_policy_profile</code>; explicit <code>path_policy_mode</code> and <code>allowed_paths</code> override profile defaults.</p>

<p dir="auto">Run/report outputs now include:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>summary.json</code>: compact deterministic run summary for dashboards/status collectors</li>
<li><code>evaluation-result.json</code>: <code>kujo.evaluation-result/v1</code> verdict, severity,
subject, counts, and integrity-bearing evidence references for generic policy
engines and orchestrators. It does not command pause, retry, or continuation.</li>
<li><code>artifact-manifest.json</code>: deterministic file index for CI artifact discovery</li>
<li><code>cli-summary.json</code>: stable machine handoff channel for run/report command outcomes</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">When checksum mode is enabled (<code>artifact_checksums: true</code> or <code>--artifact-checksums</code>), <code>artifact-manifest.json</code> also includes a <code>checksums</code> block with SHA-256 digests. Validate it with:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kujo run main.kujo verify-manifest --output-dir ./eval_results --json"><pre>kujo run main.kujo verify-manifest --output-dir ./eval_results --json</pre></div>

<p dir="auto">Eval currently uses explicit process exit classes:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th align="right">Exit Code</th>
<th>Class</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td align="right"><code>0</code></td>
<td>Success</td>
<td>Command completed successfully (for <code>run</code>, all assertions passed).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td align="right"><code>1</code></td>
<td>Assertion failure</td>
<td>At least one eval assertion failed during <code>run</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td align="right"><code>1</code></td>
<td>Usage/config/runtime error</td>
<td>Invalid command usage, missing/invalid config, or command execution error.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto">Practical CI guidance:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Treat any non-zero exit as a hard failure gate.</li>
<li>Parse <code>--json</code> envelopes to distinguish assertion failures from usage/config/runtime failures.</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Flaky Test Retry</h2><a id="user-content-flaky-test-retry" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Flaky Test Retry" href="#flaky-test-retry"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Add a <code>"retry"</code> field to any test definition to automatically retry on failure:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "name": "flaky network check",
  "check": "http_status",
  "params": { "url": "https://api.example.com/health" },
  "retry": 2
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"name"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>flaky network check<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"check"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>http_status<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"params"</span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://api.example.com/health<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> },
  <span class="pl-ent">"retry"</span>: <span class="pl-c1">2</span>
}</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The test will run up to 3 times (1 initial + 2 retries) and pass if any attempt succeeds.</p>

100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWorkcell 1.3 is a stable local and CI execution harness for bounded Kujo and agent workflows on Docker or Podman. It creates a disposable Git worktree, validates a declarative execution definition, applies bounded container resources and filesystem access, enforces an explicit network policy, exports only declared artifacts, records a structured receipt and integrity manifest, and performs ownership-scoped cleanup.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe repository also contains an additive alpha provider-neutral contract: \u003ccode\u003eworkcell-definition/v2alpha1\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eworkcell-backend/v1alpha1\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eworkcell-receipt/v2alpha1\u003c/code\u003e. Docker and Podman implement that contract through the existing stable OCI lifecycle. Digest-pinned external adapters for E2B, Vercel Sandbox, and Daytona are separately installed, strictly capability-negotiated, ownership-recoverable, and receipt-visible. gVisor and Kata are OCI runtime selections, not provider adapters. Offline conformance is not live-provider or security certification. See \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/backend-adapters.md\"\u003ebackend adapters\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe container boundary defines what is physically reachable. Kujo defines what is authorized, observable, verifiable, and exportable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe v1 guarantee is deliberately narrow. It covers the local Docker/Podman CLI, definition, receipt, verification, artifact, cleanup, and recovery contracts documented in this repository. and cleanup results. It records secret names but never intentionally stores secret values. \u003ccode\u003eworkcell verify\u003c/code\u003e detects changes to immutable evidence.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFailed-run preservation emits \u003ccode\u003ekujo.preservation-outcome/v1\u003c/code\u003e. The outcome\nseparates requested from actual mode, names the provider and cleanup owner, and\nstates reconstructability and limitations. \u003ccode\u003e--keep-failed\u003c/code\u003e maps to\n\u003ccode\u003efilesystem\u003c/code\u003e; \u003ccode\u003e--preservation-mode handoff_bundle\u003c/code\u003e writes a clean-source-plus-\npatch handoff manifest. Snapshot and live-pause requests report unsupported\nunless a backend supplies them. \u003ccode\u003e--retain-until\u003c/code\u003e records an operator-owned UTC\ndeadline; it does not claim provider-side erasure.\nAfter the deadline, an operator can run \u003ccode\u003eworkcell clean --preservation \u0026lt;preservation.json\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e; Workcell revalidates the exact ownership marker and writes\na separate deletion receipt outside the immutable run manifest. \u003ccode\u003e--dry-run\u003c/code\u003e\npreviews the exact target. Remote/provider deletion continues through the\nprovider recovery contract, not this local-filesystem command.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery non-dry execution also emits \u003ccode\u003ekujo.execution-result/v1\u003c/code\u003e plus a\n\u003ccode\u003ekujo.reexecution-descriptor/v1\u003c/code\u003e. The descriptor retains normalized inputs and\nsecret references, never secret values. Workcell promises inspectability and,\nwhen source and inputs are present, a new re-execution attempt. It does not\npromise deterministic replay. Network-enabled runs record external effects as\nunknown and require operator policy before retry.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePortable runs use receipt v2. Its controls ledger distinguishes requested, accepted, enforced or provider-claimed, observed, unsupported, and unknown state. A provider name or marketing claim never upgrades an enforcement Only declared artifacts leave the workspace.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNetwork access must be explicit. Workcell records the egress declaration but does not install firewalls, control DNS, or force arbitrary child processes through a proxy. For release deployments, use reviewed image digests, signature keys, registry allowlists, and host-enforced egress where required.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eContainers are not universal isolation. Workcell trusts the selected engine and host kernel. Higher-risk or multi-tenant workloads need an operator-provided VM, gVisor/Kata class runtime, microVM service, or equivalent stronger boundary. Workcell","","Experimental Wave C beta (opt-in, bounded single-effect required/deny; alpha retained): [normative assurance profile](docs/contracts/git-assurance-profile.md) and portable commitment vectors now define the existing local predicate for alpha and opt-in beta envelopes. No stable execution contract or default admission changes.","","","Experimental addition: [local Git effect assurance prototype](docs/effect-assurance-prototype.md), separate from stable execution and preservation.","","[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.3.0-black)](https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/releases/tag/v1.3.0)","[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)](LICENSE)","[![built with Kujo](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Kujo-white.svg)](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo)","[![CI](https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/actions/workflows/ci.yml)","","Workcell 1.3 is a stable local and CI execution harness for bounded Kujo and agent workflows on Docker or Podman. It creates a disposable Git worktree, validates a declarative execution definition, applies bounded container resources and filesystem access, enforces an explicit network policy, exports only declared artifacts, records a structured receipt and integrity manifest, and performs ownership-scoped cleanup.","","The repository also contains an additive alpha provider-neutral contract: `workcell-definition/v2alpha1`, `workcell-backend/v1alpha1`, and `workcell-receipt/v2alpha1`. Docker and Podman implement that contract through the existing stable OCI lifecycle. Digest-pinned external adapters for E2B, Vercel Sandbox, and Daytona are separately installed, strictly capability-negotiated, ownership-recoverable, and receipt-visible. gVisor and Kata are OCI runtime selections, not provider adapters. Offline conformance is not live-provider or security certification. See [backend adapters](docs/backend-adapters.md).","","\u003e The container boundary defines what is physically reachable. Kujo defines what is authorized, observable, verifiable, and exportable.","","The v1 guarantee is deliberately narrow. It covers the local Docker/Podman CLI, definition, receipt, verification, artifact, cleanup, and recovery contracts documented in this repository. It does not protect against a compromised daemon or host kernel, provide microVM isolation or hosted multi-tenant execution, provision organization-specific egress infrastructure, govern operator images or signing keys, set retention policy, or confer compliance or enterprise certification.","","## Supported contract","","Workcell 1.3 supports:","","- disposable Git worktrees and isolated-clone workspaces from clean repositories;","- strict, versioned JSON definitions with safe defaults and unknown-field rejection;","- Docker and Podman execution with bounded CPU, memory, PIDs, time, output, mounts, and writable paths;","- explicit `none`, `default`, or pre-created `custom` network selection plus a recorded egress declaration;","- declared artifact export, structured receipts, SHA-256 integrity manifests, and offline verification;","- label-scoped container cleanup, ownership-marked workspace cleanup, timeout recovery, and explicit failed-workspace preservation.","","Supported host classes are Linux with Docker Engine or rootless Docker/Podman, and macOS with Docker Desktop or Colima. Windows and unsupported Unix hosts are outside v1. Run `workcell doctor` on every target host; host file sharing, user namespaces, seccomp/AppArmor, DNS, proxy, and firewall behavior remain deployment-specific. See [platform compatibility](docs/compatibility.md).","","## Requirements and installation","","- Kujo 1.6.0 at commit `44af277848173664f72ca85f2a1b3b98d634ecdd` (the exact pin is in `RUNTIME_VERSION`).","- Git and `jq`.","- Docker for the default backend, or Podman on a supported Linux host.","- A clean Git source repository for execution. Workcell refuses dirty sources by default so it cannot silently omit user changes.","","Workcell is distributed as a source archive and can also run directly from a checkout:","","```bash","git clone https://github.com/kujolang/workcell.git","cd workcell","git checkout v1.3.0","export KUJO=/path/to/kujo-1.6.0/kujo","./bin/workcell --version","```","","The `v1.3.0` tag contains the stable source release. Its Docker and Podman lifecycle remains the stable contract. The provider-neutral definitions, backend protocol, portable receipts, and remote adapters included in the source remain alpha until each provider passes live certification. The launcher reads `KUJO` and does not download or replace the runtime.","","## Quick Start","","```bash","export KUJO=/path/to/kujo-1.6.0/kujo","docker build --tag kujolang/workcell-base:local docker/","./bin/workcell init","./bin/workcell validate --file workcell.json","./bin/workcell inspect --file workcell.json --json","./bin/workcell run --file workcell.json --repo . --no-pull","./bin/workcell verify --run .workcell/runs/\u003crun-id\u003e --json","```","","Agent hosts can use `workcell run ... --summary` for one compact `workcell-run-summary/v1` JSON object containing the verdict and evidence paths without embedding the full receipt. The receipt and integrity manifest remain authoritative.","","`workcell init` creates a restrictive starter definition. `inspect` resolves policy without starting a container. `run` creates a temporary Git workspace and writes evidence under `.workcell/runs/\u003crun-id\u003e/`. For Podman, set `runtime.backend` to `podman` and follow the identity guidance in [platform compatibility](docs/compatibility.md).","","## Portable backend quick start","","The v2 workload stays provider-neutral; the host profile selects compute. This example resolves through built-in Docker without installing an adapter:","","```bash","./bin/workcell validate --file examples/portable/workcell.json","./bin/workcell inspect \\","  --file examples/portable/workcell.json \\","  --profiles examples/portable/host-profiles.json \\","  --profile docker \\","  --summary","./bin/workcell run \\","  --file examples/portable/workcell.json \\","  --repo . \\","  --profiles examples/portable/host-profiles.json \\","  --profile docker \\","  --summary","```","","Switching profiles changes the provider, not the workload contract. Remote profiles and explicit adapter manifests are documented in [backend adapters](docs/backend-adapters.md). Unsupported security or resource requirements fail before provisioning; Workcell never silently substitutes provider defaults.","","## Agent-efficient interface","","Agents should use `inspect --summary` for a compact preflight and `run --summary` for the verdict and evidence pointers. These emit single-line `workcell-inspect-summary/v1` and `workcell-run-summary/v1` objects without commands, mounts, secrets, full capability ledgers, logs, or embedded receipts. Read `receipt.json` only when detailed evidence is needed, and use `verify --json` before trusting persisted evidence. Pass correlation through a bounded `workcell-caller-context/v1` file with `--context`; never put credentials or provider options in caller context.","","## Stable CLI surface","","| Command | Contract |","| --- | --- |","| `doctor` | Check Kujo, Git, selected backend, engine security signals, repository, temp directory, and dangerous environment overrides. |","| `init` | Create a starter `workcell.json`; refuse overwrite unless `--force` is explicit. |","| `validate` | Parse and validate a definition; `--schema` emits `workcell-definition/v1`. |","| `inspect` | Render resolved mounts, resources, environment names, backend, and security arguments without execution. |","| `run` | Execute validate, prepare, launch, collect, verify, export, record, and clean. |","| `verify` | Verify a run directory's `workcell-manifest/v1` hashes offline. |","| `clean` | Inventory or remove only Workcell-owned containers and workspaces; images require `--prune-images`. |","| `backends` | List built-ins and explicitly supplied external adapter manifests. |","| `recover` | Reconcile a durable external-backend journal without deleting resources whose ownership does not match. |","","Global `--help` and `--version` are stable. Command-specific options and unexpected positional arguments fail with usage code `2`. The machine-readable CLI and exit-code contract is available from `workcell help --json`.","","## Output and exit codes","","Each completed lifecycle writes the applicable evidence:","","```text",".workcell/runs/\u003crun-id\u003e/","├── receipt.json","├── stdout.log","├── stderr.log","├── integrations/","├── changes.patch","├── changes.json","├── manifest.json","├── preservation.json","├── handoff-bundle.json (when requested and reconstructable)","├── execution-result.json","├── reexecution.json","├── reexecution-input.json","└── artifacts/","```","","The receipt separates Workcell product version, definition version, execution, verification, artifact export, and cleanup results. It records secret names but never intentionally stores secret values. `workcell verify` detects changes to immutable evidence.","","Failed-run preservation emits `kujo.preservation-outcome/v1`. The outcome","separates requested from actual mode, names the provider and cleanup owner, and","states reconstructability and limitations. `--keep-failed` maps to","`filesystem`; `--preservation-mode handoff_bundle` writes a clean-source-plus-","patch handoff manifest. Snapshot and live-pause requests report unsupported","unless a backend supplies them. `--retain-until` records an operator-owned UTC","deadline; it does not claim provider-side erasure.","After the deadline, an operator can run `workcell clean --preservation","\u003cpreservation.json\u003e`; Workcell revalidates the exact ownership marker and writes","a separate deletion receipt outside the immutable run manifest. `--dry-run`","previews the exact target. Remote/provider deletion continues through the","provider recovery contract, not this local-filesystem command.","","Every non-dry execution also emits `kujo.execution-result/v1` plus a","`kujo.reexecution-descriptor/v1`. The descriptor retains normalized inputs and","secret references, never secret values. Workcell promises inspectability and,","when source and inputs are present, a new re-execution attempt. It does not","promise deterministic replay. Network-enabled runs record external effects as","unknown and require operator policy before retry.","","Portable runs use receipt v2. Its controls ledger distinguishes requested, accepted, enforced or provider-claimed, observed, unsupported, and unknown state. A provider name or marketing claim never upgrades an enforcement status.","","| Exit | Meaning |","| --- | --- |","| `0` | Completed successfully. |","| `2` | Usage or definition validation failure. |","| `3` | Git/source dependency or workspace preparation failure. |","| `4` | Backend or image preparation failure. |","| `5` | Container startup failure. |","| `6` | Timeout. |","| `7` | Workload command failure. |","| `8` | Verification or artifact export failure. |","| `9` | Cleanup failure. |","| `10` | Internal Workcell failure. |","","The workload's own exit code remains in `receipt.json`; the Workcell exit code identifies the lifecycle category.","","## Security posture","","The default `contained-standard` profile uses network `none`, a non-root or rootless-mapped identity, a read-only root filesystem, bounded resources, `no-new-privileges`, dropped Linux capabilities, private IPC, no devices or host namespaces, no daemon socket, explicit environment passing, and one disposable workspace mount. Only declared artifacts leave the workspace.","","Network access must be explicit. Workcell records the egress declaration but does not install firewalls, control DNS, or force arbitrary child processes through a proxy. For release deployments, use reviewed image digests, signature keys, registry allowlists, and host-enforced egress where required.","","Containers are not universal isolation. Workcell trusts the selected engine and host kernel. Higher-risk or multi-tenant workloads need an operator-provided VM, gVisor/Kata class runtime, microVM service, or equivalent stronger boundary. Read the [security model](docs/security-model.md), [enterprise deployment boundary](docs/enterprise-deployment.md), and [known limitations](docs/known-limitations.md) before deployment.","","## Compatibility and upgrades","","Workcell follows semantic versioning for the product. The `workcell-definition/v1`, `workcell-cli/v1`, `workcell-receipt/v1`, `workcell-manifest/v1`, and other evidence identifiers are independent contract versions; product 1.3.0 does not rename them. Additive fields may appear within a v1 contract. Removing or repurposing a field or exit code requires a new contract identifier and migration notes.","","Patch releases contain compatible fixes. Minor releases may add optional CLI or schema surface with safe defaults. A future product major may change supported contracts only with changelog and migration guidance. Pin both the Workcell release and Kujo runtime commit for reproducible automation. See the [API compatibility policy](docs/api-compatibility.md).","","## Verification","","Run the offline release gates with the pinned runtime:","","```bash","export KUJO=/path/to/kujo-1.6.0/kujo","./bin/workcell --help","./bin/workcell --version","./bin/workcell validate --file workcell.json","KUJO=\"$KUJO\" ./tests/version_consistency.sh","KUJO=\"$KUJO\" ./tests/run.sh","KUJO=\"$KUJO\" ./tests/quality.sh","KUJO=\"$KUJO\" ./tests/release_report.sh","./tests/markdown_links.sh","git diff --check","```","","For an explicitly selected source-runtime compatibility run, set","`WORKCELL_TEST_KUJO_VERSION=1.5.0` alongside `KUJO` when invoking the tests.","The override checks that exact reported version; it does not change","`RUNTIME_VERSION`, Docker pins, or certify a release on that runtime. Release","validation must leave the override unset.","","Docker and Podman integration, concurrent-load, egress, doctor, cleanup, self-proof, receipt verification, and ShipCheck commands are documented in [development](docs/development.md) and the [release process](docs/release-process.md).","","## Release and support boundary","","GitHub source archives and the versioned source archive, checksums, provenance record, and release report produced by the tag workflow are the supported v1 release artifacts. The workflow publishes no container image, hosted runner, package registry entry, or hosted execution service. Target-host hardening, image governance, key custody, evidence retention, egress infrastructure, and organization-specific compliance remain operator responsibilities.","","Use [GitHub issues](https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/issues) for reproducible defects in the supported v1 contract. Security reports follow the private process in [the security model](docs/security-model.md). <p dir="auto">Experimental Wave C beta (opt-in, bounded single-effect required/deny; alpha retained): <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/contracts/git-assurance-profile.md">normative assurance profile</a> and portable commitment vectors now define the existing local predicate for alpha and opt-in beta envelopes. No stable execution contract or default admission changes.</p>
<p dir="auto">Experimental addition: <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/effect-assurance-prototype.md">local Git effect assurance prototype</a>, separate from stable execution and preservation.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/releases/tag/v1.3.0"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/7db44223615c230105f717c3bd2d41c34841bdb5a58be3aff570568a88a45f6a/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f76657273696f6e2d312e332e302d626c61636b" alt="Version" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.3.0-black" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>
