<a href="https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/actions/workflows/ci.yml"><img src="https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg" alt="CI" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto">Workcell 1.3 is a stable local and CI execution harness for bounded Kujo and agent workflows on Docker or Podman. It creates a disposable Git worktree, validates a declarative execution definition, applies bounded container resources and filesystem access, enforces an explicit network policy, exports only declared artifacts, records a structured receipt and integrity manifest, and performs ownership-scoped cleanup.</p>
<p dir="auto">The repository also contains an additive alpha provider-neutral contract: <code>workcell-definition/v2alpha1</code>, <code>workcell-backend/v1alpha1</code>, and <code>workcell-receipt/v2alpha1</code>. Docker and Podman implement that contract through the existing stable OCI lifecycle. Digest-pinned external adapters for E2B, Vercel Sandbox, and Daytona are separately installed, strictly capability-negotiated, ownership-recoverable, and receipt-visible. gVisor and Kata are OCI runtime selections, not provider adapters. Offline conformance is not live-provider or security certification. See <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/backend-adapters.md">backend adapters</a>.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The container boundary defines what is physically reachable. Kujo defines what is authorized, observable, verifiable, and exportable.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The v1 guarantee is deliberately narrow. It covers the local Docker/Podman CLI, definition, receipt, verification, artifact, cleanup, and recovery contracts documented in this repository. It does not protect against a compromised daemon or host kernel, provide microVM isolation or hosted multi-tenant execution, provision organization-specific egress infrastructure, govern operator images or signing keys, set retention policy, or confer compliance or enterprise certification.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Supported contract</h2><a id="user-content-supported-contract" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Supported contract" href="#supported-contract"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Workcell 1.3 supports:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>disposable Git worktrees and isolated-clone workspaces from clean repositories;</li>
<li>strict, versioned JSON definitions with safe defaults and unknown-field rejection;</li>
<li>Docker and Podman execution with bounded CPU, memory, PIDs, time, output, mounts, and writable paths;</li>
<li>explicit <code>none</code>, <code>default</code>, or pre-created <code>custom</code> network selection plus a recorded egress declaration;</li>
<li>declared artifact export, structured receipts, SHA-256 integrity manifests, and offline verification;</li>
<li>label-scoped container cleanup, ownership-marked workspace cleanup, timeout recovery, and explicit failed-workspace preservation.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Supported host classes are Linux with Docker Engine or rootless Docker/Podman, and macOS with Docker Desktop or Colima. Windows and unsupported Unix hosts are outside v1. Run <code>workcell doctor</code> on every target host; host file sharing, user namespaces, seccomp/AppArmor, DNS, proxy, and firewall behavior remain deployment-specific. See <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/compatibility.md">platform compatibility</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Requirements and installation</h2><a id="user-content-requirements-and-installation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Requirements and installation" href="#requirements-and-installation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Kujo 1.6.0 at commit <code>44af277848173664f72ca85f2a1b3b98d634ecdd</code> (the exact pin is in <code>RUNTIME_VERSION</code>).</li>
<li>Git and <code>jq</code>.</li>
<li>Docker for the default backend, or Podman on a supported Linux host.</li>
<li>A clean Git source repository for execution. Workcell refuses dirty sources by default so it cannot silently omit user changes.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Workcell is distributed as a source archive and can also run directly from a checkout:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="git clone https://github.com/kujolang/workcell.git

git checkout v1.3.0
export KUJO=/path/to/kujo-1.6.0/kujo

<p dir="auto">The <code>v1.3.0</code> tag contains the stable source release. Its Docker and Podman lifecycle remains the stable contract. The provider-neutral definitions, backend protocol, portable receipts, and remote adapters included in the source remain alpha until each provider passes live certification. The launcher reads <code>KUJO</code> and does not download or replace the runtime.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick Start</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick Start" href="#quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">Agent hosts can use <code>workcell run ... --summary</code> for one compact <code>workcell-run-summary/v1</code> JSON object containing the verdict and evidence paths without embedding the full receipt. The receipt and integrity manifest remain authoritative.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>workcell init</code> creates a restrictive starter definition. <code>inspect</code> resolves policy without starting a container. <code>run</code> creates a temporary Git workspace and writes evidence under <code>.workcell/runs/<run-id>/</code>. For Podman, set <code>runtime.backend</code> to <code>podman</code> and follow the identity guidance in <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/compatibility.md">platform compatibility</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Portable backend quick start</h2><a id="user-content-portable-backend-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Portable backend quick start" href="#portable-backend-quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">Agents should use <code>inspect --summary</code> for a compact preflight and <code>run --summary</code> for the verdict and evidence pointers. These emit single-line <code>workcell-inspect-summary/v1</code> and <code>workcell-run-summary/v1</code> objects without commands, mounts, secrets, full capability ledgers, logs, or embedded receipts. Read <code>receipt.json</code> only when detailed evidence is needed, and use <code>verify --json</code> before trusting persisted evidence. <p dir="auto">Each completed lifecycle writes the applicable evidence:</p>

<p dir="auto">The receipt separates Workcell product version, definition version, execution, verification, artifact export, and cleanup results. It records secret names but never intentionally stores secret values. <code>workcell verify</code> detects changes to immutable evidence.</p>
<p dir="auto">Failed-run preservation emits <code>kujo.preservation-outcome/v1</code>. The outcome
separates requested from actual mode, names the provider and cleanup owner, and
states reconstructability and limitations. <code>--keep-failed</code> maps to
<code>filesystem</code>; <code>--preservation-mode handoff_bundle</code> writes a clean-source-plus-
patch handoff manifest. Snapshot and live-pause requests report unsupported
unless a backend supplies them. <code>--retain-until</code> records an operator-owned UTC
deadline; it does not claim provider-side erasure.
After the deadline, an operator can run <code>workcell clean --preservation <preservation.json></code>; Workcell revalidates the exact ownership marker and writes
a separate deletion receipt outside the immutable run manifest. <code>--dry-run</code>
previews the exact target. Remote/provider deletion continues through the
provider recovery contract, not this local-filesystem command.</p>
<p dir="auto">Every non-dry execution also emits <code>kujo.execution-result/v1</code> plus a
<code>kujo.reexecution-descriptor/v1</code>. The descriptor retains normalized inputs and
secret references, never secret values. Workcell promises inspectability and,
when source and inputs are present, a new re-execution attempt. It does not
promise deterministic replay. Network-enabled runs record external effects as
unknown and require operator policy before retry.</p>
<p dir="auto">Portable runs use receipt v2. Its controls ledger distinguishes requested, accepted, enforced or provider-claimed, observed, unsupported, and unknown state. A provider name or marketing claim never upgrades an enforcement status.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security posture</h2><a id="user-content-security-posture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security posture" href="#security-posture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The default <code>contained-standard</code> profile uses network <code>none</code>, a non-root or rootless-mapped identity, a read-only root filesystem, bounded resources, <code>no-new-privileges</code>, dropped Linux capabilities, private IPC, no devices or host namespaces, no daemon socket, explicit environment passing, and one disposable workspace mount. Only declared artifacts leave the workspace.</p>
<p dir="auto">Network access must be explicit. Workcell records the egress declaration but does not install firewalls, control DNS, or force arbitrary child processes through a proxy. For release deployments, use reviewed image digests, signature keys, registry allowlists, and host-enforced egress where required.</p>
<p dir="auto">Containers are not universal isolation. Workcell trusts the selected engine and host kernel. Higher-risk or multi-tenant workloads need an operator-provided VM, gVisor/Kata class runtime, microVM service, or equivalent stronger boundary. Read the <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/security-model.md">security model</a>, <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/enterprise-deployment.md">enterprise deployment boundary</a>, and <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/known-limitations.md">known limitations</a> before deployment.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Compatibility and upgrades</h2><a id="user-content-compatibility-and-upgrades" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Compatibility and upgrades" href="#compatibility-and-upgrades"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Workcell follows semantic versioning for the product. The <code>workcell-definition/v1</code>, <code>workcell-cli/v1</code>, <code>workcell-receipt/v1</code>, <code>workcell-manifest/v1</code>, and other evidence identifiers are independent contract versions; product 1.3.0 does not rename them. Additive fields may appear within a v1 contract. Removing or repurposing a field or exit code requires a new contract identifier and migration notes.</p>
<p dir="auto">Patch releases contain compatible fixes. Minor releases may add optional CLI or schema surface with safe defaults. A future product major may change supported contracts only with changelog and migration guidance. Pin both the Workcell release and Kujo runtime commit for reproducible automation. See the <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/api-compatibility.md">API compatibility policy</a>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Verification</h2><a id="user-content-verification" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Verification" href="#verification"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Release and support boundary</h2><a id="user-content-release-and-support-boundary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Release and support boundary" href="#release-and-support-boundary"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">GitHub source archives and the versioned source archive, checksums, provenance record, and release report produced by the tag workflow are the supported v1 release artifacts. The workflow publishes no container image, hosted runner, package registry entry, or hosted execution service. Target-host hardening, image governance, key custody, evidence retention, egress infrastructure, and organization-specific compliance remain operator responsibilities.</p>
<p dir="auto">Use <a href="https://github.com/kujolang/workcell/issues">GitHub issues</a> for reproducible defects in the supported v1 contract. Security reports follow the private process in <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/security-model.md">the security model</a>. The exact pre-tag and rollback procedures are in <a href="/kujolang/workcell/blob/189d7ab6e975301a0e5100b65e8ad3fe4a584573/docs/release-process.md">the release process</a>.</p>

The current implementation\nprioritizes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003elocal JSON storage with no network calls and no provider API keys,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eread-only git metadata collection,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eatomic writes for run files and generated reports,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eexplicit exit codes for automation,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003edefensive loading of partial or malformed run files,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003esafe run-id handling so user-supplied IDs cannot escape the ledger directory,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eper-record ownership locks for conflict-safe concurrent mutations,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emarkdown report output that stays stable when user text contains table\npunctuation.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis is not a universal enterprise-readiness certification: shared-ledger\nauthorization, efficient full-history reports at very large scales, and a\nformal security review remain open. through\n\u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;ledger\u0026gt;/locks/\u0026lt;run-id\u0026gt;.lock\u003c/code\u003e. Writers targeting different receipts remain\nindependent. Concurrent \u003ccode\u003estart\u003c/code\u003e commands atomically retry ID allocation when\nthey select the same candidate. Read-only commands do not acquire locks.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA writer waits up to 10 seconds by default. Set\n\u003ccode\u003eRUNLEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS\u003c/code\u003e to an integer from \u003ccode\u003e10\u003c/code\u003e through \u003ccode\u003e60000\u003c/code\u003e to choose a\ndifferent bound. A timeout exits 1 and names the exact lock file; it never\nremoves a lock owned by another process. Cost is \u003cstrong\u003emanual\u003c/strong\u003e: you supply\n\u003ccode\u003e--total\u003c/code\u003e (and optionally per-segment \u003ccode\u003e--input\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--output\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003e--cache\u003c/code\u003e costs\nand a \u003ccode\u003e--currency\u003c/code\u003e). This keeps the tool honest and provider-agnostic; pricing\ntables change constantly and don't belong baked into a receipt system.\nReports aggregate recorded costs per currency; unlike currencies are never\ncombined into a dimensionally invalid grand total.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eGit metadata\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-git-metadata\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Git metadata\" href=\"#git-metadata\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen \u003ccode\u003e--repo\u003c/code\u003e points inside a git repository, RunLedger records the start/end\ncommit, dirty state, and changed files using \u003cstrong\u003eread-only\u003c/strong\u003e git commands only\n(\u003ccode\u003erev-parse\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estatus --porcelain\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ediff --name-only\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003els-files\u003c/code\u003e). It never\nstages, commits, resets, checks out, or otherwise mutates git state. If git is\nabsent or the path isn't a repo, those fields are recorded as \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e/empty and\nthe command still succeeds.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eChanges committed after \u003ccode\u003estart\u003c/code\u003e count even when the worktree is clean at\n\u003ccode\u003efinish\u003c/code\u003e. The recorded file set also includes any changes still uncommitted at\nfinish. Git pathnames use NUL-delimited output to preserve embedded whitespace,\nquotes, and Unicode. These are repository observations, not proof that a\nparticular agent authored every change.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" \u003ccode\u003epartial\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003efail\u003c/code\u003e, or\n\u003ccode\u003eabandoned\u003c/code\u003e) and a non-empty pass\u003c/code\u003e means the operator reported a pass.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe launcher needs a \u003ccode\u003ekujo\u003c/code\u003e binary (via \u003ccode\u003eKUJO\u003c/code\u003e or your \u003ccode\u003ePATH\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRun files are plain JSON; editing them by hand is supported. RunLedger","","[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.2.1-black)](https://github.com/kujolang/runledger)","[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)](LICENSE)","[![built with Kujo](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Kujo-white.svg)](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo)","","A local ledger for AI-agent build runs.","","When you hand several agents (Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, a local model, a future","Kujo-native agent) the same prompt and ask them to build the same thing,","RunLedger gives you a repeatable, inspectable **receipt** for each attempt: what","model ran, against which repo and commit, what files changed, optional","token/cost data you recorded, manually recorded commands and test results,","your verdict, and the follow-ups needed.","","It is built in the Kujo language runtime and stores everything as plain JSON on","your local disk. No database, no network, no API key.","","## What RunLedger is — and is not","","RunLedger **is** a structured receipt system for agent work. It records and","compares runs so you can answer questions like:","","- Which model followed the prompt best?","- Which run changed the fewest files?","- Which run did I record as passing its tests?","- Which run needed the fewest follow-up fixes?","- Which run was most expensive?","- Which run produced the cleanest handoff?","","RunLedger is deliberately **not**:","","- a deep automated code reviewer,","- an Eval runner or benchmark judge,","- a Scout replacement,","- a ShipCheck replacement,","- a Trail replacement,","- a prompt manager or workflow-pack validator.","","It does not try to judge code quality. It records facts you give it plus a few","read-only git facts, and presents them back clearly.","","## Readiness posture","","RunLedger is intentionally small, local-first, and automation-friendly. It is","ready to use as a practical agent-run receipt ledger, but \"enterprise grade\" is","an ongoing standard rather than a one-time label. The current implementation","prioritizes:","","- local JSON storage with no network calls and no provider API keys,","- read-only git metadata collection,","- atomic writes for run files and generated reports,","- explicit exit codes for automation,","- defensive loading of partial or malformed run files,","- safe run-id handling so user-supplied IDs cannot escape the ledger directory,","- per-record ownership locks for conflict-safe concurrent mutations,","- markdown report output that stays stable when user text contains table","  punctuation.","","This is not a universal enterprise-readiness certification: shared-ledger","authorization, efficient full-history reports at very large scales, and a","formal security review remain open. File-ordered pages keep 10,000-receipt","ledgers practical for bounded reads.","See [the next review](docs/reviews/2026-09-22-readiness.md) for scoped evidence","and priorities, and read the [local security model](docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md)","before using receipts with private information. The tool remains a local","receipt store, not a multi-tenant service or an automated judge.","","## Installation","","RunLedger 1.2.1 requires Kujo 1.6.0 or newer. Install with Kennel 1.1.0 or newer:","","```bash","kennel tool install runledger@1.2.1","runledger version","```","","Alternatively, download the `v1.2.1` source release and use its POSIX launcher","or invoke `runledger.kujo` directly. No provider credentials are required.","","### Preflight: verify the right `kujo` binary","","RunLedger requires the Kujo language runtime (the one that supports","`kujo run ...`). Python's linting tool named `kujo` is not compatible.","","```bash","kujo --help","# Expected: help output includes a `run` command.","```","","```bash","# 1. Get this project","cd runledger","","# 2. Confirm Kujo is on your PATH","kujo --version","","# 3. (optional) put the launcher on your PATH","export PATH=\"$PWD/bin:$PATH\"","","# 4. Check it works","runledger version","```","","You can always invoke it directly without the wrapper:","","```bash","kujo run /path/to/runledger/runledger.kujo -- \u003ccommand\u003e [arguments]","```","","\u003e Note the `--`: it separates Kujo's own flags from RunLedger's arguments.","","## Quick start","","```bash","# Start a run (records start commit + dirty state from the repo)","runledger start \\","  --provider anthropic \\","  --model claude-opus-4-8 \\","  --task \"Build Tool X\" \\","  --prompt ./examples/build-tool-x.md \\","  --repo .","","# ... let the agent do its work ...","","# Record token usage and cost (both optional, both manual)","runledger usage \u003crun-id\u003e --input 140000 --output 22000","runledger cost  \u003crun-id\u003e --total 1.18 --currency USD","","# Manually log what you ran and the observed outcome; neither command executes code","runledger command \u003crun-id\u003e \"./tests/run.sh\"","runledger test \u003crun-id\u003e \"module and CLI suites\" --status pass --details \"all checks passed\"","","# Link execution evidence without copying telemetry payloads","runledger correlate \u003crun-id\u003e --watchdog-trace \u003ctrace-id\u003e --dispatch-run \u003crun-id\u003e","","# Add a follow-up you noticed","runledger followup \u003crun-id\u003e \"Add tests for JSON output\"","","# Finish it: status, verdict, and end git state are captured","runledger finish \u003crun-id\u003e --status partial --verdict \"good foundation, needs docs fixes\"","","# Review and report","runledger list","runledger compare","runledger report --output RUNLEDGER_REPORT.md","```","","## Comparing Claude, Codex, and DeepSeek","","Give each agent the same prompt, then record each attempt against the same task","name so they line up in `compare` and `report`. The helper below keeps the","repeated command shape copyable without obscuring the lifecycle steps:","","```bash","TASK=\"Build Tool X\"","PROMPT=\"./examples/build-tool-x.md\"","","start_run() {","  runledger start --provider \"$1\" --model \"$2\" --task \"$TASK\" --prompt \"$PROMPT\" --repo . |","    sed -n '1s/^Started run: //p'","}","","# Claude","id=$(start_run anthropic claude-opus-4-8)","# ...run the agent...","runledger usage \"$id\" --input 140000 --output 22000","runledger cost  \"$id\" --total 1.18","runledger finish \"$id\" --status pass --verdict \"clean handoff\"","","# Codex","id=$(start_run openai codex)","runledger usage \"$id\" --input 190000 --output 26000","runledger cost  \"$id\" --total 0.92","runledger followup \"$id\" \"Add tests for JSON output\"","runledger finish \"$id\" --status partial --verdict \"good start\"","","# DeepSeek","id=$(start_run deepseek deepseek-v3)","runledger usage \"$id\" --input 210000 --output 31000","runledger cost  \"$id\" --total 0.40","runledger finish \"$id\" --status fail --verdict \"tests broken\"","","runledger compare --task \"$TASK\"","runledger report  --task \"$TASK\" --output RUNLEDGER_REPORT.md","```","","## Command reference","","| Command | Description |","|---|---|","| `start` | Create a new run record and capture start git state. |","| `finish \u003crun-id\u003e` | Finalize a run: status, verdict, optional note, end git state. |","| `list` | List recorded runs in a compact table (`--json` for raw). |","| `verify` | Check every run file for malformed/unreadable entries (`--json` for diagnostics). |","| `show \u003crun-id\u003e` | Show one run in readable form (`--json` for the raw record). |","| `note \u003crun-id\u003e \"text\"` | Add a timestamped note. |","| `followup \u003crun-id\u003e \"text\"` | Add a follow-up item. |","| `command \u003crun-id\u003e \"text\"` | Manually record command text without executing it. |","| `test \u003crun-id\u003e \"name\"` | Manually record a `pass`, `fail`, or `skip` test result. |","| `usage \u003crun-id\u003e` | Record token usage. |","| `cost \u003crun-id\u003e` | Record cost (manual, with configurable currency). |","| `correlate \u003crun-id\u003e` | Link Watchdog, Dispatch, Relay, and Eval identifiers without duplicating their records. |","| `compare` | Compare runs (`--task` to filter, `--json` for raw). |","| `report` | Generate a markdown report (`--output \u003cfile\u003e` to save). |","| `help` / `--help` | Show usage. |","| `version` / `--version` | Show the current RunLedger version. |","","### Flags","","- `start`: `--model` `--provider` `--task` (required); `--prompt \u003cfile\u003e` `--repo \u003cpath\u003e` (default `.`) `--ledger \u003cdir\u003e`","- `finish`: `--status \u003cs\u003e` `--verdict \u003ctext\u003e` (required); `--notes \u003ctext\u003e` `--repo \u003cpath\u003e` (defaults to the run's recorded repo)","- `usage`: `--input` `--output` `--cache-read` `--cache-write` (all optional integers)","- `cost`: `--total` `--currency` `--input` `--output` `--cache` (amounts are floats; only provided fields change)","- `correlate`: `--watchdog-trace` `--watchdog-run` `--dispatch-run` `--relay-run` `--eval-run` (bounded identifiers only)","- `test`: `--status \u003cpass|fail|skip\u003e` (required); `--details \u003ctext\u003e` (optional)","- `list` / `compare` / `report`: `--strict` fails on any invalid run file; `--limit \u003c1..1000\u003e` and `--offset \u003cN\u003e` page through sorted run filenames; `list` and `compare` accept `--json`; `report` accepts `--output \u003cfile\u003e`","- `verify`: `--json` emits valid count and a list of `{file, error}` diagnostics","- `compare` / `report`: `--task \u003cname\u003e` to filter results","","For large ledgers, `runledger report --limit 100 --offset 0` and subsequent","pages avoid loading the other run files. The report labels its counts as","page-only. Pagination selects filenames before the optional task filter;","malformed entries within a page are skipped by default, while `--strict`","validates the entire ledger before selecting a page. Use `runledger verify`","to check all files without rendering a full report.","","Command descriptions are limited to 2,000 characters. Test names are limited","to 200 characters and details to 2,000; each run can store at most 1,000","commands and 1,000 test results. These are manual observations, not automatic","test execution or a verified test verdict. Keep secrets out of the receipt.","","Allowed statuses: `in_progress`, `pass`, `partial`, `fail`, `abandoned`. An","invalid status fails with a clear error and a non-zero exit code.","`finish` accepts only terminal statuses: `pass`, `partial`, `fail`, and","`abandoned`.","","### Exit codes","","- `0` success","- `1` operational failure (no such run, invalid status, corrupt file)","- `2` usage error (bad/missing arguments, unknown command, invalid numeric flag value)","","## Concurrent writers","","The mutating commands (`finish`, `note`, `followup`, `command`, `test`, `usage`, `cost`, and `correlate`)","serialize each receipt's complete read-modify-write transaction through","`\u003cledger\u003e/locks/\u003crun-id\u003e.lock`. Writers targeting different receipts remain","independent. Concurrent `start` commands atomically retry ID allocation when","they select the same candidate. Read-only commands do not acquire locks.","","A writer waits up to 10 seconds by default. Set","`RUNLEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` to an integer from `10` through `60000` to choose a","different bound. A timeout exits 1 and names the exact lock file; it never","removes a lock owned by another process. If a process is interrupted while it","owns a lock, confirm no writer for that receipt remains active before removing","that named stale lock. The next mutation will then proceed normally.","","## Where data is stored","","By default RunLedger writes to `./.runledger/` in your current directory.","The launcher gives new files owner-only permissions on POSIX systems; direct","interpreter invocation uses the caller's umask. See the","[security model](docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md) for access and backup guidance.","","```text",".runledger/","  locks/","    2026-05-29-codex-build-tool-x-001.lock  # present only during a mutation","  runs/","    2026-05-29-claude-opus-4-8-build-tool-x-001.json","    2026-05-29-codex-build-tool-x-001.json","    ...","```","","One run = one human-readable, sortable JSON file named by its id","(`YYYY-MM-DD-\u003cmodel\u003e-\u003ctask\u003e-NNN`). Existing run files are never silently","overwritten on `start`.","","Override the location with `--ledger \u003cdir\u003e` on any command, or set the","`RUNLEDGER_DIR` environment variable. The ledger directory is independent of the","`--repo` you record against, so a single ledger can track runs across many repos.","","## Storage format","","Each run is a single JSON object. Fields:","","| Field | Meaning |","|---|---|","| `id` | Stable, human-readable run id. |","| `created_at` / `updated_at` | ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. |","| `status` | `in_progress` \\| `pass` \\| `partial` \\| `fail` \\| `abandoned`. |","| `provider` / `model` | Who ran it. |","| `task_name` | The task the run is an attempt at. |","| `prompt_file` | Path to the prompt used (optional). |","| `repo_path` | Repo the run worked on. |","| `start_commit` / `end_commit` | Git commit at start/finish (null if no git). |","| `git_dirty_start` / `git_dirty_end` | Working-tree dirty state (null if no git). |","| `changed_files` | Files changed between the start/end commits (when available), plus staged, unstaged, and untracked files at finish; names are de-duplicated. |","| `commands` / `tests` | Manually recorded command descriptions and test outcomes. |","| `usage` | `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`. |","| `cost` | `currency`, `input_cost`, `output_cost`, `cache_cost`, `total_cost`. |","| `correlation` | Optional `watchdog_trace_id`, `watchdog_run_id`, `dispatch_run_id`, `relay_run_id`, and `eval_run_id` links. |","| `verdict` | Your one-line human verdict. |","| `followups` | Timestamped follow-up items. |","| `notes` | Timestamped notes. |","","`null` means \"unknown\" (e.g. token counts you never recorded, or git facts when","the repo isn't under git) — distinct from a genuine zero.","","### Example run record","","```json","{","  \"id\": \"2026-05-29-codex-build-tool-x-001\",","  \"created_at\": \"2026-05-29T18:19:59Z\",","  \"updated_at\": \"2026-05-29T18:19:59Z\",","  \"status\": \"partial\",","  \"provider\": \"openai\",","  \"model\": \"codex\",","  \"task_name\": \"Build Tool X\",","  \"prompt_file\": \"./examples/build-tool-x.md\",","  \"repo_path\": \".\",","  \"start_commit\": \"b5d96adb054cb26fe92aa8e8b6524e5d89a56051\",","  \"end_commit\": \"b5d96adb054cb26fe92aa8e8b6524e5d89a56051\",","  \"git_dirty_start\": false,","  \"git_dirty_end\": true,","  \"changed_files\": [\"main.kujo\"],","  \"commands\": [],","  \"tests\": [],","  \"usage\": {","    \"input_tokens\": 190000,","    \"output_tokens\": 26000,","    \"cache_read_tokens\": null,","    \"cache_write_tokens\": null","  },","  \"cost\": {","    \"currency\": \"USD\",","    \"input_cost\": null,","    \"output_cost\": null,","    \"cache_cost\": null,","    \"total_cost\": 0.92","  },","  \"verdict\": \"good start\",","  \"followups\": [","    { \"at\": \"2026-05-29T18:20:00Z\", \"text\": \"Add tests for JSON output\" }","  ],","  \"notes\": []","}","```","","## Example markdown report","","`runledger report` produces a clean markdown summary. A full sample lives in","[examples/RUNLEDGER_REPORT.example.md](examples/RUNLEDGER_REPORT.example.md):","","```markdown","# RunLedger Report","","Generated: 2026-05-29T18:20:01Z","","## Summary","","| Runs | Pass | Partial | Fail | Abandoned |","| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |","| 3 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |","","## Runs","","| ID | Task | Provider | Model | Status | Verdict | Changed files | Follow-ups | Cost |","| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |","| ...-claude-opus-4-8-... | Build Tool X | anthropic | claude-opus-4-8 | pass | clean handoff | 1 | 0 | 1.18 USD |","| ...-codex-...           | Build Tool X | openai    | codex           | partial | good start | 1 | 1 | 0.92 USD |","| ...-deepseek-v3-...     | Build Tool X | deepseek  | deepseek-v3     | fail | tests broken | 1 | 1 | 0.4 USD |","```","","The report never declares a \"best\" or \"worst\" run automatically — it surfaces","your verdicts and the raw counts and lets you decide.","","## Cost and pricing","","RunLedger does not hardcode provider pricing. Cost is **manual**: you supply","`--total` (and optionally per-segment `--input` / `--output` / `--cache` costs","and a `--currency`). This keeps the tool honest and provider-agnostic; pricing","tables change constantly and don't belong baked into a receipt system.","Reports aggregate recorded costs per currency; unlike currencies are never","combined into a dimensionally invalid grand total.","","## Git metadata","","When `--repo` points inside a git repository, RunLedger records the start/end","commit, dirty state, and changed files using **read-only** git commands only","(`rev-parse`, `status --porcelain`, `diff --name-only`, `ls-files`). It never","stages, commits, resets, checks out, or otherwise mutates git state. If git is","absent or the path isn't a repo, those fields are recorded as `null`/empty and","the command still succeeds.","","Changes committed after `start` count even when the worktree is clean at","`finish`. The recorded file set also includes any changes still uncommitted at","finish. Git pathnames use NUL-delimited output to preserve embedded whitespace,","quotes, and Unicode. These are repository observations, not proof that a","particular agent authored every change.","","## Running the tests","","```bash","./tests/run.sh","# or","kujo run tests/runledger_test.kujo","```","","The suite is filesystem-isolated (it uses uniquely named temporary ledgers and","git repos), needs no network or API key, and exits non-zero","on any failure. `tests/run.sh` runs both the module-level Kujo test harness and","CLI integration checks through `bin/runledger`, including concurrent-writer and","lock-ownership regression cases.","","## Limitations","","- Token usage and cost are recorded manually; RunLedger does not capture them","  from any provider automatically.","- `finish` requires an explicit terminal status (`pass`, `partial`, `fail`, or","  `abandoned`) and a non-empty `--verdict`.","- Commands and test outcomes are recorded manually, not run or checked by","  RunLedger. `test --status pass` means the operator reported a pass.","- The launcher needs a `kujo` binary (via `KUJO` or your `PATH`).","- Run files are plain JSON; editing them by hand is supported. RunLedger","  tolerates missing fields, rejects mismatched run IDs, and skips invalid run","  files during list/report operations.","- An interrupted mutating process can leave its sidecar lock behind. RunLedger","  reports the exact path and requires deliberate operator recovery rather than","  guessing that another writer's lock is stale.","","## Non-goals","","Repo intelligence, generic code review, automated benchmarking/Eval, prompt","management, and workflow-pack validation are explicitly out of scope. RunLedger","stays a small, focused, local receipt system for agent runs.","","## Project layout","","```text","runledger/","  runledger.kujo          # entrypoint","  bin/runledger           # launcher wrapper","  kujo.toml               # project manifest","  src/","    util.kujo             # slugs, time, padding, display helpers","    record.kujo           # run record shape + status validation","    storage.kujo          # ledger dir, id minting, safe save/load/list","    args.kujo             # flag and positional argument parser","    gitmeta.kujo          # defensive read-only git metadata","    render.kujo           # tables, single-run view, markdown report","    cli.kujo              # command validation, dispatch, and output","  tests/","    runledger_test.kujo   # test suite","    cli_integration.sh    # user-facing CLI checks","    run.sh                # test runner","  examples/","    build-tool-x.md             # sample prompt","    RUNLEDGER_REPORT.example.md  # sample generated report","  docs/audits/","    repository-hardening.md      # evidence-backed hardening receipt","  docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md          # local trust boundary and operator guidance","  docs/reviews/","    2026-09-22-readiness.md       # next-session review and priorities","  evaluation/scale_benchmark.py   # reproducible large-ledger paired timings","  .agent/","    next-agent-guide.md","```","","## Contributor notes","","Canonical copyable examples live in this README and","`examples/build-tool-x.md`. `examples/RUNLEDGER_REPORT.example.md` is a sample","generated report for output shape. The current hardening evidence lives under","`docs/audits/`.","","For repo sweeps, exclude generated/bulk paths such as `.runledger/` and avoid","treating generated report output as source examples unless the task explicitly","targets report formatting.","","## Kujo runtime measurement references","","Use `runtime-measurement` to verify and retain a summary artifact reference in existing receipt notes. <p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/kujolang/runledger"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/77ed10dc38ded9ab72f0f450e95d821dfb266c13f870b0bc012457e639ce3f26/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f76657273696f6e2d312e322e312d626c61636b" alt="Version" data-canonical-src="https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.2.1-black" style="max-width: 100%;"></a>

<p dir="auto">A local ledger for AI-agent build runs.</p>
<p dir="auto">When you hand several agents (Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, a local model, a future
Kujo-native agent) the same prompt and ask them to build the same thing,
RunLedger gives you a repeatable, inspectable <strong>receipt</strong> for each attempt: what
model ran, against which repo and commit, what files changed, optional
token/cost data you recorded, manually recorded commands and test results,
your verdict, and the follow-ups needed.</p>
<p dir="auto">It is built in the Kujo language runtime and stores everything as plain JSON on
your local disk. No database, no network, no API key.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">What RunLedger is — and is not</h2><a id="user-content-what-runledger-is--and-is-not" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: What RunLedger is — and is not" href="#what-runledger-is--and-is-not"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger <strong>is</strong> a structured receipt system for agent work. It records and
compares runs so you can answer questions like:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Which model followed the prompt best?</li>
<li>Which run changed the fewest files?</li>
<li>Which run did I record as passing its tests?</li>
<li>Which run needed the fewest follow-up fixes?</li>
<li>Which run was most expensive?</li>
<li>Which run produced the cleanest handoff?</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger is deliberately <strong>not</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>a deep automated code reviewer,</li>
<li>an Eval runner or benchmark judge,</li>
<li>a Scout replacement,</li>
<li>a ShipCheck replacement,</li>
<li>a Trail replacement,</li>
<li>a prompt manager or workflow-pack validator.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">It does not try to judge code quality. It records facts you give it plus a few
read-only git facts, and presents them back clearly.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Readiness posture</h2><a id="user-content-readiness-posture" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Readiness posture" href="#readiness-posture"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger is intentionally small, local-first, and automation-friendly. It is
ready to use as a practical agent-run receipt ledger, but "enterprise grade" is
an ongoing standard rather than a one-time label. The current implementation
prioritizes:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>local JSON storage with no network calls and no provider API keys,</li>
<li>read-only git metadata collection,</li>
<li>atomic writes for run files and generated reports,</li>
<li>explicit exit codes for automation,</li>
<li>defensive loading of partial or malformed run files,</li>
<li>safe run-id handling so user-supplied IDs cannot escape the ledger directory,</li>
<li>per-record ownership locks for conflict-safe concurrent mutations,</li>
<li>markdown report output that stays stable when user text contains table
punctuation.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This is not a universal enterprise-readiness certification: shared-ledger
authorization, efficient full-history reports at very large scales, and a
formal security review remain open. File-ordered pages keep 10,000-receipt
ledgers practical for bounded reads.
See <a href="/kujolang/runledger/blob/ab0ec5d2edb7ffd913f48d092aa6fc17cab58d13/docs/reviews/2026-09-22-readiness.md">the next review</a> for scoped evidence
and priorities, and read the <a href="/kujolang/runledger/blob/ab0ec5d2edb7ffd913f48d092aa6fc17cab58d13/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md">local security model</a>
before using receipts with private information. The tool remains a local
receipt store, not a multi-tenant service or an automated judge.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Installation</h2><a id="user-content-installation" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Installation" href="#installation"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger 1.2.1 requires Kujo 1.6.0 or newer. Install with Kennel 1.1.0 or newer:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="kennel tool install runledger@1.2.1
runledger version"><pre>kennel tool install runledger@1.2.1
runledger version</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Alternatively, download the <code>v1.2.1</code> source release and use its POSIX launcher
or invoke <code>runledger.kujo</code> directly. No provider credentials are required.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Preflight: verify the right <code>kujo</code> binary</h3><a id="user-content-preflight-verify-the-right-kujo-binary" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Preflight: verify the right kujo binary" href="#preflight-verify-the-right-kujo-binary"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger requires the Kujo language runtime (the one that supports
<code>kujo run ...</code>). Python's linting tool named <code>kujo</code> is not compatible.</p>

<p dir="auto">Give each agent the same prompt, then record each attempt against the same task
name so they line up in <code>compare</code> and <code>report</code>. The helper below keeps the
repeated command shape copyable without obscuring the lifecycle steps:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="TASK="Build Tool X"
PROMPT="./examples/build-tool-x.md"

start_run() {
  runledger start --provider "$1" --model "$2" --task "$TASK" --prompt "$PROMPT" --repo . |
    sed -n '1s/^Started run: //p'
}

# Claude
id=$(start_run anthropic claude-opus-4-8)
# ...run the agent...
runledger usage "$id" --input 140000 --output 22000
runledger cost  "$id" --total 1.18
runledger finish "$id" --status pass --verdict "clean handoff"

# Codex
id=$(start_run openai codex)
runledger usage "$id" --input 190000 --output 26000
runledger cost  "$id" --total 0.92
runledger followup "$id" "Add tests for JSON output"
runledger finish "$id" --status partial --verdict "good start"

id=$(start_run deepseek deepseek-v3)
runledger usage "$id" --input 210000 --output 31000
runledger cost  "$id" --total 0.40
runledger finish "$id" --status fail --verdict "tests broken"

runledger compare --task "$TASK"

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Flags</h3><a id="user-content-flags" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Flags" href="#flags"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>start</code>: <code>--model</code> <code>--provider</code> <code>--task</code> (required); <code>--prompt <file></code> <code>--repo <path></code> (default <code>.</code>) <code>--ledger <dir></code></li>
<li><code>finish</code>: <code>--status <s></code> <code>--verdict <text></code> (required); <code>--notes <text></code> <code>--repo <path></code> (defaults to the run's recorded repo)</li>
<li><code>usage</code>: <code>--input</code> <code>--output</code> <code>--cache-read</code> <code>--cache-write</code> (all optional integers)</li>
<li><code>cost</code>: <code>--total</code> <code>--currency</code> <code>--input</code> <code>--output</code> <code>--cache</code> (amounts are floats; only provided fields change)</li>
<li><code>correlate</code>: <code>--watchdog-trace</code> <code>--watchdog-run</code> <code>--dispatch-run</code> <code>--relay-run</code> <code>--eval-run</code> (bounded identifiers only)</li>
<li><code>test</code>: <code>--status <pass|fail|skip></code> (required); <code>--details <text></code> (optional)</li>
<li><code>list</code> / <code>compare</code> / <code>report</code>: <code>--strict</code> fails on any invalid run file; <code>--limit <1..1000></code> and <code>--offset <N></code> page through sorted run filenames; <code>list</code> and <code>compare</code> accept <code>--json</code>; <code>report</code> accepts <code>--output <file></code></li>
<li><code>verify</code>: <code>--json</code> emits valid count and a list of <code>{file, error}</code> diagnostics</li>
<li><code>compare</code> / <code>report</code>: <code>--task <name></code> to filter results</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For large ledgers, <code>runledger report --limit 100 --offset 0</code> and subsequent
pages avoid loading the other run files. The report labels its counts as
page-only. Pagination selects filenames before the optional task filter;
malformed entries within a page are skipped by default, while <code>--strict</code>
validates the entire ledger before selecting a page. Use <code>runledger verify</code>
to check all files without rendering a full report.</p>
<p dir="auto">Command descriptions are limited to 2,000 characters. Test names are limited
to 200 characters and details to 2,000; each run can store at most 1,000
commands and 1,000 test results. These are manual observations, not automatic
test execution or a verified test verdict. Keep secrets out of the receipt.</p>
<p dir="auto">Allowed statuses: <code>in_progress</code>, <code>pass</code>, <code>partial</code>, <code>fail</code>, <code>abandoned</code>. An
invalid status fails with a clear error and a non-zero exit code.
<code>finish</code> accepts only terminal statuses: <code>pass</code>, <code>partial</code>, <code>fail</code>, and
<code>abandoned</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Exit codes</h3><a id="user-content-exit-codes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Exit codes" href="#exit-codes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>0</code> success</li>
<li><code>1</code> operational failure (no such run, invalid status, corrupt file)</li>
<li><code>2</code> usage error (bad/missing arguments, unknown command, invalid numeric flag value)</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Concurrent writers</h2><a id="user-content-concurrent-writers" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Concurrent writers" href="#concurrent-writers"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The mutating commands (<code>finish</code>, <code>note</code>, <code>followup</code>, <code>command</code>, <code>test</code>, <code>usage</code>, <code>cost</code>, and <code>correlate</code>)
serialize each receipt's complete read-modify-write transaction through
<code><ledger>/locks/<run-id>.lock</code>. Writers targeting different receipts remain
independent. Concurrent <code>start</code> commands atomically retry ID allocation when
they select the same candidate. Read-only commands do not acquire locks.</p>
<p dir="auto">A writer waits up to 10 seconds by default. Set
<code>RUNLEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS</code> to an integer from <code>10</code> through <code>60000</code> to choose a
different bound. A timeout exits 1 and names the exact lock file; it never
removes a lock owned by another process. If a process is interrupted while it
owns a lock, confirm no writer for that receipt remains active before removing
that named stale lock. The next mutation will then proceed normally.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Where data is stored</h2><a id="user-content-where-data-is-stored" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Where data is stored" href="#where-data-is-stored"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">By default RunLedger writes to <code>./.runledger/</code> in your current directory.
The launcher gives new files owner-only permissions on POSIX systems; direct
interpreter invocation uses the caller's umask. See the
<a href="/kujolang/runledger/blob/ab0ec5d2edb7ffd913f48d092aa6fc17cab58d13/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md">security model</a> for access and backup guidance.</p>

<p dir="auto">One run = one human-readable, sortable JSON file named by its id
(<code>YYYY-MM-DD-<model>-<task>-NNN</code>). Existing run files are never silently
overwritten on <code>start</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Override the location with <code>--ledger <dir></code> on any command, or set the
<code>RUNLEDGER_DIR</code> environment variable. The ledger directory is independent of the
<code>--repo</code> you record against, so a single ledger can track runs across many repos.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Storage format</h2><a id="user-content-storage-format" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Storage format" href="#storage-format"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Each run is a single JSON object. Fields:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Field</th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>id</code></td>
<td>Stable, human-readable run id.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>created_at</code> / <code>updated_at</code></td>
<td>ISO-8601 UTC timestamps.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>status</code></td>
<td><code>in_progress</code> | <code>pass</code> | <code>partial</code> | <code>fail</code> | <code>abandoned</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>provider</code> / <code>model</code></td>
<td>Who ran it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>task_name</code></td>
<td>The task the run is an attempt at.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>prompt_file</code></td>
<td>Path to the prompt used (optional).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>repo_path</code></td>
<td>Repo the run worked on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>start_commit</code> / <code>end_commit</code></td>
<td>Git commit at start/finish (null if no git).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>git_dirty_start</code> / <code>git_dirty_end</code></td>
<td>Working-tree dirty state (null if no git).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>changed_files</code></td>
<td>Files changed between the start/end commits (when available), plus staged, unstaged, and untracked files at finish; names are de-duplicated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>commands</code> / <code>tests</code></td>
<td>Manually recorded command descriptions and test outcomes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>usage</code></td>
<td><code>input_tokens</code>, <code>output_tokens</code>, <code>cache_read_tokens</code>, <code>cache_write_tokens</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cost</code></td>
<td><code>currency</code>, <code>input_cost</code>, <code>output_cost</code>, <code>cache_cost</code>, <code>total_cost</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>correlation</code></td>
<td>Optional <code>watchdog_trace_id</code>, <code>watchdog_run_id</code>, <code>dispatch_run_id</code>, <code>relay_run_id</code>, and <code>eval_run_id</code> links.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>verdict</code></td>
<td>Your one-line human verdict.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>followups</code></td>
<td>Timestamped follow-up items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>notes</code></td>
<td>Timestamped notes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><code>null</code> means "unknown" (e.g. token counts you never recorded, or git facts when
the repo isn't under git) — distinct from a genuine zero.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Cost and pricing</h2><a id="user-content-cost-and-pricing" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Cost and pricing" href="#cost-and-pricing"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">RunLedger does not hardcode provider pricing. Cost is <strong>manual</strong>: you supply
<code>--total</code> (and optionally per-segment <code>--input</code> / <code>--output</code> / <code>--cache</code> costs
and a <code>--currency</code>). This keeps the tool honest and provider-agnostic; pricing
tables change constantly and don't belong baked into a receipt system.
Reports aggregate recorded costs per currency; unlike currencies are never
combined into a dimensionally invalid grand total.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Git metadata</h2><a id="user-content-git-metadata" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Git metadata" href="#git-metadata"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When <code>--repo</code> points inside a git repository, RunLedger records the start/end
commit, dirty state, and changed files using <strong>read-only</strong> git commands only
(<code>rev-parse</code>, <code>status --porcelain</code>, <code>diff --name-only</code>, <code>ls-files</code>). It never
stages, commits, resets, checks out, or otherwise mutates git state. If git is
absent or the path isn't a repo, those fields are recorded as <code>null</code>/empty and
the command still succeeds.</p>
<p dir="auto">Changes committed after <code>start</code> count even when the worktree is clean at
<code>finish</code>. The recorded file set also includes any changes still uncommitted at
finish. Git pathnames use NUL-delimited output to preserve embedded whitespace,
quotes, and Unicode. These are repository observations, not proof that a
particular agent authored every change.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Running the tests</h2><a id="user-content-running-the-tests" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Running the tests" href="#running-the-tests"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="./tests/run.sh
# or
kujo run tests/runledger_test.kujo"><pre>./tests/run.sh
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> or</span>
kujo run tests/runledger_test.kujo</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The suite is filesystem-isolated (it uses uniquely named temporary ledgers and
git repos), needs no network or API key, and exits non-zero
on any failure. <code>tests/run.sh</code> runs both the module-level Kujo test harness and
CLI integration checks through <code>bin/runledger</code>, including concurrent-writer and
lock-ownership regression cases.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Limitations</h2><a id="user-content-limitations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Limitations" href="#limitations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Token usage and cost are recorded manually; RunLedger does not capture them
from any provider automatically.</li>
<li><code>finish</code> requires an explicit terminal status (<code>pass</code>, <code>partial</code>, <code>fail</code>, or
<code>abandoned</code>) and a non-empty <code>--verdict</code>.</li>
<li>Commands and test outcomes are recorded manually, not run or checked by
RunLedger. <code>test --status pass</code> means the operator reported a pass.</li>
<li>The launcher needs a <code>kujo</code> binary (via <code>KUJO</code> or your <code>PATH</code>).</li>
<li>Run files are plain JSON; editing them by hand is supported. RunLedger
tolerates missing fields, rejects mismatched run IDs, and skips invalid run
files during list/report operations.</li>
<li>An interrupted mutating process can leave its sidecar lock behind. RunLedger
reports the exact path and requires deliberate operator recovery rather than
guessing that another writer's lock is stale.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Non-goals</h2><a id="user-content-non-goals" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Non-goals" href="#non-goals"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Repo intelligence, generic code review, automated benchmarking/Eval, prompt
management, and workflow-pack validation are explicitly out of scope. RunLedger
stays a small, focused, local receipt system for agent runs.</p>

Its dashboard and JSON APIs show latency, token use, estimated costs and failures.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePoint an OpenAI-compatible client at \u003ccode\u003e/proxy/v1\u003c/code\u003e. Watchdog forwards requests to your provider and records telemetry. Native producers can also submit canonical batches or supported OTLP traces.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCosts are estimated direct-provider equivalents, not invoices. See \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/PRICING_ESTIMATES.md\"\u003epricing estimates\u003c/a\u003e for catalog sources, model mappings and repricing commands.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWatchdog runs locally by default. Before exposing it to other machines, configure token authentication, TLS, network access, retention, backups and secret storage. See the \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/DEPLOYMENT_HARDENING_RUNBOOK.md\"\u003edeployment guide\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCurrent release\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-current-release\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Current release\" href=\"#current-release\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWatchdog 1.2.2 updates the pricing catalogs, supported Node.js versions and service-readiness checks. dir=\"auto\"\u003eProxy forwarding is broader than telemetry decoding. Chat Completions JSON/SSE\nhas the first endpoint-specific decoder for model, usage, finish-reason, and\nbounded summaries. Other paths are opaque: Watchdog records transport metadata\nand correlation but forwards request/response bodies byte-for-byte without\ntrying to interpret provider extensions, multipart uploads, images, audio,\nfiles, fine-tuning payloads, or arbitrary JSON as chat telemetry.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe proxy forwards JSON responses and incrementally passes through streaming\nchat SSE responses when run with a Kujo build containing generic HTTP response\nstreaming. It returns the upstream status/body to the caller and records the\nfirst meaningful content delta plus completion or disconnect lifecycle facts.\nSafe scalar query parameters are forwarded to upstream list and\nretrieve endpoints, while suspicious path/query text such as path traversal,\nembedded URL schemes, fragments, and query delimiters in path segments is\nrejected before any upstream request is made.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAuth modes\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca
