\u003ccode\u003eWDG_EXPORTERS_CONFIG_PATH\u003c/code\u003e, enable a profile, and run \u003ccode\u003ekujo run export_worker.kujo\u003c/code\u003e once or with \u003ccode\u003e--watch\u003c/code\u003e. Profiles are isolated by durable queue/checkpoint state; optional destination failure never changes proxy success. Remote endpoints require HTTPS. Loopback HTTP is accepted for local collectors, while private-network HTTPS requires the profile's explicit \u003ccode\u003eallow_private_network\u003c/code\u003e opt-in.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eencoding: \"protobuf\"\u003c/code\u003e is the recommended OTLP/HTTP transport and sends \u003ccode\u003eapplication/x-protobuf\u003c/code\u003e; it requires Kujo 1.2.2 or newer for binary request/response bodies. \u003ccode\u003eencoding: \"json\"\u003c/code\u003e remains the compatibility default when the field is omitted. Set \u003ccode\u003ecompression: \"gzip\"\u003c/code\u003e for bounded binary-safe request compression. Mapping profiles are independently pinned as \u003ccode\u003eotel.base.v1\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eotel.genai.v1\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003eopeninference.v1\u003c/code\u003e. Grafana/Tempo, Datadog, Honeycomb, Phoenix, Langfuse, and other compatible destinations should normally receive these profiles through their OTLP endpoint or an OpenTelemetry Collector, not a destination-specific Watchdog trace client.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eExporter credentials never belong in the profile. Map a header to an environment-variable name with \u003ccode\u003eheaders_from_env\u003c/code\u003e, for example \u003ccode\u003e{\"Authorization\":\"WATCHDOG_OTLP_AUTH\"}\u003c/code\u003e, then set that environment variable only in the worker process. The worker caps batches at 256 records and 512 KiB, retries bounded transient failures, pauses on authentication rejection, expires old queue entries, and retains bounded dead-letter metadata without raw export payloads.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe guarded trace receiver is \u003ccode\u003ePOST /telemetry/v2/otlp/v1/traces\u003c/code\u003e. It accepts OTLP/HTTP JSON and Protobuf, optionally gzip-compressed, under the same authentication, request-size, rate, and privacy controls as other ingestion. It retains only spans carrying recognized GenAI/OpenInference/Watchdog semantics, returns OTLP partial success for rejected spans, strips content at the authoritative policy boundary, and rejects generic traces, logs, metrics, malformed wire data, and over-limit decompression. Watchdog does not accept arbitrary OpenTelemetry data.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eRate limiting\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-rate-limiting\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Rate limiting\" href=\"#rate-limiting\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eWDG_RATE_LIMIT_MODE=basic\u003c/code\u003e enables lightweight SQLite-backed throttling for both Watchdog API routes and proxy routes. Persisted buckets avoid concurrent dashboard requests corrupting shared process state.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBuckets are keyed by \u003ccode\u003eX-Observe-Session-Id\u003c/code\u003e when present, otherwise by forwarded IP/host fallbacks.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003eWDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eWDG_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS\u003c/code\u003e to tune burst tolerance for your environment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003eWDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BUCKETS\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eWDG_RATE_LIMIT_BUCKET_TTL_SECS\u003c/code\u003e to bound limiter memory and evict stale buckets in long-running deployments.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAutomated database backups\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-automated-database-backups\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Automated database backups\" href=\"#automated-database-backups\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWatchdog enables verified SQLite backups by default every 24 hours. Open the\n\u003cstrong\u003eBackups\u003c/strong\u003e dashboard tab to change the frequency, destination folder,\nretention count, encryption setting, or to create a backup immediately.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBackups use SQLite's online \u003ccode\u003eVACUUM INTO\u003c/code\u003e path, so Watchdog does not need to stop.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEach backup is checked with \u003ccode\u003ePRAGMA quick_check\u003c/code\u003e and receives a \u003ccode\u003e.sha256\u003c/code\u003e sidecar.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eA Dropbox or Google Drive folder can be selected by entering its local synced path.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eScheduling is activity-aware: startup, dashboard refreshes, proxy traffic, and direct telemetry trigger a due check. If Watchdog is idle, the next activity creates the overdue backup before continuing.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eGenerated files use \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog-backup-\u0026lt;UTC timestamp\u0026gt;-\u0026lt;suffix\u0026gt;.db\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e.db.enc\u003c/code\u003e; retention only removes files matching that pattern.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThe main backup list now shows only files still present in the configured folder. Deleted or missing files stay available under the archived history view, and active backups can be deleted directly from the dashboard.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor encrypted backups, create a dedicated passphrase file outside the repository:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"mkdir -p \u0026quot;$HOME/.config/watchdog\u0026quot;\nopenssl rand -base64 48 \u0026gt; \u0026quot;$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u0026quot;\nchmod 600 \u0026quot;$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u0026quot;\nexport WDG_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE=\u0026quot;$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u0026quot;\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003emkdir -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-smi\"\u003e$HOME\u003c/span\u003e/.config/watchdog\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\nopenssl rand -base64 48 \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-smi\"\u003e$HOME\u003c/span\u003e/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\nchmod 600 \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-smi\"\u003e$HOME\u003c/span\u003e/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eexport\u003c/span\u003e WDG_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE=\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-smi\"\u003e$HOME\u003c/span\u003e/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRestart Watchdog, then enable encryption in the Backups tab. Encryption uses\nAES-256-CBC with PBKDF2-SHA256 and 200,000 iterations. Restore an encrypted file:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"openssl file:\u0026quot;$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\u0026quot;\nsqlite3 restored-watchdog.db 'PRAGMA quick_check;'\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eopenssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 200000 -md Give each app a distinct \u003ccode\u003eX-Observe-Project-Id\u003c/code\u003e (for example,\n\u003ccode\u003esignalbox\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eai-chat\u003c/code\u003e) and the unfiltered dashboard stats include both;\nthe request table can still be filtered by project when needed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eKeep the three credential roles separate:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eWDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN\u003c/code\u003e protects Watchdog's dashboard JSON APIs.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eWDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN\u003c/code\u003e controls which clients may use the proxy.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUpstream provider keys authenticate Watchdog to OpenAI-compatible providers.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor several apps using the same upstream account, \u003ccode\u003eoverride\u003c/code\u003e mode is simplest:\nall apps share the Watchdog proxy URL/token while Watchdog injects its single\nconfigured upstream key. For apps with different upstream keys, use\n\u003ccode\u003epassthrough\u003c/code\u003e mode so each client sends its own upstream \u003ccode\u003eAuthorization\u003c/code\u003e value,\nand send the Watchdog access credential separately in\n\u003ccode\u003eX-Watchdog-Proxy-Token\u003c/code\u003e. dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe granular contract is optional and producer-neutral. Watchdog is a passive collector: applications, model providers, and tool executors remain independently usable, and a tool can append its own telemetry without importing or depending on another tool. New producers should send \u003ccode\u003eschema_version: \"kujo.telemetry.v1\"\u003c/code\u003e; the checked-in contract is \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/schemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eschemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e. Trace metrics are cumulative absolute values, and trace/span/event/tool identities are replay-safe for durable at-least-once delivery. See \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/GRANULAR_TRACING.md\"\u003eGranular Tracing\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe Sources tab and \u003ccode\u003ewatchdog.sources-panel.v1\u003c/code\u003e API report inbound producers\nwithout conflating them with exporter destinations. Status is based only on\nconfiguration and accepted local telemetry. Native/OTLP registration changes\nmanage display/setup metadata; they do not start, stop, or disconnect another\napplication. Named proxy profile changes are saved to the existing proxy\nconfiguration and apply to new requests without restarting Watchdog. In-flight\nrequests retain the profile snapshot they started with. See \u003ca href=\"/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/CONNECTED_SOURCES.md\"\u003eConnected Sources\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e/api/insights\u003c/code\u003e reports observed legacy telemetry: runs are grouped by task ID, workflow ID, or session ID; a success signal means no request error was recorded; retry signals are inferred from retry-named trace events; and its token-volume section does not measure context capacity. The Canonical Evidence dashboard tab uses explicit terminal events, typed relations, nullable timing, versioned context limits, and distinct cost kinds instead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp Valid batches are\nprivacy-filtered once, then retain repository validation, identity-conflict checks\nand transactional persistence.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCanonical repository intake reuses each validated record's stable JSON and SHA-256\nwithin its bounded batch for conflict checks and insertion. It does not cache\nrecords across requests or bypass privacy, validation, or transactional conflict\nrejection. Legacy rows without stored hashes still backfill from their canonical\nJSON. Routes and telemetry schemas remain compatible.","","### Included 1.2.1 improvements","","[Watchdog 1.2.1](https://github.com/kujolang/watchdog/releases/tag/v1.2.1) fixes credential forwarding, telemetry validation, OTLP retries and delivery queue limits. It reduces canonical intake work, client cloning and backup memory use, and updates pricing catalogs. Existing routes and telemetry schemas remain compatible; malformed records and conflicting OTLP retries now return errors. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.","","---","","## How it works","","1. Your client sends requests to this server at `/proxy/v1/...`.","2. The server forwards them to a configurable upstream base URL.","3. The server logs request metrics and traces in SQLite.","4. The dashboard UI reads those logs from JSON API endpoints.","","No changes are required in your app code beyond setting the base URL (and API","key behavior) to use the proxy.","","---","","## Quick start","","Use [Kujo 1.6.0](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo/releases/tag/v1.6.0) for the verified release workflow and runtime-measurement adapter. Watchdog does not authorize execution or replay.","","### 1) Start the Watchdog server","","```bash","cd /path/to/kujo-watchdog","kujo run dashboard_server.kujo","```","","### 2) Open the dashboard","","```text","http://localhost:7700","```","","When `WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=token`, the dashboard opens an API access prompt.","Enter the configured `WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN`; the browser keeps it in","`sessionStorage` for the current tab session and sends it as","`X-Watchdog-Token` on dashboard API requests. A missing or invalid token is","shown explicitly instead of leaving the dashboard in an empty loading state.","","### 3) Verify proxy configuration endpoint","","```bash","curl -s http://localhost:7700/api/proxy-config","```","","Expected response shape:","","```json","{","  \"ok\": true,","  \"data\": {","    \"upstream_base_url\": \"https://api.openai.com/v1\",","    \"auth_mode\": \"passthrough\",","    \"has_override_api_key\": false,","    \"api_auth_mode\": \"off\",","    \"api_auth_enabled\": false,","    \"proxy_auth_mode\": \"off\",","    \"proxy_auth_enabled\": false","  }","}","```","","### 4) Optional smoke test (passthrough auth mode)","","```bash","curl -i -s \\","    -X POST http://localhost:7700/proxy/v1/chat/completions \\","    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\","    -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-4.1-mini\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"proxy smoke\"}]}'","```","","If no API key header is passed in passthrough mode, you should see an upstream","`401` and a corresponding error row in `/api/requests`.","","---","","## Canonical examples and generated paths","","Use `src/` as the canonical implementation source. The root files","`dashboard_server.kujo`, `dashboard.html`, `watchdog.kujo`, and","`watchdog_shared.kujo` are compatibility mirrors kept in sync from `src/`.","","`demo.kujo`, this README, and `docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md` are the","primary copyable examples. Prefer compact, runnable snippets in those files and","keep repeated output formatting behind small local helpers when it improves","scannability.","","The demo seeder writes to `data/watchdog-demo.db` and refuses the production","`watchdog.db`. Demo rows are labeled `source_app=watchdog-demo` and","`data_class=fixture`; live proxy and external application telemetry remain in","the production database with distinct classifications.","","Treat `tests/` as contract and regression coverage. Unknown profile names are","rejected before any upstream request. The dashboard records the selected profile","name as the request provider, making account/provider filtering unambiguous.","","---","","## Proxy routes","","| Method | Path | Notes |","|--------|------|-------|","| `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE` | `/proxy/v1/:resource` | Example: `/proxy/v1/models` |","| `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE` | `/proxy/v1/:resource/:action` | Example: `/proxy/v1/chat/completions` |","| `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE` | `/proxy/v1/:resource/:action/:subaction` | Example: `/proxy/v1/fine_tuning/jobs` |","| `GET,POST,PUT,PATCH,DELETE` | `/proxy/v1/:resource/:action/:subaction/:tail` | Example: `/proxy/v1/fine_tuning/jobs/\u003cid\u003e/cancel` |","","Proxy forwarding is broader than telemetry decoding. Chat Completions JSON/SSE","has the first endpoint-specific decoder for model, usage, finish-reason, and","bounded summaries. Other paths are opaque: Watchdog records transport metadata","and correlation but forwards request/response bodies byte-for-byte without","trying to interpret provider extensions, multipart uploads, images, audio,","files, fine-tuning payloads, or arbitrary JSON as chat telemetry.","","The proxy forwards JSON responses and incrementally passes through streaming","chat SSE responses when run with a Kujo build containing generic HTTP response","streaming. It returns the upstream status/body to the caller and records the","first meaningful content delta plus completion or disconnect lifecycle facts.","Safe scalar query parameters are forwarded to upstream list and","retrieve endpoints, while suspicious path/query text such as path traversal,","embedded URL schemes, fragments, and query delimiters in path segments is","rejected before any upstream request is made.","","---","","## Auth modes","","### `passthrough` (default)","","- Forwards incoming provider `Authorization` to upstream. A bearer value equal to the configured Watchdog proxy token is stripped; send `X-Watchdog-Proxy-Token` separately from provider authorization.","- Best when each client profile manages its own key.","","### `override`","","- Ignores incoming auth and injects a server-side upstream key.","- Set key via `WDG_UPSTREAM_API_KEY` or `WDG_UPSTREAM_API_KEY_ENV`.","","## Watchdog API auth mode","","### `off` (default)","","- Leaves Watchdog API endpoints (`/api/*`) open for local development.","","### `token`","","- Requires `WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN` for every `/api/*` request.","- Accepts either `X-Watchdog-Token: \u003ctoken\u003e` or `Authorization: Bearer \u003ctoken\u003e`.","","Example:","","```bash","WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=token \\","WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN='replace-with-long-random-token' \\","kujo run dashboard_server.kujo","```","","Then call protected routes with:","","```bash","curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/stats -H 'X-Watchdog-Token: replace-with-long-random-token'","```","","## Proxy route auth mode","","### `off` (default)","","- Leaves proxy endpoints (`/proxy/*`) open.","","### `token`","","- Requires `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN` for non-allowlisted proxy requests.","- Accepts either `X-Watchdog-Proxy-Token: \u003ctoken\u003e` or `Authorization: Bearer \u003ctoken\u003e`.","- Uses exact-path allowlist entries from `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_ALLOWLIST` (default keeps `/healthz` and `/readyz` open).","","Example:","","```bash","WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_MODE=token \\","WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN='replace-with-long-random-proxy-token' \\","WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_ALLOWLIST='/healthz,/readyz,/proxy/v1/models' \\","kujo run dashboard_server.kujo","```","","## Non-local deployment hardening","","- Set `WDG_HOST=127.0.0.1` for loopback-only access; the default is `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces).","- Treat `WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=off` as local-only usage.","- For non-local access, enable `WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=token`, enable `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_MODE=token`, and place Watchdog behind firewall rules or a reverse proxy.","","## Production startup policy","","- Set `WDG_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=production` for non-local deployments.","- In production profile mode, Watchdog fails startup unless all of the following are configured:","    - `WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=token`","    - `WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN` is non-empty","    - `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_MODE=token`","    - `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN` is non-empty","- `WDG_ALLOW_INSECURE_STARTUP=true` acts as break-glass override for controlled emergency scenarios and prints policy warnings at startup.","","## Response security headers","","Watchdog responses include:","","- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`","- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`","- `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`","- `Cache-Control: no-store`","","These headers are applied to dashboard, API, and proxy responses.","","## Dashboard asset policy","","- Remote font stylesheets are not used by default; dashboard typography relies on local/system fonts.","- Dashboard charts use Dither Kit components installed in source mode with `npx @dither-kit/cli`.","- The generated `dither-kit.json` lockfile records the installed component versions and hashes.","- Built JavaScript and CSS are served locally from `/assets/vendor/dither-charts.js` and `/assets/vendor/dither-charts.css`; charts do not require a runtime CDN.","- Departure Mono is bundled locally under `vendor/fonts/` with its SIL Open Font License and embedded into the dashboard response; titles, metrics, and chart labels use the SiteKit-compatible mono stack.","","To update or rebuild the chart assets:","","```bash","npx @dither-kit/cli update","npm run build:charts","```","","## Telemetry redaction policy","","- `WDG_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=off` (default) prevents proxy prompt and response summaries from being persisted.","- `WDG_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=summaries` explicitly enables bounded proxy summaries.","- `WDG_REDACTION_MODE=basic` (default) redacts sensitive terms from any enabled summaries, tool-call payload fields, step metadata, and error messages before data is stored or exported.","- `WDG_REDACTION_MODE=off` keeps original text for local debugging workflows.","- Extend the matching vocabulary with `WDG_REDACT_TERMS` to include environment-specific secret markers.","","## OTLP export","","Copy `config/exporters.example.json` to the path selected by `WDG_EXPORTERS_CONFIG_PATH`, enable a profile, and run `kujo run export_worker.kujo` once or with `--watch`. Profiles are isolated by durable queue/checkpoint state; optional destination failure never changes proxy success. Remote endpoints require HTTPS. Loopback HTTP is accepted for local collectors, while private-network HTTPS requires the profile's explicit `allow_private_network` opt-in.","","`encoding: \"protobuf\"` is the recommended OTLP/HTTP transport and sends `application/x-protobuf`; it requires Kujo 1.2.2 or newer for binary request/response bodies. `encoding: \"json\"` remains the compatibility default when the field is omitted. Set `compression: \"gzip\"` for bounded binary-safe request compression. Mapping profiles are independently pinned as `otel.base.v1`, `otel.genai.v1`, or `openinference.v1`. Grafana/Tempo, Datadog, Honeycomb, Phoenix, Langfuse, and other compatible destinations should normally receive these profiles through their OTLP endpoint or an OpenTelemetry Collector, not a destination-specific Watchdog trace client.","","Exporter credentials never belong in the profile. Map a header to an environment-variable name with `headers_from_env`, for example `{\"Authorization\":\"WATCHDOG_OTLP_AUTH\"}`, then set that environment variable only in the worker process. The worker caps batches at 256 records and 512 KiB, retries bounded transient failures, pauses on authentication rejection, expires old queue entries, and retains bounded dead-letter metadata without raw export payloads.","","The guarded trace receiver is `POST /telemetry/v2/otlp/v1/traces`. It accepts OTLP/HTTP JSON and Protobuf, optionally gzip-compressed, under the same authentication, request-size, rate, and privacy controls as other ingestion. It retains only spans carrying recognized GenAI/OpenInference/Watchdog semantics, returns OTLP partial success for rejected spans, strips content at the authoritative policy boundary, and rejects generic traces, logs, metrics, malformed wire data, and over-limit decompression. Watchdog does not accept arbitrary OpenTelemetry data.","","## Rate limiting","","- `WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MODE=basic` enables lightweight SQLite-backed throttling for both Watchdog API routes and proxy routes. Persisted buckets avoid concurrent dashboard requests corrupting shared process state.","- Buckets are keyed by `X-Observe-Session-Id` when present, otherwise by forwarded IP/host fallbacks.","- Use `WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS` and `WDG_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS` to tune burst tolerance for your environment.","- Use `WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BUCKETS` and `WDG_RATE_LIMIT_BUCKET_TTL_SECS` to bound limiter memory and evict stale buckets in long-running deployments.","","## Automated database backups","","Watchdog enables verified SQLite backups by default every 24 hours. Open the","**Backups** dashboard tab to change the frequency, destination folder,","retention count, encryption setting, or to create a backup immediately.","","- Backups use SQLite's online `VACUUM INTO` path, so Watchdog does not need to stop.","- Each backup is checked with `PRAGMA quick_check` and receives a `.sha256` sidecar.","- A Dropbox or Google Drive folder can be selected by entering its local synced path.","- Scheduling is activity-aware: startup, dashboard refreshes, proxy traffic, and direct telemetry trigger a due check. If Watchdog is idle, the next activity creates the overdue backup before continuing.","- Generated files use `watchdog-backup-\u003cUTC timestamp\u003e-\u003csuffix\u003e.db` or `.db.enc`; retention only removes files matching that pattern.","- The main backup list now shows only files still present in the configured folder. Deleted or missing files stay available under the archived history view, and active backups can be deleted directly from the dashboard.","","For encrypted backups, create a dedicated passphrase file outside the repository:","","```bash","mkdir -p \"$HOME/.config/watchdog\"","openssl rand -base64 48 \u003e \"$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\"","chmod 600 \"$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\"","export WDG_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE=\"$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\"","```","","Restart Watchdog, then enable encryption in the Backups tab. Encryption uses","AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2-SHA256 and 200,000 iterations. Restore an encrypted file:","","```bash","openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 200000 -md sha256 \\","  -in watchdog-backup-TIMESTAMP.db.enc \\","  -out restored-watchdog.db \\","  -pass file:\"$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key\"","sqlite3 restored-watchdog.db 'PRAGMA quick_check;'","```","","---","","## Integrating any OpenAI-compatible client","","Set the client base URL to:","","```text","http://localhost:7700/proxy/v1","```","","Keep normal OpenAI-style paths, for example `chat/completions`.","","Optional headers for better dashboard grouping:","","- `X-Observe-Session-Id`","- `X-Observe-User-Id`","- `X-Observe-Tenant-Id`","- `X-Observe-Project-Id`","- `X-Observe-Workflow-Id`","- `X-Observe-Task-Id`","- `X-Observe-Correlation-Id`","","Tenant/project values can also be supplied in JSON request bodies using","`tenant_id` and `project_id` when headers are not available.","","If omitted, the proxy auto-generates values.","","### Aggregating multiple apps and API keys","","One Watchdog server aggregates every app that sends traffic through its","`/proxy/v1` URL into the same telemetry database. API keys do not partition","dashboard data. Give each app a distinct `X-Observe-Project-Id` (for example,","`signalbox` and `ai-chat`) and the unfiltered dashboard stats include both;","the request table can still be filtered by project when needed.","","Keep the three credential roles separate:","","- `WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN` protects Watchdog's dashboard JSON APIs.","- `WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN` controls which clients may use the proxy.","- Upstream provider keys authenticate Watchdog to OpenAI-compatible providers.","","For several apps using the same upstream account, `override` mode is simplest:","all apps share the Watchdog proxy URL/token while Watchdog injects its single","configured upstream key. For apps with different upstream keys, use","`passthrough` mode so each client sends its own upstream `Authorization` value,","and send the Watchdog access credential separately in","`X-Watchdog-Proxy-Token`. Both modes still write to the same database.","","Named upstream profiles let one Watchdog process route several provider","accounts while retaining one telemetry database and dashboard.","","---","","## AI Chat integration example (no AI Chat code changes)","","For a Kennel-focused end-to-end setup and validation flow, see","[docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md](docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md).","","In `kujo-ai-chat`:","","1. `GET` | `/api/export` | Full export (`json` default or `jsonl`/`ndjson`) |","","The granular contract is optional and producer-neutral. Watchdog is a passive collector: applications, model providers, and tool executors remain independently usable, and a tool can append its own telemetry without importing or depending on another tool. New producers should send `schema_version: \"kujo.telemetry.v1\"`; the checked-in contract is [`schemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json`](schemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json). Trace metrics are cumulative absolute values, and trace/span/event/tool identities are replay-safe for durable at-least-once delivery. See [Granular Tracing](docs/GRANULAR_TRACING.md).","","The Sources tab and `watchdog.sources-panel.v1` API report inbound producers","without conflating them with exporter destinations. Status is based only on","configuration and accepted local telemetry. Native/OTLP registration changes","manage display/setup metadata; they do not start, stop, or disconnect another","application. Named proxy profile changes are saved to the existing proxy","configuration and apply to new requests without restarting Watchdog. In-flight","requests retain the profile snapshot they started with. See [Connected Sources](docs/CONNECTED_SOURCES.md).","","`/api/insights` reports observed legacy telemetry: runs are grouped by task ID, workflow ID, or session ID; a success signal means no request error was recorded; retry signals are inferred from retry-named trace events; and its token-volume section does not measure context capacity. The Canonical Evidence dashboard tab uses explicit terminal events, typed relations, nullable timing, versioned context limits, and distinct cost kinds instead.","","List endpoints now support optional query parameters for pagination and filtering:","","- `page` (default `1`)","- `page_size` (default endpoint-specific, capped)","- common filters where applicable: `session_id`, `user_id`, `tenant_id`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `task_id`, `correlation_id`, `status`, `provider`, `model`, `tool_name`, `agent_id`, `step_type`","- time window: `since_ms`, `until_ms` (epoch milliseconds)","- export format: `format=json|jsonl|ndjson` (`/api/export`; invalid values return `400`)","- export row bound: `max_rows` (`/api/export`; default from `WDG_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS`, max `50000`)","- export chunk cursor: `cursor` and `chunk_size` (`/api/export`; works for json/jsonl/ndjson; `max_rows` caps the effective chunk size per exported kind)","- tenant/project scoping extends to `/api/sessions` and chart endpoints such as `/api/charts/requests-over-time`, `/api/charts/status-breakdown`, and `/api/charts/provider-breakdown`","","Retention and export control examples:","","- Dry-run prune before timestamp:","    `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/admin/prune -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"before_ms\": 1700000000000, \"dry_run\": true}'`","- Filtered export by session/time window:","    `curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?session_id=sess_123\u0026since_ms=1700000000000\u0026until_ms=1800000000000\"`","- Filtered export by tenant/project scope:","    `curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?tenant_id=team_alpha\u0026project_id=checkout-api\"`","- Row-bounded export for controlled payload size:","    `curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=json\u0026max_rows=500\"`","- Cursor-based chunk export progression:","    `curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=json\u0026chunk_size=500\u0026cursor=0\"`","- JSONL export for pipeline ingestion:","    `curl -s \"http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=jsonl\u0026session_id=sess_123\"`","","## Benchmark script","","Run quick and soak benchmark profiles with human-readable output plus JSON summary output:","","`node scripts/benchmark_profiles.js --profiles=quick,soak --json-out=tmp/benchmark-report.json`","","Run deterministic fixture mode for local validation/schema checks:","","`node scripts/benchmark_profiles.js --fixture --profiles=quick,soak --json-out=tmp/benchmark-fixture.json`","","Constrained CI or Workcell environments may set `WDG_LOAD_MIN_RPS` or","`WDG_LOAD_MIN_RPS_QUICK`/`WDG_LOAD_MIN_RPS_SOAK` to document the local CPU","budget. <p dir="auto">Watchdog records AI requests, tool calls and agent steps in a local SQLite database. Its dashboard and JSON APIs show latency, token use, estimated costs and failures.</p>
<p dir="auto">Point an OpenAI-compatible client at <code>/proxy/v1</code>. Watchdog forwards requests to your provider and records telemetry. Native producers can also submit canonical batches or supported OTLP traces.</p>
<p dir="auto">Costs are estimated direct-provider equivalents, not invoices. See <a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/PRICING_ESTIMATES.md">pricing estimates</a> for catalog sources, model mappings and repricing commands.</p>
<p dir="auto">Watchdog runs locally by default. Before exposing it to other machines, configure token authentication, TLS, network access, retention, backups and secret storage. See the <a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/DEPLOYMENT_HARDENING_RUNBOOK.md">deployment guide</a>.</p>

<ol dir="auto">
<li>Your client sends requests to this server at <code>/proxy/v1/...</code>.</li>
<li>The server forwards them to a configurable upstream base URL.</li>
<li>The server logs request metrics and traces in SQLite.</li>
<li>The dashboard UI reads those logs from JSON API endpoints.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">No changes are required in your app code beyond setting the base URL (and API
key behavior) to use the proxy.</p>

<p dir="auto">When <code>WDG_API_AUTH_MODE=token</code>, the dashboard opens an API access prompt.

<p dir="auto">Use <code>src/</code> as the canonical implementation source. The root files
<code>dashboard_server.kujo</code>, <code>dashboard.html</code>, <code>watchdog.kujo</code>, and
<code>watchdog_shared.kujo</code> are compatibility mirrors kept in sync from <code>src/</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>demo.kujo</code>, this README, and <code>docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md</code> are the
primary copyable examples. Prefer compact, runnable snippets in those files and
keep repeated output formatting behind small local helpers when it improves
scannability.</p>
<p dir="auto">The demo seeder writes to <code>data/watchdog-demo.db</code> and refuses the production
<code>watchdog.db</code>. Demo rows are labeled <code>source_app=watchdog-demo</code> and
<code>data_class=fixture</code>; live proxy and external application telemetry remain in
the production database with distinct classifications.</p>
<p dir="auto">Treat <code>tests/</code> as contract and regression coverage. Do not shorten fixtures or
expected-output checks just to reduce tokens when explicit examples make a test
clearer.</p>
<p dir="auto">Exclude generated and bulk runtime paths from broad readability sweeps unless a
task explicitly targets them: <code>tmp/</code>, <code>data/</code>, <code>vendor/</code>, SQLite artifacts, and
local proxy config files.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Named upstream profiles</h3><a id="user-content-named-upstream-profiles" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Named upstream profiles" href="#named-upstream-profiles"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

      "auth_mode": "override",
      "upstream_api_key_env": "OPENROUTER_WORK_API_KEY"
    },
    "ollama-work": {

    }
  }
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_base_url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://ollama.com/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"auth_mode"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>override<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_api_key_env"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>OLLAMA_PERSONAL_API_KEY<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_profiles"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"openrouter-work"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_base_url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://openrouter.ai/api/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"auth_mode"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>override<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_api_key_env"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>OPENROUTER_WORK_API_KEY<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
    },
    <span class="pl-ent">"ollama-work"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"upstream_base_url"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>https://ollama.com/v1<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,

<p dir="auto">Clients select a configured non-default profile with the trusted proxy header
<code>X-Watchdog-Upstream-Profile: openrouter-work</code>. Unknown profile names are
rejected before any upstream request. The dashboard records the selected profile
name as the request provider, making account/provider filtering unambiguous.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Proxy routes</h2><a id="user-content-proxy-routes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Proxy routes" href="#proxy-routes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<tr>
<th>Method</th>

<p dir="auto">Proxy forwarding is broader than telemetry decoding. Chat Completions JSON/SSE
has the first endpoint-specific decoder for model, usage, finish-reason, and
bounded summaries. Other paths are opaque: Watchdog records transport metadata
and correlation but forwards request/response bodies byte-for-byte without
trying to interpret provider extensions, multipart uploads, images, audio,
files, fine-tuning payloads, or arbitrary JSON as chat telemetry.</p>
<p dir="auto">The proxy forwards JSON responses and incrementally passes through streaming
chat SSE responses when run with a Kujo build containing generic HTTP response
streaming. It returns the upstream status/body to the caller and records the
first meaningful content delta plus completion or disconnect lifecycle facts.
Safe scalar query parameters are forwarded to upstream list and
retrieve endpoints, while suspicious path/query text such as path traversal,
embedded URL schemes, fragments, and query delimiters in path segments is
rejected before any upstream request is made.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto"><code>passthrough</code> (default)</h3><a id="user-content-passthrough-default" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: passthrough (default)" href="#passthrough-default"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Non-local deployment hardening</h2><a id="user-content-non-local-deployment-hardening" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Non-local deployment hardening" href="#non-local-deployment-hardening"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>Set <code>WDG_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=production</code> for non-local deployments.</li>
<li>In production profile mode, Watchdog fails startup unless all of the following are configured:

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Telemetry redaction policy</h2><a id="user-content-telemetry-redaction-policy" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Telemetry redaction policy" href="#telemetry-redaction-policy"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>WDG_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=off</code> (default) prevents proxy prompt and response summaries from being persisted.</li>
<li><code>WDG_CONTENT_CAPTURE_MODE=summaries</code> explicitly enables bounded proxy summaries.</li>
<li><code>WDG_REDACTION_MODE=basic</code> (default) redacts sensitive terms from any enabled summaries, tool-call payload fields, step metadata, and error messages before data is stored or exported.</li>
<li><code>WDG_REDACTION_MODE=off</code> keeps original text for local debugging workflows.</li>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">OTLP export</h2><a id="user-content-otlp-export" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: OTLP export" href="#otlp-export"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Copy <code>config/exporters.example.json</code> to the path selected by <code>WDG_EXPORTERS_CONFIG_PATH</code>, enable a profile, and run <code>kujo run export_worker.kujo</code> once or with <code>--watch</code>. Profiles are isolated by durable queue/checkpoint state; optional destination failure never changes proxy success. Remote endpoints require HTTPS. Loopback HTTP is accepted for local collectors, while private-network HTTPS requires the profile's explicit <code>allow_private_network</code> opt-in.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>encoding: "protobuf"</code> is the recommended OTLP/HTTP transport and sends <code>application/x-protobuf</code>; it requires Kujo 1.2.2 or newer for binary request/response bodies. <code>encoding: "json"</code> remains the compatibility default when the field is omitted. Set <code>compression: "gzip"</code> for bounded binary-safe request compression. Mapping profiles are independently pinned as <code>otel.base.v1</code>, <code>otel.genai.v1</code>, or <code>openinference.v1</code>. Grafana/Tempo, Datadog, Honeycomb, Phoenix, Langfuse, and other compatible destinations should normally receive these profiles through their OTLP endpoint or an OpenTelemetry Collector, not a destination-specific Watchdog trace client.</p>
<p dir="auto">Exporter credentials never belong in the profile. Map a header to an environment-variable name with <code>headers_from_env</code>, for example <code>{"Authorization":"WATCHDOG_OTLP_AUTH"}</code>, then set that environment variable only in the worker process. The worker caps batches at 256 records and 512 KiB, retries bounded transient failures, pauses on authentication rejection, expires old queue entries, and retains bounded dead-letter metadata without raw export payloads.</p>
<p dir="auto">The guarded trace receiver is <code>POST /telemetry/v2/otlp/v1/traces</code>. It accepts OTLP/HTTP JSON and Protobuf, optionally gzip-compressed, under the same authentication, request-size, rate, and privacy controls as other ingestion. It retains only spans carrying recognized GenAI/OpenInference/Watchdog semantics, returns OTLP partial success for rejected spans, strips content at the authoritative policy boundary, and rejects generic traces, logs, metrics, malformed wire data, and over-limit decompression. Watchdog does not accept arbitrary OpenTelemetry data.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Rate limiting</h2><a id="user-content-rate-limiting" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Rate limiting" href="#rate-limiting"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MODE=basic</code> enables lightweight SQLite-backed throttling for both Watchdog API routes and proxy routes. Persisted buckets avoid concurrent dashboard requests corrupting shared process state.</li>
<li>Buckets are keyed by <code>X-Observe-Session-Id</code> when present, otherwise by forwarded IP/host fallbacks.</li>
<li>Use <code>WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS</code> and <code>WDG_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECS</code> to tune burst tolerance for your environment.</li>
<li>Use <code>WDG_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BUCKETS</code> and <code>WDG_RATE_LIMIT_BUCKET_TTL_SECS</code> to bound limiter memory and evict stale buckets in long-running deployments.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Automated database backups</h2><a id="user-content-automated-database-backups" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Automated database backups" href="#automated-database-backups"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Watchdog enables verified SQLite backups by default every 24 hours. Open the
<strong>Backups</strong> dashboard tab to change the frequency, destination folder,
retention count, encryption setting, or to create a backup immediately.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Backups use SQLite's online <code>VACUUM INTO</code> path, so Watchdog does not need to stop.</li>
<li>Each backup is checked with <code>PRAGMA quick_check</code> and receives a <code>.sha256</code> sidecar.</li>
<li>A Dropbox or Google Drive folder can be selected by entering its local synced path.</li>
<li>Scheduling is activity-aware: startup, dashboard refreshes, proxy traffic, and direct telemetry trigger a due check. If Watchdog is idle, the next activity creates the overdue backup before continuing.</li>
<li>Generated files use <code>watchdog-backup-<UTC timestamp>-<suffix>.db</code> or <code>.db.enc</code>; retention only removes files matching that pattern.</li>
<li>The main backup list now shows only files still present in the configured folder. Deleted or missing files stay available under the archived history view, and active backups can be deleted directly from the dashboard.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For encrypted backups, create a dedicated passphrase file outside the repository:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/watchdog"
openssl rand -base64 48 > "$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key"
export WDG_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE="$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key""><pre>mkdir -p <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.config/watchdog<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
openssl rand -base64 48 <span class="pl-k">></span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
chmod 600 <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
<span class="pl-k">export</span> WDG_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Restart Watchdog, then enable encryption in the Backups tab. Encryption uses
AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2-SHA256 and 200,000 iterations. Restore an encrypted file:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 200000 -md sha256 \
  -in watchdog-backup-TIMESTAMP.db.enc \
  -out restored-watchdog.db \
  -pass file:"$HOME/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key"
sqlite3 restored-watchdog.db 'PRAGMA quick_check;'"><pre>openssl enc -d -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 200000 -md sha256 \
  -in watchdog-backup-TIMESTAMP.db.enc \
  -out restored-watchdog.db \
  -pass file:<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-smi">$HOME</span>/.config/watchdog/backup-encryption-key<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
sqlite3 restored-watchdog.db <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>PRAGMA quick_check;<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Integrating any OpenAI-compatible client</h2><a id="user-content-integrating-any-openai-compatible-client" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Integrating any OpenAI-compatible client" href="#integrating-any-openai-compatible-client"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Set the client base URL to:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="http://localhost:7700/proxy/v1"><pre lang="text" class="notranslate"><code>http://localhost:7700/proxy/v1
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Keep normal OpenAI-style paths, for example <code>chat/completions</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Optional headers for better dashboard grouping:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>X-Observe-Session-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-User-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-Tenant-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-Project-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-Workflow-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-Task-Id</code></li>
<li><code>X-Observe-Correlation-Id</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Tenant/project values can also be supplied in JSON request bodies using
<code>tenant_id</code> and <code>project_id</code> when headers are not available.</p>
<p dir="auto">If omitted, the proxy auto-generates values.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Aggregating multiple apps and API keys</h3><a id="user-content-aggregating-multiple-apps-and-api-keys" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Aggregating multiple apps and API keys" href="#aggregating-multiple-apps-and-api-keys"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">One Watchdog server aggregates every app that sends traffic through its
<code>/proxy/v1</code> URL into the same telemetry database. API keys do not partition
dashboard data. Give each app a distinct <code>X-Observe-Project-Id</code> (for example,
<code>signalbox</code> and <code>ai-chat</code>) and the unfiltered dashboard stats include both;
the request table can still be filtered by project when needed.</p>
<p dir="auto">Keep the three credential roles separate:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>WDG_API_AUTH_TOKEN</code> protects Watchdog's dashboard JSON APIs.</li>
<li><code>WDG_PROXY_AUTHZ_TOKEN</code> controls which clients may use the proxy.</li>
<li>Upstream provider keys authenticate Watchdog to OpenAI-compatible providers.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">For several apps using the same upstream account, <code>override</code> mode is simplest:
all apps share the Watchdog proxy URL/token while Watchdog injects its single
configured upstream key. For apps with different upstream keys, use
<code>passthrough</code> mode so each client sends its own upstream <code>Authorization</code> value,
and send the Watchdog access credential separately in
<code>X-Watchdog-Proxy-Token</code>. Both modes still write to the same database.</p>
<p dir="auto">Named upstream profiles let one Watchdog process route several provider
accounts while retaining one telemetry database and dashboard.</p>
<hr>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">AI Chat integration example (no AI Chat code changes)</h2><a id="user-content-ai-chat-integration-example-no-ai-chat-code-changes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: AI Chat integration example (no AI Chat code changes)" href="#ai-chat-integration-example-no-ai-chat-code-changes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">For a Kennel-focused end-to-end setup and validation flow, see
<a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md">docs/KENNEL_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">In <code>kujo-ai-chat</code>:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>In Settings, choose provider <code>Custom OpenAI-Compatible</code>.</li>
<li>Set profile <code>Base URL</code> to your Watchdog proxy base (for example,
<code>https://your-watchdog-host/proxy/v1</code>).</li>
<li>Set the profile API key as usual.</li>
<li>Ensure <code>ALLOWED_CUSTOM_PROVIDER_HOSTS</code> in AI Chat includes your proxy host.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Important: current AI Chat security validation rejects localhost/private hosts
for custom providers and requires HTTPS. For local testing, use an HTTPS host
that resolves externally (for example, via a secure tunnel) and allowlist that
host in <code>ALLOWED_CUSTOM_PROVIDER_HOSTS</code>.</p>

<p dir="auto">The granular contract is optional and producer-neutral. Watchdog is a passive collector: applications, model providers, and tool executors remain independently usable, and a tool can append its own telemetry without importing or depending on another tool. New producers should send <code>schema_version: "kujo.telemetry.v1"</code>; the checked-in contract is <a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/schemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json"><code>schemas/telemetry-trace-v1.schema.json</code></a>. Trace metrics are cumulative absolute values, and trace/span/event/tool identities are replay-safe for durable at-least-once delivery. See <a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/GRANULAR_TRACING.md">Granular Tracing</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto">The Sources tab and <code>watchdog.sources-panel.v1</code> API report inbound producers
without conflating them with exporter destinations. Status is based only on
configuration and accepted local telemetry. Native/OTLP registration changes
manage display/setup metadata; they do not start, stop, or disconnect another
application. Named proxy profile changes are saved to the existing proxy
configuration and apply to new requests without restarting Watchdog. In-flight
requests retain the profile snapshot they started with. See <a href="/kujolang/watchdog/blob/7a0bd9a63d68421831ed66d6eed29805c48e1b24/docs/CONNECTED_SOURCES.md">Connected Sources</a>.</p>
<p dir="auto"><code>/api/insights</code> reports observed legacy telemetry: runs are grouped by task ID, workflow ID, or session ID; a success signal means no request error was recorded; retry signals are inferred from retry-named trace events; and its token-volume section does not measure context capacity. The Canonical Evidence dashboard tab uses explicit terminal events, typed relations, nullable timing, versioned context limits, and distinct cost kinds instead.</p>
<p dir="auto">List endpoints now support optional query parameters for pagination and filtering:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>page</code> (default <code>1</code>)</li>
<li><code>page_size</code> (default endpoint-specific, capped)</li>
<li>common filters where applicable: <code>session_id</code>, <code>user_id</code>, <code>tenant_id</code>, <code>project_id</code>, <code>workflow_id</code>, <code>task_id</code>, <code>correlation_id</code>, <code>status</code>, <code>provider</code>, <code>model</code>, <code>tool_name</code>, <code>agent_id</code>, <code>step_type</code></li>
<li>time window: <code>since_ms</code>, <code>until_ms</code> (epoch milliseconds)</li>
<li>export format: <code>format=json|jsonl|ndjson</code> (<code>/api/export</code>; invalid values return <code>400</code>)</li>
<li>export row bound: <code>max_rows</code> (<code>/api/export</code>; default from <code>WDG_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS</code>, max <code>50000</code>)</li>
<li>export chunk cursor: <code>cursor</code> and <code>chunk_size</code> (<code>/api/export</code>; works for json/jsonl/ndjson; <code>max_rows</code> caps the effective chunk size per exported kind)</li>
<li>tenant/project scoping extends to <code>/api/sessions</code> and chart endpoints such as <code>/api/charts/requests-over-time</code>, <code>/api/charts/status-breakdown</code>, and <code>/api/charts/provider-breakdown</code></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Retention and export control examples:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Dry-run prune before timestamp:
<code>curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/admin/prune -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"before_ms": 1700000000000, "dry_run": true}'</code></li>
<li>Filtered export by session/time window:
<code>curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?session_id=sess_123&since_ms=1700000000000&until_ms=1800000000000"</code></li>
<li>Filtered export by tenant/project scope:
<code>curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?tenant_id=team_alpha&project_id=checkout-api"</code></li>
<li>Row-bounded export for controlled payload size:
<code>curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=json&max_rows=500"</code></li>
<li>Cursor-based chunk export progression:
<code>curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=json&chunk_size=500&cursor=0"</code></li>
<li>JSONL export for pipeline ingestion:
<code>curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:7700/api/export?format=jsonl&session_id=sess_123"</code></li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Canonical batch intake bounds</h3><a id="user-content-canonical-batch-intake-bounds" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Canonical batch intake bounds" href="#canonical-batch-intake-bounds"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>POST /telemetry/v2/batches</code> requires 1–100 record objects in the raw request.
Oversized arrays and non-object entries return HTTP 400 before privacy filtering;
they are never silently reduced to a successful partial batch. Valid batches are
privacy-filtered once, then retain repository validation, identity-conflict checks
and transactional persistence.</p>
<p dir="auto">Canonical repository intake reuses each validated record's stable JSON and SHA-256
within its bounded batch for conflict checks and insertion. It does not cache
records across requests or bypass privacy, validation, or transactional conflict
rejection. Legacy rows without stored hashes still backfill from their canonical
JSON. The identity-conflict fixture covers mixed duplicate/new batches and this
legacy retry path.</p>
<p dir="auto">Canonical HTTP intake relies on the repository's structural validation before
its transaction rather than repeating the same full validation in the route.
Raw container bounds and authoritative privacy projection still precede it;
validation failures return HTTP 400 and identity conflicts return HTTP 409.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Concurrent canonical intake</h3><a id="user-content-concurrent-canonical-intake" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Concurrent canonical intake" href="#concurrent-canonical-intake"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Disk-backed canonical batches use a dedicated SQLite connection per request so
overlapping HTTP callbacks cannot nest transactions on the dashboard connection.
Validation, privacy filtering, atomic insertion and identity-conflict checks remain
unchanged. Private <code>:memory:</code> stores retain their shared connection semantics and

ShipCheck","","[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.2-black)](https://github.com/kujolang/shipcheck)","[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey)](LICENSE)","[![built with Kujo](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Kujo-white.svg)](https://github.com/kujolang/kujo)","","ShipCheck checks whether a local repo is ready enough to ship by running explicit release-readiness checks and reporting blockers.","","It audits a local repository and produces:","","- a human-readable Markdown report,","- a machine-friendly JSON report,","- a release checklist,","- and a deterministic gate result for CI.","","ShipCheck surfaces blockers and follow-up work; it does not certify a release or replace human review.","","## Positioning","","ShipCheck is a production-forward alpha: the CLI surface, JSON shape, and gate semantics are stable enough for local workflows and CI experimentation, and the project now passes its own release gate. It is not an enterprise certification engine yet. Treat it as a clear, deterministic readiness scanner that helps teams see missing release signals before humans make the final ship decision.","","## Install / Quick Start","","Requirements:","","- Kujo runtime available as `kujo`","- Git available on `PATH`","","Run from this repository:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo help","kujo run shipcheck.kujo scan","kujo run shipcheck.kujo gate","```","","Expected gate behavior:","","- `scan` prints findings without failing the command.","- `gate` exits `1` when error-level checks fail.","- `gate` exits `0` when only warnings or passing checks remain.","- `gate --format json` emits valid JSON and still uses the exit code for pass/fail automation.","","## Usage Examples","","Emit JSON for automation:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo scan --format json","```","","Scan another repository:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo scan --dir ../kujo-spec","kujo run shipcheck.kujo gate --dir ../kujo-spec --format json","```","","Use `help` and `version`; standalone `--help` and `--version` aliases are not implemented in this wrapper.","","Unsupported output formats fail with exit `2`:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo scan --format yaml","```","","## Release-Readiness Capabilities","","- Scans repository health, code quality, documentation, and release metadata.","- Distinguishes informational scanning from the blocking `gate` command.","- Uses error vs warning severity so teams can gate on what matters.","- Works fully offline on local repositories.","- Produces structured JSON for automation and reporting systems.","- Passes target directories as literal Git process arguments without a shell.","","## Command Reference","","| Command | Description |","| --- | --- |","| `scan` | Run all checks and print a full release-readiness report |","| `checklist` | Print an actionable release checklist plus current check state |","| `gate` | Run checks and exit nonzero if any error-level checks fail |","| `release-note` | Draft release notes using recent git commits |","| `version` | Print tool version and summary |","| `help` | Print usage and examples |","","Supported flags:","","- `--dir \u003cpath\u003e` target directory (default: current directory)","- `--format markdown|json` output format for `scan` and `gate` (default: `markdown`)","","Scan is informational: it can report findings without failing the command. Gate is the blocking verification command.","","## Gate Semantics","","- Error-level failures cause `gate` to exit with status `1`.","- Warning-only results still pass the gate.","- Successful gate runs exit with status `0`.","","This makes ShipCheck useful in CI merge/release workflows, with human review still needed for warnings and release decisions.","","## JSON Contract and Compatibility","","`scan --format json` and `gate --format json` conform to the versioned","[JSON schema](schemas/shipcheck-report.schema.json). The schema is part of the","public CLI contract for the current `1.x` line.","","ShipCheck makes additive changes to the JSON report only in backward-compatible","releases. Renaming, removing, or changing the meaning/type of an existing field","requires a documented breaking release and a schema-version update. Consumers","should ignore unrecognized fields and rely on the command exit status plus","`summary.gate_passed` for gate decisions.","","See [the compatibility policy](docs/compatibility.md) for the complete policy,","including the stable compatibility boundary.","","## Security and Limitations","","ShipCheck reads repository metadata and invokes local Git commands; it does not","run project tests, inspect release artifacts, call network services, publish","releases, or certify a project. Read the [threat model and security","boundaries](docs/security.md) before using it against untrusted workspaces.","","## Check Coverage","","ShipCheck runs 16 checks across 4 categories:","","- Repository health","- Code quality","- Documentation","- Release metadata","","Full catalog and severity definitions are documented in [docs/check-catalog.md](docs/check-catalog.md).","","## CI Integration","","Example release gate step:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo gate --dir . --format json","```","","If your policy needs a saved artifact:","","```bash","kujo run shipcheck.kujo scan --dir . --format json \u003e shipcheck-report.json","```","","Additional operational guidance is in [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md).","","This repository includes a GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It builds a pinned Kujo runtime, runs CLI and hardening contract tests plus source validation, and then runs ShipCheck's own scan and gate.","","## Project Status","","Current release line: `v1.0.2`. Requires Kujo 1.6.0 or newer.","","ShipCheck 1.0 has a stable core command surface and gate behavior covered by contract tests. Current self-scan status is 16/16 checks passing with zero warnings.","","## Repository Layout","","- `shipcheck.kujo` CLI entry point","- `src/checks.kujo` individual release checks","- `src/scan.kujo` scan orchestration","- `src/report.kujo` markdown/json/checklist/release-note output","- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` CI contract and self-gate workflow","- `docs/` operational and check reference documentation","- `AGENTS.md` contributor and agent guidance for canonical examples and search hygiene","","The example shell script under `examples/` uses `KUJO_BIN` when set and otherwise expects the Kujo runtime to be available as `kujo` on `PATH`.","","## Changelog","","Release notes and history are tracked in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).","","## Dogfood Artifacts","","Historical implementation and ecosystem notes are preserved under [.dogfood/shipcheck](.dogfood/shipcheck). Treat them as background context, not canonical examples.","","Generated or bulk evaluation output lives under `eval_results/`; exclude it from broad readability sweeps unless the task explicitly <p dir="auto">ShipCheck checks whether a local repo is ready enough to ship by running explicit release-readiness checks and reporting blockers.</p>
<p dir="auto">It audits a local repository and produces:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>a human-readable Markdown report,</li>
<li>a machine-friendly JSON report,</li>
<li>a release checklist,</li>
<li>and a deterministic gate result for CI.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">ShipCheck surfaces blockers and follow-up work; it does not certify a release or replace human review.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Positioning</h2><a id="user-content-positioning" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Positioning" href="#positioning"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">ShipCheck is a production-forward alpha: the CLI surface, JSON shape, and gate semantics are stable enough for local workflows and CI experimentation, and the project now passes its own release gate. It is not an enterprise certification engine yet. Treat it as a clear, deterministic readiness scanner that helps teams see missing release signals before humans make the final ship decision.</p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>Scans repository health, code quality, documentation, and release metadata.</li>
<li>Distinguishes informational scanning from the blocking <code>gate</code> command.</li>
<li>Uses error vs warning severity so teams can gate on what matters.</li>
<li>Works fully offline on local repositories.</li>
<li>Produces structured JSON for automation and reporting systems.</li>
<li>Passes target directories as literal Git process arguments without a shell.</li>
</ul>
